sections.title: Event log, runner, and limits
sections.summary: How Ostra stores each session as an append-only event log, folds it into state, drives it with one task, recovers it after a restart, and limits its parallel executions and its spend.
sections.body:
A session lasts from minutes to days. It starts many agents, opens gates, and waits for a user. The user can pause it, add context, or restart the server. If the server keeps the state only in memory, a restart loses the session. If it keeps the state in rows that change in place, two writers can disagree about it.

Ostra stores one append-only list of events for each session. The state of a session is the fold of its events. A fold is a function that reads the events in order and builds the state. The same events always give the same state. Thus a restart reads the log, folds it, and continues.

This page covers:

- the events and the fold
- the driver task of each live session
- restart recovery
- pause, resume, stop, and inspect
- context that a user adds to a running session
- the approval check for the format command
- the execution slot and the session budget
- the session context file
- the views that the browser reads

The rules that choose each next step are on [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md). The judge calls are on [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md). The database tables are on [Storage](storage.md).

## Session events and the stored log

`SessionEvent` in [`crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs) is the enum of every fact that Ostra records about a session. It has 28 variants. The JSON form has a `type` field in snake case, for example `execution_finished`. A `StoredEvent` wraps an event with `seq` and `at`. The `seq` is the number of the event in its session, from 1. The `at` is the time of the append, with millisecond precision.

`WorkspaceDb::append_event` gives the next `seq` with `MAX(seq) + 1` inside an immediate transaction. It also sets `sessions.updated_at`. Two appends to one session cannot get the same number.

### Event groups

| Group | Events | What they record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session life | `SessionCreated`, `RequestAmended`, `SessionPaused`, `SessionResumed`, `YoloSet`, `Note`, `SessionCompleted`, `SessionFailed` | The request, the user actions, and the end of the session |
| Executions | `ExecutionStarted`, `ExecutionResumed`, `ExecutionFinished`, `ContainmentSignal` | The start, the continuation, and the result of each agent execution |
| Coordination | `AgentAsked`, `AgentReplied`, `MessageDelivered` | Questions between subagents. [Agents, prompts, and coordination](agents-and-prompts.md) explains them. |
| Gates and decisions | `GateOpened`, `GateAnswered`, `DecisionMade`, `DecisionOverridden` | Each question to the user and each judge decision |
| Commands and work | `CommandStarted`, `CommandRan`, `AutofixApplied`, `SecurityBlock`, `PhaseBlocked`, `BookWritten` | Format and staging commands, auto-fixes, blocked phases, and the written book |
| Created projects | `ProjectCreated`, `ProjectInitFinished`, `InitStepFailed` | Projects that an agent creates during the session |

### Types that the fold keys on

- `ExecPurpose` says what an execution was for. It has 17 variants, for example `Explore`, `Spec`, `Implement`, `Review`, `Docs`, `Inspect`, and `Consult`. The fold finds the work loop or the stage of an execution from it.
- `WorkKind` says why an implement or write-test execution ran: `Initial`, `Fix`, `BlockerFix`, `Resume`, `Rescue`, or `Rerun`.
- `WorkKind::Rerun` marks a repeat of work that did not finish. The fold sets it in three cases, listed below.
- `GatePayload` has 14 variants, one for each gate card. `GateAnswer` has 6 variants. `AnswerSource` says who answered: `User`, `Yolo`, or `Engine`. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) explains the gates.
- `ExecPurpose::run_label` gives the label of one execution. `numbered_run_label` adds a pass number to later executions with the same label.

The fold sets `WorkKind::Rerun` in these cases:

- A work loop starts again after a server restart.
- A work-loop execution ends `Interrupted` and the restart is not a fresh-project restart. This includes the restart after an `Interrupt::Context` cancel (`state.rs`, about lines 3206-3218).
- A work-loop execution ends with status `Error`, and the loop has not used its automatic retry (`state.rs`, about lines 3226-3239). The retry does not apply to an error that starts with `harness-`. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) owns the retry count.

A `Rerun` keeps the instructions of the interrupted start. A fresh-project restart (Rule O4) uses `WorkKind::Initial` instead.

### Old logs stay readable

A log that an earlier version wrote must still fold. Thus a field that Ostra added later has `#[serde(default)]`. The variant `ExecPurpose::Docs` also accepts the old name `module_docs` through `#[serde(alias)]`. The fields `routed` on `RequestAmended` and `GateAnswered` default to `false`, and the code says that such events fold as they always did.

The fold ignores one event: `SecurityBlock` changes no state. Ostra records it so that the board can show it.

## Append an event

`Inner::append` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs) is the only way to add an event. Each caller of the engine uses it: the driver, the user actions, and the hosts of running executions.

These steps happen in order:

1. Load the live session, or fold its log from the database.
2. Lock the session state. The lock puts appends of one session in one order, so the order of `seq` is the order of the fold.
3. Refuse `ExecutionStarted`, `ExecutionResumed`, and `CommandStarted` if the session already ended. The error is `EngineError::Ended`.
4. Store the event with `WorkspaceDb::append_event`.
5. Write the gate or decision row for `GateOpened`, `GateAnswered`, and `DecisionMade`.
6. Apply the stored event to `SessionState`.
7. If this event ended the session, remove the session cache of the sandbox tools.
8. Update the session row: category, status, lane, stage label, projects, YOLO flag, cost, and title.
9. Broadcast `EngineNotice::SessionUpdated`, and `ProjectsChanged` when an init session starts or ends.
10. Unlock, broadcast `EngineNotice::Event`, and send a Web Push notice when the event needs one.
11. Wake the driver of the session.

### Sequence of one append

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller
    participant Inner
    participant Db
    participant State
    participant Bus
    participant Driver
    Caller->>Inner: append(session, event)
    Inner->>State: lock, read was_terminal
    Inner->>Db: append_event
    Db-->>Inner: StoredEvent with seq
    Inner->>Db: upsert_gate, answer_gate, insert_decision
    Inner->>State: apply(stored)
    Inner->>Db: update_session
    Inner->>Bus: SessionUpdated
    Inner->>Bus: Event
    Inner->>Driver: wake.notify_one
```

```rust
let mut st = lock(&live.state);
let was_terminal = st.is_terminal();
// A stop can land while a step is being set up; nothing may start after it, and this
// check sits under the state lock, so it cannot race the stop.
if was_terminal && matches!(event,
    SessionEvent::ExecutionStarted { .. }
        | SessionEvent::ExecutionResumed { .. }
        | SessionEvent::CommandStarted { .. })
{
    return Err(EngineError::Ended);
}
let stored = self.db.append_event(session, &event)?;
self.materialize(session, &event)?;
st.apply(&stored);
```

### Why the check sits under the lock

A stop can arrive when a spawn is half set up. The spawn checks the state without the lock, then appends `ExecutionStarted`. Without the check under the lock, the start can land after the stop. The test `a_stop_during_spawn_setup_starts_nothing` in [`crates/ostra-engine/tests/pause.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/tests/pause.rs) holds a spawn, stops the session, releases the spawn, and checks that no execution exists.

### What happens when

- If the append returns `Ended`, the driver does not log it. The step is dropped without a note.
- If the database write fails, the append returns `EngineError::Store` and the fold does not change.
- If the update of the session row fails, the engine ignores the error. The log stays the source of truth.
- A slow subscriber of the broadcast channel can fall behind. The channel holds 4096 notices.
- A Web Push notice goes out for a new gate, a finished or stopped session, a blocked phase, and the third containment signal. Under YOLO a gate sends no notice, except a harness login failure. [Secrets, credentials, and Web Push](secrets-and-push.md) explains the delivery.

Activity items of an execution (tool calls, text, usage) are not events. The host of the execution writes them to a separate table and broadcasts them as `EngineNotice::Delta`.

## Fold the log into session state

`SessionState::fold(id, events)` starts from `SessionState::new` and calls `apply` for each stored event. The code is in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs). `apply` uses the time in the stored event and never the clock. This rule keeps the fold deterministic.

### Fields that this page uses

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `completed`, `failed` | Set by `SessionCompleted` and `SessionFailed`. `is_terminal()` is true when either one is set. |
| `paused` | True after `SessionPaused` or the third containment signal of one execution |
| `contained` | The execution whose signals paused the session |
| `interrupting` | Executions that the engine cancels, each with an `Interrupt` reason |
| `resume_from` | Interrupted executions to continue, keyed by `purpose_key` |
| `waiting_keys` | Executions that ended in status `Waiting`, keyed by `purpose_key` |
| `executions`, `gates`, `decisions` | One record for each `ExecutionStarted`, `GateOpened`, and `DecisionMade` |
| `amendments` | Each `RequestAmended`, with a flag for delivery to the agents |
| `budget_raised`, `budget_gate` | The dollars that the user added, and the open budget gate |
| `last_seq` | The `seq` of the last event that the fold applied |

### How the fold treats an event

- `ExecutionStarted` adds a record with no result. `running_executions()` returns the records with no result.
- `ExecutionFinished` sets the result. If a pause interrupted the execution, the fold stores it in `resume_from`.
- `GateAnswered` sets the answer only when the gate has none. The first answer wins, and a second answer has no effect.
- `DecisionOverridden` replaces the output of a decision and sets `overridden`. The fold ignores an unknown decision id.
- `ExecutionFinished` for an unknown execution has no effect.
- `CommandRan` with purpose `Stage` moves the work loop from `Stage` to `Done`. It sets `staged` when the exit code is `0`.

### Interrupt reasons

The fold marks each execution that the engine must cancel in `interrupting`. The reason decides what happens to the execution after the cancel. `Interrupt::message` gives the text that the execution shows.

| `Interrupt` | Cause | After the cancel | Message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Pause` | The user paused the session, or containment paused it | The execution continues under its own id after resume | `The session was paused.` |
| `Context` | The user sent context with delivery `Now` | The step starts again from its spawn block | `Interrupted to deliver the context the user added.` |
| `ProjectCreated` | The execution created the project of its phase | The phase starts again in the new project, after the init | `Stopped after creating the project, which Ostra initializes before this phase starts again in it.` |

### Resume keys

`purpose_key` maps an execution purpose to one work loop, one review loop, or one stage. `Implement` and `Verify` give `work:{phase}:false`. `WriteTest` gives `work:{phase}:true`. `Review` gives `review:{phase}:{tests}`. The others give `spec`, `plan`, `fact-check:{target}`, or the JSON of the purpose. A paused execution and its replacement have the same key. The fold and the runner use the key to find the execution to continue.

### Constants in the fold

Two constants in `state.rs` have text that users can read. `STOPPED_EXECUTION` is `You stopped this execution.` The fold uses it as the error of a cancelled execution that has no error text. `NO_PRIOR_FINDINGS` is `no findings on the previous pass`. A fact-check pass that finds nothing leaves this text as the `Prior findings:` value of the next pass. The next checker then knows that the pass is a repeat and not a first pass (Rule D3a). The review caps and the retry counts in `state.rs` belong to [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md).

## The driver task of a session

Each live session has one `Live` value in `Inner.sessions`. It holds the folded state, a `Notify` called `wake`, a set of step keys called `inflight`, and the flag `driving`. The driver is the async task that plans and starts the steps of the session.

`ensure_driver` starts the driver. It sets `driving` with an atomic swap. If the flag was already set, it only wakes the driver. If not, it spawns `drive`.

`drive` repeats these actions:

1. Lock the state. If the session ended, leave the loop.
2. Build a `PlanCtx` and call `next_steps(&state, &ctx)`. The planner is a pure function. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) explains it.
3. For each step, compute `step.key()`. If `inflight` already has the key, skip the step.
4. Spawn one task for each new step. The task calls `perform`.
5. Wait on `wake`.

Each append wakes the driver, so the driver plans again after every event. A step task also wakes the driver when it ends. `Notify::notify_one` keeps one permit, so a wake that arrives during planning is not lost.

### Step kinds that `perform` runs

| Step | What the runner does |
| --- | --- |
| `Judge` | Calls a judge and appends `DecisionMade`. |
| `Spawn` | Starts an agent execution. See the execution slot below. |
| `OpenGate` | Appends `GateOpened`. For an `ImplementationReview` gate it writes the session context file first. |
| `YoloAnswer` | Asks the YOLO judge to answer a gate. |
| `Deliver` | Appends `MessageDelivered` and hands the message to a waiting execution. |
| `Command` | Runs the format or staging command. |
| `Autofix` | Applies review findings on a blocking thread. |
| `AnnounceBlocked` | Appends `PhaseBlocked`. |
| `Complete` | Writes the completion report. For an init session it first checks the inventory and the profile of the project, because later executions route by these two files. A broken file fails the init at this step. Without the check, every agent gets an empty profile and no error shows. If the check finds a problem, the step appends `SessionFailed` with the error `Init did not finish: <problem>. Run init again.` and does not append `SessionCompleted`. If the check passes, the step sets the project status to `Initialized` and appends `SessionCompleted`. |
| `Fail` | Appends `SessionFailed`. |
| `FinishInit`, `RecordInitProblem` | Close or report the init of a created project. |
| `WriteBook` | Writes the documentation book and appends `BookWritten`. |

### What happens when

- If a step returns an error other than `Ended`, the driver logs it and appends a `Note` event with the text `A step failed: <error>`. It then removes the key from `inflight` and plans again.
- If two steps have the same key, only one runs. The key stops a second start of a step that is still in progress.
- If the session ended, the loop leaves and `driving` returns to `false`.
- If the budget guard of the planner drops a spawn, the driver starts nothing for it. See the session budget below.

## Start a session

`Engine::create_session` checks the request and calls `start_session`. An empty request gives `Describe the task first.` A `docs_book` value must be a valid book ID. `create_init_session` starts the init flow for one project. It fails with `NotFound` when the workspace has no such project.

`start_session` runs these checks and actions:

1. If `yolo.default` is on, set the YOLO option. [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md) explains YOLO.
2. For a pipeline session, keep only the projects that have `.ostra/INVENTORY.md`. If none is left, return an error that asks the user to initialize a project. Every agent routes its work by the inventory.
3. If the user pinned projects, reject an unknown or uninitialized key. Then keep only the pinned projects (Rule O6).
4. Validate the attached files and uploads.
5. Create the session folder and claim the uploads. [Workspace artifacts and uploads](artifacts-and-uploads.md) explains uploads.
6. Write `*` to `.gitignore` in the sessions folder if the file does not exist. The session files then stay out of Git.
7. Create the session row, the `Live` value, and the `SessionCreated` event.
8. Start the driver.

## Restart recovery

A server restart ends every execution that ran in the old process. `Engine::recover` makes the log say so, and then it starts the drivers again. The server calls it when it attaches a workspace.

### Flow of recovery

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["recover"] --> B["list sessions and fold each log"]
    B --> C{"execution without a result"}
    C -->|"has an open ask"| D["append ExecutionFinished with status Waiting"]
    C -->|"no open ask"| E["append ExecutionFinished with status Interrupted"]
    D --> F["answer stale permission gates with Deny"]
    E --> F
    F --> G{"session ended?"}
    G -->|"no"| H["ensure_driver"]
    G -->|"yes"| I["start no driver"]
    H --> J["mark_running_interrupted"]
    I --> J
```

For each execution that has no result, `recover` does these actions:

- It copies the usage and the native session ID from the stored execution row. The usage deltas were stored when the execution ran, so the cost is not lost.
- It sets the status to `Interrupted` and the error to `The server restarted while this execution ran.`
- If the execution has an open question to another subagent, it sets the status to `Waiting` and no error (Rule H2). The answer then resumes the harness session.
- It writes the result to the row and appends `ExecutionFinished`.

For each open permission gate, `recover` appends `GateAnswered` with source `Engine` and the answer `Deny`. The reason is `The execution that asked ended when the server restarted.` The execution that asked does not exist any more, so nobody can use an `Allow` answer. After the loop over all sessions, `mark_running_interrupted` sets every database row that still says `running` to `interrupted`. This step covers executions that are not in a session log, for example side-panel answers.

### Why the step starts again

The fold treats an `Interrupted` result as work that did not happen. A work loop gets `WorkKind::Rerun` with the same instructions. An explore task, a spec, a plan, and a quick answer start again from their spawn block. The test `recovery_keeps_usage_and_reruns` in [`crates/ostra-engine/tests/recover.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/tests/recover.rs) opens the same database in a second engine. It checks that the interrupted execution keeps its `0.5` dollars and that a second explore starts.

### Stop a session when the server is off

If a session is still open in the log, the next start recovers it and runs its executions again. `stop_session_offline(db, session)` prevents that. It folds the log and refuses a session that has no events or that already ended. Then it does these actions:

1. Mark each running execution `Cancelled` with the error `Stopped by the user.` and keep its usage.
2. Append `ExecutionFinished` for each one.
3. Append `SessionFailed` with the same text.
4. Set the session row to status `Failed`, lane `Done`, and the label `Stopped: Stopped by the user.`

It returns the count of cancelled executions. The command `ostra stop <session>` calls it. The command refuses when the server runs, because a running server holds the session in memory. In that case use the board or `POST /api/sessions/{session}/stop`. The test `offline_stop_prevents_rerun_on_recovery` checks that no execution starts after such a stop.

## Pause and resume a session

A pause stops new work and interrupts the running work. A resume continues each interrupted execution where it stopped.

### States of a session

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Running
    Running --> Paused: SessionPaused
    Running --> Paused: third containment signal
    Paused --> Running: SessionResumed
    Running --> Ended: SessionCompleted
    Running --> Ended: SessionFailed
    Paused --> Ended: SessionFailed
```

### Pause (Rule P1)

`pause_session` refuses a session that ended (`This session has already ended.`) and a session that is paused (`This session is already paused.`). Then it does these actions:

1. Append `SessionPaused`. The fold sets `paused` and marks every running execution in `interrupting` with `Interrupt::Pause`.
2. Call `Inner::interrupt`. It cancels the token of each marked execution.
3. For each open permission gate of those executions, answer `Deny` with source `Engine`. The execution that asked is ending.
4. After the executor returns `Cancelled`, `perform_spawn` changes the status to `Interrupted` and sets the error to `The session was paused.` It also writes this text as an Activity status line.

The planner returns no steps when `paused` is set. It starts no judge, no spawn, and no YOLO answer. `perform_spawn` checks `paused` again after it gets a slot, because a pause can land between the plan and the start. An execution that starts in that window gets `Interrupt::Pause` from the fold.

### Resume (Rule P2)

`resume_session` refuses a session that is not paused or that ended. It appends `SessionResumed`. The fold clears `paused` and `contained`. The planner then plans again, and each spawn that replaces a paused execution gets `resumes` from `resume_from`.

`perform_spawn` finds the old record when its agent matches and its status is `Interrupted` or `Waiting`. It then does these actions:

- It keeps the executor and the model of the old execution. The conversation continues on the executor that it started on, which also keeps the prompt cache.
- It builds `ResumeInfo` with the old native session ID and the note `Continue the workflow.` (`PAUSE_RESUME_NOTE`).
- It appends `ExecutionResumed`. The fold clears the result of the execution and its containment signals.
- It reopens the execution row and uses the old usage as `usage_base`. New usage adds to the old usage.
- It writes the Activity line `The session continued, so this run resumes where it stopped.` (`RESUMED_STATUS`).

The execution keeps its own ID. The session therefore has one row for it, and its Activity and its cost stay in one place. The test `pause_interrupts_and_resume_continues_the_run` checks that the two starts use the same ID and that the cost is `2.0` after two runs of `1.0` dollar.

### Pause after containment signals (Rule P3)

An execution that tries to leave its sandbox records containment signals. The runner records at most `PAUSE_AFTER` signals for one execution, so a retry loop cannot flood the log. The third signal pauses the session like a user pause, and the fold sets `contained` to that execution. The board then shows `Paused: read the <agent> execution's Activity, because it tripped 3 containment signals`. [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) explains which events count as signals.

A resume clears `contained` and the signal count of the resumed execution. The code comment says that continuing is the decision of the user that the behavior was fine. The test `containment_signals_pause_the_session` sends five refusals and finds three recorded signals.

### What happens when

- If the user sends context with delivery `Queue` when the session is paused, the context joins the request for later steps.
- If the user adds any context, the fold clears `resume_from`. A resumed conversation does not see the new context, so the execution starts again from its spawn block.
- If the user stops a paused session, the session ends. The interrupted executions do not resume.
- If the server restarts when the session is paused, the log holds `SessionPaused`. The fold sets `paused` again, and the session stays paused.

## Stop a session or an execution

`stop_session` ends the session and cancels its work. Nothing that the session already did is undone.

1. It refuses a session that already ended.
2. It appends `SessionFailed` with the error `Stopped by the user.` (`STOPPED_BY_USER`). The append makes the session terminal.
3. It cancels the token of each execution that had no result in the earlier state.
4. It answers `Deny` to each waiting permission ask.

The terminal state comes first, so no step can start after the stop. The cancelled executions still append `ExecutionFinished`, with status `Cancelled`. The append at the end of the session also removes the tool caches of the session in the sandbox, because a later session must not build from the downloads of an ended one. The test `an_ended_session_loses_its_tool_caches` checks this.

`cancel_execution` cancels one execution. It returns `This execution is not running.` when the engine has no live token for the ID. The result is `Cancelled`. Rule P4 says that nothing retries such an execution without the user, and YOLO does not retry it either. The user then answers the failure gate with `retry` or `abandon`.

`resume_execution` is the retry for a failed, cancelled, or interrupted execution. It needs an open `ExecutionFailed` or `HarnessFailure` gate for that execution. It stores a resume hint for the purpose key, with the old native session ID. Then it answers the gate with the option `retry`. The next spawn for that key continues the old conversation. A side-panel answer has no session and cannot be resumed.

## Add context to a running session

`Engine::amend` adds text, files, or uploads to a session that has not ended. It refuses an empty addition and an ended session. It appends `RequestAmended`.

The field `delivery` decides when the agents see the context (`ContextDelivery`):

| Delivery | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `Queue` (default) | Running executions finish on the old request. The next step sees the new context. |
| `Now` | The fold marks every running execution with `Interrupt::Context`. The runner cancels them, and each starts again with the new context. |

### Routing of the addition (Rule C2)

`SessionState::routes_amendments` decides if an addition waits for the Route answer judge. It is true only when both of these conditions hold:

- A classify decision exists.
- The category is Research, Spec, Plan, or Implement.

If `routes_amendments` is true, the addition waits for the judge before it reaches the agents. For other categories, for example Test or Docs, the engine does not route the addition. It reaches the agents at once. Before the classify decision exists, the Classify judge reads the addition with the request.

The test `context_sent_now_restarts_running_work` checks that a restart after `Now` is a fresh start and not a resume.

### Attached files (Rule C1)

`validate_files` checks each attached path:

- A request or an addition can attach at most `MAX_CONTEXT_FILES`, which is `50` files. The reason is that every agent reads each file.
- A path in a project must exist inside that project after Ostra resolves it. The error is `Tag a file or folder inside <project>. <path> is not one.`
- The project must belong to the session. Otherwise the error is `Tag files from this session's projects only.`
- A tag for a workspace artifact must name a visible artifact that exists. A hidden artifact cannot be tagged.
- Ostra removes a leading `./`, changes `\\` to `/`, and ends a folder path with `/`. It removes duplicates.

## Reopen an ended harness execution

A user can reopen the conversation of an ended harness execution to read it and to ask about it. `Engine::inspect_execution` starts a read-only execution for this. The execution runs outside the pipeline and changes no state of the session.

The call refuses these cases:

- The execution does not exist.
- The execution is not a harness execution. A native run has its Activity tab.
- The execution is itself a read-only session.
- The execution still runs.
- The execution has no recorded native session ID.
- The execution belongs to no session.
- A paused agent resumes the execution later. The user must continue or stop the session first, because the resumed agent sees the questions of the user.
- The executor is not available.

If all checks pass, the engine creates a new execution with these properties:

- Its purpose is `ExecPurpose::Inspect { of }`, and its row has no session.
- It has no capabilities, so the agent has no tools. The system prompt `INSPECT_PROMPT` tells the agent to answer from the conversation and not to call any tool.
- Its permission mode is `Plan`, YOLO is off, and every permission ask gets `Deny`.
- It ends by itself after `INSPECT_TIMEOUT_SECS`, which is `14400` seconds (4 hours).
- It holds no execution slot.
- `ResumeInfo.inspect` is `true`, so the executor resumes the old harness session.

The user can cancel it with `cancel_execution`. The test `an_ended_harness_run_reopens_read_only` checks the refusals, the empty capability list, and the missing session. The side-panel question (`Engine::ask`) also runs outside the pipeline and takes no slot. [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md) explains it.

## Format command approval before staging

A repository can change its own `project.toml` with a `git pull`. The format command in it is the one project command that Ostra runs itself. Thus the runner runs it only after the user approved that exact command (Rule A1). [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) explains how an approval is stored and when it expires.

`perform_command` handles the `Format` step in this order:

1. If the project has no format command, it skips the step. The output is `No format command in project.toml, so format was skipped.`
2. If `Services::command_approved` returns `false`, it skips the step. The output is `FORMAT_NOT_APPROVED`: `The format command in project.toml changed outside Ostra, so format was skipped. Approve it in the project's settings to run it next time.`
3. Otherwise it appends `CommandStarted`, so a long format run shows on the board. Then it runs `bash -c <command>` in the project folder under the agent sandbox, with a limit of `600` seconds.
4. It appends `CommandRan` with the exit code and the last `4000` bytes of the output.

A skipped step has the exit code `None` and no `CommandStarted` event. The session continues.

### Order of format and staging

`closing_stages` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/plan.rs) pushes the `Format` step once for each project (Rule D8). It does this after the `impl_loop` of every phase of the project is terminal. The implementer loop reaches `Done` only after its `Stage` command ran. Thus the staging of the implementer loop comes before format, and format does not block it. Only the later staging of a test loop can follow format.

The `Stage` step runs `git add -A` for the files that the review loop reported. It has a limit of `60` seconds. Before it runs, it removes a planted `.git` entry inside the project. Staging keeps the next review focused on the unstaged diff. If the list of files is empty, the output is `No files to stage.`

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | Shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Approval of the `commands.format` text of `project.toml` | Not approved, unless Ostra wrote the file | The machine registry, key `trust:format:<project path>` | At the next format step, because the runner asks at that time | The `output_tail` of the `CommandRan` event, and the pending commands of the workspace | Approve the command in the project settings. To revoke, change the command text, because an approval covers one exact text. |

## The parallel execution slot

A fan-out stage can start many agents at once. The init scouts, the skill generation, and the research tasks are examples. Each agent can use a top-tier model. Without a limit, one session can start dozens of costly executions together. The slot limit caps the number of agent executions that run at one time in one workspace.

The engine counts the slots in `Inner.slots`. `Slot` is a value whose `Drop` gives the slot back and wakes the waiting spawns. Thus a slot returns after each end of an execution: success, failure, cancellation, or a panic in the executor.

### Flow of a slot request

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["acquire_slot"] --> B["read limits.max_parallel_executions, minimum 1"]
    B --> C{"slots in use below the limit?"}
    C -->|"yes"| D["add 1 and return a Slot"]
    C -->|"no"| E["wait on slot_free for 2 seconds at most"]
    E --> B
```

```rust
impl Drop for Slot {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let mut n = lock(&self.0.slots);
        *n = n.saturating_sub(1);
        drop(n);
        self.0.slot_free.notify_waiters();
    }
}
// acquire_slot: re-read the limit on each loop, then
tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), self.slot_free.notified()).await;
```

A waiting spawn checks again when a slot becomes free, and at least every 2 seconds. Each time, it reads the limit from the workspace settings. If you raise the limit, waiting spawns start in 2 seconds or less, with no restart. If you lower it, Ostra cancels nothing. The executions that run finish, and new spawns wait until the count is below the new limit.

### Which executions hold a slot

- **Holds a slot:** each agent execution that a session spawns through `perform_spawn`, on every executor. The limit is for each workspace, so two sessions in the same workspace share it. `perform_spawn` takes the slot before it checks that the session is still live. It returns the slot at once if the session ended or paused.
- **Gives its slot back when it waits:** an execution that waits for a message with its process alive (Rule H2). It takes a slot again before it gets the message. Without this rule, a limit of `1` blocks the session. The waiting execution holds the only slot, and the execution that it waits for cannot start. The test `subagents_wake_each_other_and_pair_loops_continue_conversations` runs with the limit `1` and checks this case.
- **Does not hold a slot:** judge calls, side-panel quick answers, read-only reopened sessions, and the format and staging commands.

### What happens when

- If the setting is `0` in a file, the settings check rejects it with `Allow at least one execution at a time.` The runner also uses `max(1)`, so it never uses a limit below `1`.
- If the limit is `1`, the session runs its executions one at a time. A waiting execution that gets a message waits for a slot again.
- If a pause or a stop arrives when a spawn waits, the spawn gets the slot, sees the state, and returns with no start.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | Shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limits.max_parallel_executions` (`Limits` in `config.rs`) | `3` executions | The machine registry, saved with the workspace settings | For waiting spawns, within 2 seconds, with no restart | The number of executions with status `Running` on the session board | Set a higher value for more parallel executions. Set `1` for one at a time. The minimum is `1`. |

The registry holds this value and not `workspace.toml`. Rule A2 gives the reason: a repository can otherwise lift its own limits. [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) explains the settings stores.

## The session budget

The session budget caps what one session spends. When the session reaches it, the planner starts no new execution and opens a gate. The user decides to raise the budget or to stop.

The runner reads `limits.session_budget_usd` at each planner pass, and a value of `0` or less means no limit. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) explains `next_steps`, the `PlanCtx` input, and the budget guard in the planner.

The guard computes these values:

- `limit = budget + budget_raised`, where `budget_raised` is the dollars that the user added with earlier answers.
- `spent = SessionState::spent_usd()`, the sum of the cost of finished executions.

If `spent >= limit`, the planner drops the spawn. If no budget gate is open, it opens one with the title `The session reached its budget` and the payload `GatePayload::BudgetReached { spent_usd, budget_usd }`. The `budget_usd` in the payload is the limit at that time.

### What the budget counts

- It counts the usage of finished executions. A resumed execution counts once, with its total usage.
- It does not count the executions that still run. They finish, and their cost is added then. The cost of a session can therefore pass the limit.
- It does not count the cost of judge calls. The runner keeps the judge cost in memory for the session cost on the board only.
- It blocks only spawns. Judge calls, commands, and gates continue.

### Answer the budget gate

The gate takes a `Choice` answer. YOLO never answers this gate, because spending more is the decision of the user.

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `raise` | The fold adds `extra + max(spent - limit, 0)` to `budget_raised`. The new limit gives the session `extra` more dollars. |
| `stop` (any other option) | The session fails with `Stopped at the session budget after spending $<amount>.` |

The `text` of a `raise` answer holds the extra dollars. A leading `$` is allowed. If the text is missing, is not a finite number, or is not above `0`, the extra amount is the limit again, with a minimum of `1.0`. Thus the session can spend as much again before the next gate.

The session does not get the status `Paused`. It shows `Waiting` when no execution runs. If executions still run, it shows `Running`. The gate belongs to the stage `Intake`.

### What happens when

- If the user lowers the budget below the amount spent, the next planner pass opens the gate.
- If the user sets the budget to `0`, the next planner pass does not check the budget.
- If the server restarts, the fold rebuilds `budget_raised` and `budget_gate` from the log.
- If the setting is negative or not finite, the settings check rejects it. The message says that the budget is a dollar amount of 0 or more.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | Shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limits.session_budget_usd` (`Limits` in `config.rs`) | `25.0` dollars | The machine registry, saved with the workspace settings | At the next planner pass, which follows the next event of the session | The cost of the session on the board, and the `budget_reached` gate | Set `0` for no limit. Answer the gate with `raise` and the extra dollars, or with `stop`. |

## The session context file

A session can take many feedback rounds. If an agent keeps one long conversation, its context grows without limit. Ostra instead writes a Markdown index of the session. A revision reads the file and not a conversation (Rule F2). The index holds paths and short summaries, so the agent opens only the files that it needs.

`context::render` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/context.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/context.rs) builds the file from the fold. The runner writes it to `ostra-session-context.md` in the session folder. It overwrites the file each time, so the file always matches the log.

### Sections of the file

| Section | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `# Session context` | A note that Ostra rewrites the file from the event log before each revision |
| `## Request` | `full_request()`: the request, the attached files and uploads, and each delivered addition |
| `## Route` | The category, the track (or `none`), and the projects in scope |
| `## Research documents` | The paths of the research files, oldest first. Omitted when empty. |
| `## Spec` | The spec path, its summary, and `approved: true` or `false` |
| `## Plan` | The master plan path and its summary |
| `## Phases` | One line for each phase: `passed review`, `blocked: <reason>`, `not started`, or `in progress`. It lists the implementer report, and the review ledger when a review ran. |
| `## Feedback rounds` | The text of each round, a note for a requirement change, and the phases that built it |

### When the runner writes it

- Before the planner opens an `ImplementationReview` gate. The payload of the gate holds `context_path`.
- Before a spawn whose input files include the context path. `perform_spawn` checks `req.inputs.context_files`.

If the write fails, the step returns `Could not write <path>: <error>`. The driver then appends a `Note` event, like it does for every failed step.

## Views of session state for the browser

The browser does not read the fold. [`crates/ostra-engine/src/view.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/view.rs) projects the fold into the types that the API returns. Each function takes a `SessionState` and returns plain data.

### Session status

`summary` picks the status in this order:

1. `Completed`, if `completed` is set.
2. `Failed`, if `failed` is set.
3. `Paused`, if `paused` is set.
4. `Waiting`, if at least one gate is open and no execution runs.
5. `Running`, in all other cases.

The cost in the summary is the cost of finished executions plus the judge cost that the runner keeps in memory. The runner updates the session row at each append and at each usage delta. The list of sessions thus shows the cost when executions run.

### Stage label

`inferred_stage` returns a lane and a label from the latest activity. The first rule that matches wins:

1. A completed session shows `Complete`.
2. A failed session shows `Stopped: ` and the first line of the error, cut at 120 characters.
3. A session paused by containment shows the text that names the execution.
4. An open gate shows `Waiting: <title>` in the lane of the gate.
5. A running execution shows a label such as `Implementing phase 2`, `Reviewing phase 2, pass 1`, `Reviewing tests of phase 2, pass 1`, or `Writing tests for phase 2`. Other executions show the label of their stage.
6. A running command shows `Formatting <project>` or `Staging reviewed files in <project>`.
7. A session with no category shows `Classifying the request`. Otherwise it shows `Working`.

### Other projections

| Function | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `stages` | One `StageCard` for each stage. The status is `Pending`, `Running`, `Waiting`, `Done`, `Skipped`, `Failed`, or `Blocked`. A work loop shows `Waiting` when it is at a cap, at a rescue gate, or failed. |
| `phases` | One `PhaseView` for each phase. The status is `Removed`, `Blocked`, `Passed`, `Queued`, `Reviewing`, or `Implementing`. The tests field is `none`, `skipped`, `passed`, `blocked`, `queued`, or `running`. |
| `artifacts` | The files of the session, without duplicates, in this order: uploads, research, spec, plan, phase files, reports, ledgers, the book, and the completion report |
| `run_labels` | The label of each execution, sorted by start time and then by ID. The key is the agent, the project, and the base label. The first execution has the base label and later ones get `· pass n`. |
| `decorate` | Adds the run label, the transcript flag, the project folder, and the newest open gate of the execution |
| `execution_groups` | Executions grouped by agent and project, in the order of the first start of each group |
| `tree_session` | The node of the session in the Sessions tree. Its cost is the larger of the summary cost and the sum of the execution costs. |
| `fact_checks` | Each fact-check pass of the spec and the plan, with its version, its verdict, and `current` when it checked the latest version |
| `file_changes` | The files that the work passes reported as changed in one project, each with the latest finished execution that reported it |
| `detail` | The `SessionDetail` of the session page: summary, stages, phases, executions, gates, decisions, artifacts, the completion report text, groups, fact checks, files, uploads, and additions |

`file_changes` reads the `changed_files` list in the submit of each finished execution. It turns each path into a path relative to the project with `/` separators. It drops a path that leaves the project. If two executions reported one path, it keeps the one with the later end time. [Project files, Git dock, and cloning](project-files-and-git.md) uses it for the attribution of changed files.

A harness execution has a terminal only when the engine holds its token. `detail` and `Engine::execution` set `has_terminal` from the live executions. The transcript flag is true when the terminal log file exists in the session folder.

## Constants and limits

| Name | Value | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `STOPPED_BY_USER` | `Stopped by the user.` | The error of a stopped session and of its cancelled executions |
| `STOPPED_EXECUTION` | `You stopped this execution.` | The error of a cancelled execution that has no error text |
| `NO_PRIOR_FINDINGS` | `no findings on the previous pass` | The `Prior findings:` value after a clean fact-check pass |
| `PAUSE_RESUME_NOTE` | `Continue the workflow.` | The note that a resumed execution hears |
| `RESUMED_STATUS` | `The session continued, so this run resumes where it stopped.` | The Activity line where a resumed execution continues |
| `MAX_CONTEXT_FILES` | `50` files | The files that one request or addition can attach |
| `INSPECT_PROMPT` | A system prompt text | The instruction of a read-only reopened session |
| `INSPECT_TIMEOUT_SECS` | `14400` seconds | The time after which a read-only session ends |
| `FORMAT_NOT_APPROVED` | A fixed message | The output of a format step that waits for approval |
| Format command limit | `600` seconds | The time that the format command can run |
| Staging command limit | `60` seconds | The time that `git add` can run |
| Output tail | `4000` bytes | The part of command output that `CommandRan` keeps |
| Slot wait | `2` seconds | The longest wait between two checks of a waiting spawn |
| Notice channel | `4096` notices | The capacity of the engine broadcast channel |
| `limits.max_parallel_executions` | `3`, minimum `1` | Executions that run at one time in a workspace |
| `limits.session_budget_usd` | `25.0`, `0` for no limit | Dollars that a session spends before the budget gate |

The planner and the review loop use these constants of `state.rs`. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) owns their values and rules:

- `REVIEW_CAP`
- `FACTCHECK_RECURRING_LIMIT`
- `ERROR_RETRIES`
- `SUFFICIENCY_ROUNDS`
- `AUTO_FIXABLE_PARAM`

### Limits of this design

- The log records what happened. It does not undo anything. A stop leaves the file changes of the session in place.
- The budget check runs before a spawn and not during an execution. Ostra does not cancel a running execution at the limit.
- The slot limit is for one workspace in one server process. It does not limit the judge calls.
- A restart interrupts every execution that was not waiting. The work of the interrupted execution starts again, and the cost of the first start stays in the total.
