sections.title: Judge calls and YOLO mode
sections.summary: Explains the ten judge calls, their JSON schemas, the judge route, how the engine stores and overrides a decision, how YOLO answers gates, the judge prompts, and the advisor and quick-answer agents.
sections.body:
## What judge calls are and why they exist

The engine runs the pipeline from code, and a model decides only where code cannot. Examples are the category of a request and the route of a user answer. Each such decision is a judge call. Free text from a model cannot drive a planner that must stay pure. A judge call therefore returns JSON that matches a schema, and the engine stores the JSON as a `DecisionMade` event with a `reason` for the user.

This page covers:

- The ten judge calls and what each one changes.
- The output schema, the input, and the prompt of each judge call.
- The judge route that picks the model.
- How the engine stores a decision, and how a user overrides it.
- YOLO mode, in which the engine answers gates for the user.
- The advisor agent and the quick-answer agent. They are agents and not judge calls.

The planner that asks for each judge call is on [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md). The event log that stores each decision is on [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md).

## The ten judge calls

The `JudgeKind` enum in `crates/ostra-core/src/event.rs` has ten values. Each value has one prompt file in `assets/judges` with the same name. The planner pushes a `Step::Judge { judge, subject }` step when it needs a decision. The `subject` field tells the judge call what to look at.

| Judge call | The planner asks when | Output fields | Effect when the engine folds the decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `classify` | The session has no category and no Classify decision. | `category`, `projects`, `explore_tasks`, `opts_in`, `reason`, `title` | Sets the category, the scope, the opt-ins, the title, and the first research tasks. |
| `sufficiency` | Research ended, a task has an unjudged `Not covered` item, and the sufficiency round cap is not reached. | `items` (each with `item`, `needed`, `reason`, `task`), `reason` | Queues one more research task for each needed item. It skips an item when an unfinished task with the same project and task exists. |
| `track` | An `IMPLEMENT` session finished research and has no track. | `track` (`light` or `full`), `reason` | Sets the track. |
| `stakes` | An `IMPLEMENT` session on the full track finished its spec stage and has no stakes. | `stakes` (`low`, `medium`, `high`), `reason` | Sets the stakes. The value `low` skips the plan stage and creates one inline phase for each project in scope. |
| `feedback` | A feedback round on the implementation has no answer route. | `route`, `targets`, `items`, `research`, `forget`, `reason` | Routes the round to a spec change or to a direct revision, or keeps or drops the text. |
| `route-answer` | A spec or plan answer is held, the user added context, or a phase loop waits for a route. | `route`, `items`, `research`, `forget`, `reason` | Delivers, keeps, or drops the answer, and queues research. |
| `rescue` | An agent returned `STUCK` and its loop waits for a rescue. | `action`, `explore_task`, `fact`, `reason` | Queues research, runs the agent again with a fact, or opens a gate for the user. |
| `resolve-review` | A review loop reached its budget under YOLO. | `action`, `instructions`, `reason` | Starts one fix pass with exact instructions, or blocks the phase. |
| `yolo-answer` | A gate opens under YOLO and `yolo_plan` returns a `Judge` plan. | `answer`, `reason` | None in the fold. The runner turns `answer` into a gate answer. |
| `completion` | The session work ended and no completion decision exists. | `report_markdown`, `reason` | Stores the completion report. |

The caps for sufficiency rounds, review passes, and retries belong to the planner. See [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) for their values.

The `route-answer` call has two other inputs besides a gate answer. The first is context that the user added to a running session. The second is a phase loop in the `AwaitRoute` state. The subject of the call tells the input builder which case it has.

The subject of a decision depends on the judge call:

- `sufficiency`: a comma list of research task numbers.
- `feedback`: the number of the feedback round.
- `route-answer`: the gate ID, or a marker for added context.
- `rescue`: the ID of the stuck execution.
- `resolve-review`: the key of the review loop.
- `yolo-answer`: the gate ID.
- `classify`, `track`, `stakes`, `completion`: no subject.

## Run a judge call

The runner runs each judge call in the same way. The code is `perform_judge` and `call_judge` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs`. The API keys, the provider settings, and the route settings that a judge call needs are on [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md).

1. `perform_judge` takes a snapshot of the session state. It calls `judge_input` to build the user message and a short summary, and `output_schema` to build the schema.
2. `call_judge` loads the system prompt with `judge_prompt(kind.as_str())`. If no prompt exists, it returns the error `No prompt for the {kind} judge.`.
3. `call_judge` resolves the judge route. See the next part.
4. `call_judge` calls `services.judge` with effort `Low`. It tries at most 3 times.
5. `Services::judge` calls `structured` in `crates/ostra-providers/src/lib.rs`. `structured` calls `structured_cancellable` with a new cancellation token.
6. `structured_cancellable` loops at most 2 times. Each loop sends one request with one tool, `decide`, and `tool_choice` forces the tool. If the first response has no `decide` call, the function adds a reminder turn and sends a second request. The `max_tokens` value is 16000.
7. The runner adds the cost of the call to the cost of the session.
8. The runner checks the output with `validate`. The check parses the JSON into the output type of the judge call. For `feedback`, the output must also have at least 1 target. For `yolo-answer`, the check always passes, and `yolo_answer_from_judge` checks the answer later.
9. The runner appends a `DecisionMade` event with the output and the `reason`.

The providers, the request headers, the token reserves, and the provider retry are on [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md). The tool name `decide` is the constant `DECIDE_TOOL`.

### Sequence of one judge call

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Planner
    participant Runner
    participant Factory as AgentsFactory
    participant Services
    participant Provider
    participant Store
    Planner->>Runner: Step::Judge with judge and subject
    Runner->>Runner: judge_input and output_schema
    Runner->>Factory: judge_prompt(kind)
    Factory-->>Runner: system prompt
    Runner->>Runner: resolve_route(JUDGE_ROUTE)
    Runner->>Services: judge(route, system, input, schema, Low)
    Services->>Provider: structured with forced decide tool
    Provider-->>Services: tool input and usage
    Services-->>Runner: value and usage
    Runner->>Runner: validate(value)
    Runner->>Store: append DecisionMade
    Store-->>Planner: fold gives the next step
```

The retry loop of `call_judge` has this shape:

```rust
for attempt in 0..3 {
    match self.services.judge(&route, &system, &input, schema.clone(), Effort::Low).await {
        Ok((value, usage)) => {
            *lock(&self.judge_cost).entry(session.clone()).or_insert(0.0) += usage.cost_usd;
            if validate(&value) {
                let reason = judge::reason_of(&value);
                self.append(session, SessionEvent::DecisionMade { /* id, judge, subject, summary, output, reason */ })?;
                return Ok(value);
            }
            last = "the answer did not match the schema".into();
        }
        Err(e) => last = e,
    }
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500 * (attempt + 1))).await;
}
```

### What happens when

- **The output does not match the schema.** The runner waits 500 ms, 1000 ms, and 1500 ms after the first, second, and third attempt. It then tries again, except after the third attempt. The runner pays for each attempt.
- **The model does not call `decide`.** `structured_cancellable` adds one reminder turn: "Call the `decide` tool now with your decision. Do not answer in text." It then sends a second request. If that response also has no `decide` call, the function fails with the error `the model did not call the \`decide\` tool`.
- **The model refuses.** `structured_cancellable` fails at once with a refusal error and sends no reminder. The attempt counts as failed.
- **The route does not resolve.** `call_judge` returns the error of route resolution before the first attempt.
- **All 3 attempts fail, and the judge call is not `completion`.** The runner appends `SessionFailed` with the text `The {kind} judge call failed: {last}. Check that the judge route has a provider with a working API key.`
- **All 3 attempts fail, and the judge call is `completion`.** The runner does not fail the session, because the work is done. It stores a fallback decision with the summary `Fallback after a failed judge call`. The report lists the state of the session and has no prose.
- **The `yolo-answer` call fails.** The runner appends a `Note` event that starts with `YOLO could not answer`. The gate waits for the user.
- **The Classify output does not parse when the fold reads it.** The fold sets the session to failed with the text `The Classify judge returned output that does not match its schema.`
- **The server restarts.** The decision is an event in the log. The fold restores it, and the planner does not ask the same judge call again.
- **Execution slots.** A judge call does not take a slot of the parallel execution limit. See [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md) for the limit.

The cost of every judge call goes into a total for each session. The `cost_usd` of the session is the sum of its executions and this total.

## Judge route and model

A judge call is not an agent execution. It is one API request through the provider of the routed model. The constant `JUDGE_ROUTE` in `crates/ostra-core/src/agent.rs` has the value `judge`. It is the routing key of every judge call, and it sits beside the agent names.

`call_judge` asks route resolution for the model of `JUDGE_ROUTE`, with the default tier `Advanced`. [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns route resolution, the tiers, and the settings that change the judge model.

The route supplies only the model. `Services::judge` in `crates/ostra-server/src/services.rs` calls `providers.for_model(&route.model)`, and the executor of the route has no effect. A judge call needs an API key for the provider of that model, also when the agents run in a harness. The effort is `Low` in code, and no setting changes it. A judge call cannot be switched off.

## Judge output schemas

`output_schema(kind, answer_schema)` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/judge.rs` builds the JSON schema of each judge call. The model must give its answer as the input of the `decide` tool, and this schema is the input schema of the tool.

Every schema has a required `reason` field. The description of the field is "One or two sentences the user will read." The function `reason_of` reads this field, and the engine stores it with the decision. The schema of `sufficiency` also has a `reason` inside each item, which is not required to be one sentence.

### Fields that more than one judge call uses

- **`items`** (`feedback`, `route-answer`). The list has one `AnswerItem` for each answer. Its fields are `id`, `disposition`, `note`, and `stages`. All four are required in the schema.
- **`disposition`.** It has 3 values: `deliver`, `remember`, and `discard`. The value `deliver` means that the current stage acts on the answer now. The value `remember` keeps the `note` for later stages only. The value `discard` drops the answer, and the gate answer stays in the log.
- **`stages`.** It lists the later stages that also get the `note`. The values are `implement`, `tests`, and `docs` (the `NoteStage` enum).
- **`ANSWER_ITEM`.** The value is `answer`. It is the item ID for a gate with one text and no question IDs.
- **`research`.** The list holds `{project, task}` entries. The schema sets `maxItems` to `MAX_ANSWER_RESEARCH`, which is 3.
- **`forget`.** The list holds IDs of notes that the user took back or replaced, such as `N1`. A forgotten note stays in the log but reaches no agent.
- **`route`** (`AnswerRoute`). The values are `requirement_change`, `implementation_detail`, and `stage_choice`. The schema of `feedback` offers only the first two. The schema of `route-answer` offers all three.

### Merge of split items

A model can split one answer into several items. `item_for(items, id)` merges the parts of one ID with these rules:

1. If the judge gave no item for the ID, the answer is delivered.
2. If any part is `deliver`, the result is `deliver`, because the user gave the answer.
3. Otherwise, if any part is `remember`, the result is `remember`.
4. Otherwise, the result is `discard`.
5. The note and the stages come from the first part that has stages.

When the ID is `answer`, `parts_for` counts every item. On a gate with one text, every item is about that text.

### Session title

The `title` field of `classify` is a 2 to 5 word label. `clean_title` joins the words with single spaces, removes wrapping quotes (`"`, `'`, or a backtick) and a final period, and cuts the text to `TITLE_CHARS`, which is 60 characters. It returns nothing when no text is left. The `title` field has a serde default, so a decision from an older version parses with an empty title.

### Old decisions

The output types give `reason`, `items`, `research`, `forget`, and `title` serde defaults. A decision that an older version stored still parses. Without `items`, the engine delivers every answer.

## Judge inputs and excerpt limits

`judge_input(state, kind, subject, projects)` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/judge_input.rs` builds the user message of a judge call and a short summary. The engine stores the summary with the decision. The input has only what the judge call needs, because the model sees no other state.

| Judge call | The input holds | Summary stored |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classify` | The request, the toggles of the New task form (`tests`, `docs`, `yolo`), the pinned projects, and each project with its path, stack, initialization state, and module map areas. | `Request: ` and the first line of the request |
| `sufficiency` | The request, each finished research task with its findings, the `Not covered` items of the judged tasks, and the project keys that a task can target. | The count of `Not covered` items and documents |
| `stakes` | The request, the approved spec (counts, summary, and an excerpt), and the projects in scope. | `Approved spec and request` |
| `track` | The request, the projects in scope, and every research document with an excerpt. | `Research for: ` and the first line of the request |
| `feedback` | The request, the track, the current spec or a note that none exists, the phases built so far with their reports, the research documents, the kept notes, and the feedback text. | `Feedback: ` and the first line of the text |
| `route-answer` | The request, the session facts, the gate with each question and its numbered options, and the answer of the user. For added context: the text and the stopped work. | `Answer: ` and the first line of the answer |
| `rescue` | The request, the stuck agent, its phase, the diagnostic verbatim, what it needs, and earlier rescue decisions. | `STUCK: ` and the first line of the need |
| `resolve-review` | The phase and loop counters, the open findings, the review ledger, and the phase file. | `Open findings and the review ledger` |
| `yolo-answer` | The request, the gate title and explanation, the gate payload as JSON, and the research findings, the spec excerpt, or the plan excerpt that the gate kind needs. | The title of the gate |
| `completion` | The state of the whole session. Under YOLO it also lists each gate that the engine answered, with its title, gate ID, and reason, under `Decided for you under YOLO`. | `Session state at completion` |

Two constants cap the file text in an input:

- `FILE_EXCERPT` is 24000. It limits the text of one file, such as a spec, a plan, a ledger, or a phase file.
- `TRACK_EXCERPT` is 12000. It limits each research document in the `track` input. The `track` call reads every research document of the session, so each document gets a smaller limit.

The limit counts bytes. `excerpt_n` cuts at a character boundary and adds the line `(truncated at N characters)`. When a file cannot be read, the input has the text `(could not read <path>)` in place of the file.

The classify input has this rule: when the user pinned projects, the judge sees only the pinned projects, because they are the whole scope (Rule O6). A project without an inventory shows the note `not initialized: no pipeline task may target it`.

## Decisions in the log and the store

A decision is the `DecisionMade` event of a judge call. Its fields are `id` (a `DecisionId`), `judge`, `subject`, `input_summary`, `output`, and `reason`. The fold in `crates/ostra-engine/src/state.rs` keeps each one as a `DecisionRecord` with an `overridden` flag and a time. It then calls `on_decision`, which applies the effects in the table of the judge calls.

The runner also writes each decision to the `decisions` table of the workspace database. The columns are `id`, `session_id`, `judge`, `subject`, `input_summary`, `output`, `reason`, `overridden`, `can_override`, and `at`. The table is a copy for queries. The event log is the source of truth. The schema and the database are on [Storage: databases and lesson memory](storage.md).

The session view builds a `DecisionView` for each decision. The field `can_override` of the view is not the column. `view.rs` computes it from the fold with `SessionState::can_override` on every read. The console shows each decision as "Ostra chose X because Y" with an override button when `can_override` is true.

## Override a decision

A user can replace the output of some decisions before work depends on them. The request is `POST /api/decisions/{id}/override` with the body `OverrideDecision { output, reason }`. The handler calls `override_decision` in the runner and returns the new `DecisionView`.

`override_decision` does these checks in order:

1. The decision must exist. Otherwise the error is `NotFound`.
2. `can_override` must be true. Otherwise the error is `Work that depends on this decision has already started, so it can no longer be overridden.`
3. The new output must parse as the output type of the judge call. Only `classify`, `stakes`, `track`, and `sufficiency` have such a type here. Otherwise the error is `The override does not match the decision's output shape.`

After the checks, the runner calls `mark_overridden`. It replaces `output` and `reason` in the table and sets `overridden` to 1. Then it appends a `DecisionOverridden { id, output, reason }` event. The fold replaces the output and the reason of the record and applies the new output with `on_decision`.

The rule for `can_override` depends on the judge call:

| Judge call | The override is possible until |
| --- | --- |
| `classify` | A research task starts, or a phase starts work. |
| `sufficiency` | The first spec run starts. |
| `track` | The first spec run starts, or a phase starts work. |
| `stakes` | The first plan run starts, or a phase starts work. |
| Every other judge call | Never. The override is not possible. |

An ended session cannot be overridden. A `yolo-answer` decision also cannot be overridden, so the undo link that its prompt mentions has no override behind it.

The override changes the effects as follows:

- **`classify`.** The fold applies the new category, scope, opt-ins, and title. It drops the research tasks that came from the first Classify decision and the phases, and queues the new tasks. An override without a title keeps the old title.
- **`sufficiency`.** The fold drops all unstarted research tasks with the origin `Sufficiency`, not only the tasks of the overridden decision. It keeps every task whose origin is not `Sufficiency` and every task that started. Then it queues the tasks of the new output. The override does not add 1 to the count of sufficiency rounds.
- **`stakes`.** The fold sets the new stakes and clears the phases. For `low` on an `IMPLEMENT` request, it creates the inline phases.
- **`track`.** The fold sets the new track.

## YOLO mode

Without YOLO, a session stops at each gate and waits for the user. In a long session, this wait blocks every step that follows. YOLO mode tells the engine to answer the gates, so the session runs without a wait. The prompt of the `yolo-answer` judge states the limit: YOLO changes who answers, and it never changes what must be true. Guards still apply, an approval still needs a fact-check `PASS`, `BLOCKER` security findings are still removed, and the deny rules of the user still apply. The guards are on [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md).

### How a session gets YOLO mode

- The user sets the `yolo` toggle on the New task form. It is the `yolo` field of `SessionOptions`.
- `start_session` sets `options.yolo` to true for every new session when `yolo.default` is true. `init_project` passes `yolo.default` to an init session in the same way.
- The user turns YOLO on or off in a running session with `POST /api/sessions/{id}/yolo` and the body `SetYolo { enabled }`. The runner appends a `YoloSet` event. The planner reads the flag on each pass, so the change applies to the next gate or tool call.
- When the user turns YOLO on, `set_yolo` answers every open `Permission` gate at once with `AllowOnce`. The reason is `YOLO was switched on, so every permission ask is allowed.`

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored | Takes effect | Shows state | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yolo.default` | `false` | The machine registry, in the access record of the workspace. `workspace.toml` never holds it, and Ostra never reads it from a folder file. | For each session that starts after the change | The `yolo` flag of the session summary, and the section `Decided for you` of the completion report | Set `yolo.default` to `false` in the settings editor |
| The `yolo` toggle of the New task form (`SessionOptions.yolo`) | Off, unless `yolo.default` is `true` | The `SessionCreated` event | At the start of the session | The `yolo` flag of the session summary | Do not set the toggle |
| `POST /api/sessions/{id}/yolo` with `enabled` | The value from the start of the session | A `YoloSet` event in the session log | At the next gate or tool call | The `yolo` flag of the session summary | Send `enabled: false` |

The registry holds `yolo.default` for this reason: the module comment of `crates/ostra-workspace/src/trust.rs` states that the permission mode and YOLO live in the registry and are never read from a folder file. A folder file can arrive with a repository, a `git pull`, or an agent edit. See [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) for the approval of folder files.

### How the planner and the runner answer a gate

The planner method `flows` pushes a `Step::YoloAnswer { gate }` step for each open gate of a running session. It skips a paused session, because a paused session starts nothing. It also skips two cases:

- A `Permission` gate. The execution that asked answers it. Under YOLO, the runner opens the gate and answers it with `AllowOnce`. The reason is `Under YOLO every permission ask is allowed.`
- A gate that `yolo_leaves_open` names: `BudgetReached`, and `ExecutionFailed` for an execution that the user stopped (Rule P4). Spending more money and retrying a stopped run are decisions for the user.

`perform_yolo` calls `yolo_plan` for the gate. The plan is `Fixed` or `Judge`.

#### Flow of one YOLO answer

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Gate opens while yolo is on"] --> B{"Left open by yolo_leaves_open?"}
    B -- yes --> C["Gate waits for the user"]
    B -- no --> D{"yolo_plan"}
    D -- Fixed --> E["Append GateAnswered, source Yolo, with reason"]
    D -- Judge --> F["Call the yolo-answer judge"]
    F -- call fails --> G["Append Note, gate waits"]
    F -- ok --> H["yolo_answer_from_judge"]
    H -- refused --> G
    H -- accepted --> E
```

| Gate | Answered by | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OpenQuestions` | The judge | One answer for each question. The schema fixes `minItems` and `maxItems` to the question count. A missing answer gets the label of the recommended option. |
| `SpecApproval`, `PlanApproval` | The judge | An approval. The engine refuses it when `approved` is true and the current artifact has no fact-check `PASS`. It also refuses a rejection with no feedback. |
| `Stuck` | The judge | The option `fact` with text, or `block`. The option `fact` with no text becomes `block`, because the judge must not guess a fact that only the user has. |
| `ImplementationReview` | Fixed | `done`. Only the user can say what to change. |
| `ClosingGate` | Fixed | For each project, tests and docs are on only when the request already asked for them (Rules T2 and T3). |
| `FactCheckRecurring` | Fixed | `another-round` when `passes` is below 6. Otherwise `stop`. |
| `ReviewCap` | Fixed | `another-pass`. |
| `PhaseBlocked` | Fixed | `leave`. The engine records the block and runs independent work (Rule D9). |
| `ExecutionFailed` | Fixed | `retry` when fewer than 2 earlier answered `ExecutionFailed` gates exist for the same agent. Otherwise `abandon`. |
| `HarnessFailure` | Fixed | `native`. The execution moves to the native executor. |
| `SkillApproval` | Fixed | The default disposition of each skill in the proposal. |
| `Permission` | Fixed | `AllowOnce`. |
| `BudgetReached` | Nobody | The gate stays open. |

The prompt `assets/judges/yolo-answer.md` also describes some gates that the table lists as Fixed, such as the closing gate and the review cap. The judge never gets those gates, because `yolo_plan` answers them in code.

The engine checks the judge answer in `yolo_answer_from_judge`. This excerpt shows the approval guard:

```rust
let passed = match &g.payload {
    GatePayload::SpecApproval { .. } => s.spec.passed_current(),
    _ => s.plan.passed_current(),
};
if approved && !passed {
    return Err("approval requires a fact-check PASS".into());
}
if !approved && feedback.is_none() {
    return Err("a rejection needs feedback saying what to change".into());
}
```

### What happens when

- **The `yolo-answer` call fails or the engine refuses its answer.** The runner appends a `Note` event: `YOLO could not answer "<title>": <error>. The gate waits for you.` or `The YOLO answer was refused: <error>. The gate waits for you.` The gate stays open.
- **The gate has an answer when the runner appends.** `perform_yolo` checks again and does nothing if a user answered first.
- **The answer has content.** The runner sets `routed` with `answer_needs_route`, the same function that it uses for a user answer. A YOLO answer with text then also goes to the `route-answer` judge before an agent sees it.
- **The user pauses the session.** The planner starts no YOLO answer until the session continues.
- **A push notice.** Under YOLO, the runner sends no push notice for a new gate, except for a `HarnessFailure` gate that needs a login.

### The review loop under YOLO

The review loop has a larger budget under YOLO. `YOLO_REVIEW_BUDGET` is 10 review passes for each loop. Without YOLO, the cap is `REVIEW_CAP`. The values and the loop rules are on [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md).

At the budget, the loop does not open a `ReviewCap` gate. It goes to the `resolve-review` judge. The judge reads the ledger and returns one of two actions:

- **`fix`.** The engine starts one fix pass with one exact instruction for each open finding. It adds 1 to `resolve_rounds` and 1 to the cap, so one verification review follows.
- **`block`.** The engine marks the phase blocked and records the open findings and the ledger path in the completion report. Only work that does not depend on the phase continues.

The loop returns to the judge again only if the last resolution round reduced the count of open findings. If a resolution round does not reduce the count, the engine blocks the phase with the text `The review loop stopped converging after N resolution rounds`. `BLOCKER` security findings never reach this judge call.

### The completion report

The `completion` input lists each gate that YOLO answered. The prompt asks the judge to write one line for each decision in a section `Decided for you`, with the reason. This list lets the user read what the engine decided.

## Prompts in assets/judges

The folder `assets/judges` has one Markdown file for each judge call. `ostra_agents::judge_prompt(name)` reads the files from the embedded assets and caches them. The runner calls it through `AgentsFactory::judge_prompt`. The prompt is the system message of the call.

Each prompt has the same four parts: the role text, `## Input`, a part that tells the judge how to decide, and `## Output`. The decide part is `## Decide` in 8 prompts. It is `## Decide, by gate kind` in `yolo-answer.md` and `## Write` in `completion.md`, which has no `## Decide`. The `route-answer.md` prompt also has the parts `## The user decides` and `## Context the user added`. The `## Output` part of each prompt tells the model to call `decide` once.

The `reason` field differs by prompt. The prompts for `sufficiency` and `completion` ask for a `reason` of one sentence. The other 8 prompts ask for one or two sentences for the user. The schema description of `reason` says "One or two sentences the user will read" for every call.

The prompts cite rule IDs such as J1, C2, O6, D1, D2, D9, D10, T3, and T5. Those rules are on [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md).

| File | What it tells the judge | Which way doubt resolves, and why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `classify.md` | Pick 1 of 10 categories by what the request asks Ostra to produce. Return the projects, the research tasks, the opt-ins, and a title. | Pick the category that gives more of the pipeline, because a skipped stage gives a wrong result and an extra stage costs one round. |
| `sufficiency.md` | For each `Not covered` item, say if the request depends on it. | Mark the item needed, because a wasted research pass costs one round and a missed dependency gives a wrong spec after approval. |
| `track.md` | Pick `light` unless the research shows one of 6 kinds of evidence for `full`. | Pick `light`, because the user reviews the built result and a spec round costs several approvals. |
| `stakes.md` | Rate the approved spec as `low`, `medium`, or `high`. | Rate higher, because a skipped plan removes the phase review. |
| `feedback.md` | Pick the answer route, the target projects, and what happens to the feedback. | Pick `requirement_change` when a requirement addresses the subject, because a spec that disagrees with the code misleads every later stage. |
| `route-answer.md` | Decide where a user answer goes before an agent sees it. The user decides, and Ostra rules are the only limit. | Pick `requirement_change`, because a stale spec damages every later stage and an extra spec round costs one round trip. |
| `rescue.md` | Pick `rerun`, `explore`, or `gate` for a stuck agent. | After 2 rescues of the same phase with the same diagnostic, pick `gate`, because neither rescue changed the failure. |
| `resolve-review.md` | Pick `fix` or `block` for a loop at its budget. | Pick `block` when the finding count does not fall or the findings need a fact only the user has. |
| `yolo-answer.md` | Answer a gate for the user. Never invent a requirement or a fact. | Choose the answer that sets the work aside, when the gate needs a fact only the user has. |
| `completion.md` | Write the report in a fixed order of sections. Report every stage that did not run (Rule T7). | Report only what the input records. A command that the input does not show did not run. |

The prompt of `classify` also keeps the pipeline coherent. A request that asks for files to change is never `RESEARCH` or `QUICK_ANSWER`. An edit to a prompt, a `SKILL.md`, an agent file, or a judge prompt under `assets/` is `PROMPT`, because prompt generation applies the prompt writing rules. A documentation book about existing code is `DOCS`.

The prompts for agents are on [Agents, prompts, and coordination](agents-and-prompts.md). `AgentsFactory::judge_prompt` also serves an agent prompt for the name `__agent:<agent>`. The side panel uses it for the quick-answer prompt.

## Advisor agent

The advisor is an agent and not a judge call, and it is not a side-panel agent. It reads one pipeline step that failed or got stuck, and it tells Ostra how to continue. Today the planner runs it only for the init of a project that an agent created (Rule O5). The definition is in `assets/agents/advisor`.

### Why it exists

The engine keeps little context about why a step failed. A plain retry of a step with the same inputs repeats the same failure. The advisor reads what the step saw and did, and it states a cause and an action.

### What it gets and returns

`advisor_request` in `crates/ostra-engine/src/init.rs` builds the spawn. The input lines are:

- `Failed step`: the agent and mode, such as `initializer detect`.
- `Problem`: the error, the stuck report, or the check that Ostra ran on the result.
- `Step inputs`: the spawn block of the failed run.
- `Step result`: the submit payload of the failed run, cut at `MAX_STEP_RESULT_CHARS`, which is 8000 characters.
- `Step context`: what the step is for.
- `Earlier guidance`: the advice that did not fix the step.

The advisor submits `action`, `guidance`, and `reason`. The action is `retry` or `escalate`. The agent is read-only. Its default tier is `advanced`, its timeout is 900 seconds, and its effort is `high` on every executor.

The prompt has two rules for the decision:

- Keep the step inside its own instructions. A guard refuses a write that the step is not allowed to do, so a retry that asks for it fails again.
- Escalate only for what the output of the step needs. If the step can finish without a missing fact, retry and say how.

The guidance for a retry has at most 12 short lines. It names concrete paths and values.

### What happens when

- **The advisor returns `retry`.** The engine stores the guidance, clears the result of the failed step, and runs the step again. The step reads the guidance on its `Advisor guidance:` line.
- **The advisor returns `escalate`, fails, or returns no usable result.** The engine sets `escalated`. It appends the reason to the failure text, and the failed-step gate opens for the user.
- **The advice run is interrupted.** The engine changes nothing and the planner asks again.
- **The step failed twice with advice.** `MAX_ADVICE` is 2 advisor rounds for each failing step. After that, the user gets the gate.
- **The user stopped the step.** The user gets the gate and not the advisor, because the advisor retries a step that the user stopped (Rule P4).
- **The init is not of a created project.** The user gets the gate. See [Project init and skills](init-and-skills.md) for the init flow.

The route key of the advisor is `advisor`.

## Quick-answer agent in the side panel

The side panel answers one question about the projects of the workspace, outside the pipeline. The quick-answer agent does the work. The definition is in `assets/agents/quick-answer`. The agent reads the code, the project memory, and retrieved pages. It writes no file and changes no pipeline state.

### The flow

1. The console sends `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/ask` with `AskQuestion { question, session }`. An empty question returns the error `Ask a question first.`
2. `Engine::ask` takes the first project of the workspace. If none exists, it returns `Add a project first.`
3. `ask` builds a first message. It lists every project with its path. When the question comes from a session, it also lists the artifacts of that session.
4. `prepare_quick` resolves the route with the key `quick-answer`, the default tier `balanced`, and the native executor. [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns route resolution.
5. The runner starts the native executor in a background task and returns `AskStarted { execution }` to the console.

### The limits

- **Executor.** The native executor only. `forced_executor` also forces it for the agent `QuickAnswer` in a session. See [Native executor loop](native-executor.md).
- **Permission mode.** `Plan`. YOLO is off, and no session exists.
- **Effort and timeout.** Effort `medium` on every executor. The timeout is 300 seconds.
- **Tools.** Read, search, glob, web search, web fetch, memory recall, code tools, and `DocsSearch`.
- **Slot.** The side-panel run takes no execution slot.
- **Records.** The execution row has no session. The cost report lists it under `side-panel`. A side-panel answer cannot be resumed.
- **Scratch folder.** The session folder is a temporary folder named `ostra-quick/<execution id>`.

The agent submits `answer` and `sources` with the tool `submit_quick_answer`. The prompt makes the agent put the answer first and cite each claim about code as `path:line`. Most answers have at most 150 words. The agent calls memory recall first, tries at least 3 term variations before it reports an absence, and checks a recalled lesson against the current code.

A question that asks for a code change is a work request. The agent does not do the work. It tells the user to press **Turn into task**, so the request runs as a session with a spec, review, and gates.

The pipeline uses the same agent for the category `QUICK_ANSWER`. In that case the planner spawns it inside the session, and the answer becomes the completion report. A failure opens an `ExecutionFailed` gate.

## Judge and advisor evals

The evals check the judge prompts against cases that an engineer wrote. They call real models and cost money, so `#[ignore]` marks them. The variables and the commands are on [Testing and evals](testing.md).

- **`tests/evals/judges.toml`** has 83 cases: 23 for `classify`, 25 for `route_answer`, 16 for `feedback`, 14 for `track`, 3 for `stakes`, and 2 for `sufficiency`. No case covers `rescue`, `resolve-review`, `yolo-answer`, or `completion`.
- **`crates/ostra-server/tests/judge_evals.rs`** builds the session that the engine builds for each judge call, with the same fold and `judge_input`. It calls the judge with `structured` and `output_schema`, `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` times for each model (default 3). It scores the category, the projects, the track, the stakes, the needed items, the answer route, the targets, the dispositions, the stages, the research, and `forget`. It writes a report to `target/evals/`. The test `eval_cases_build_their_sessions` runs without a model and checks that each case builds.
- **`tests/evals/advisor.toml`** has 13 cases of failed init steps. Some cases come in pairs with the same problem text and opposite correct answers. A pair catches an advisor that matches the text of the problem and does not read the files.

The test fails only when calls fail, because model results vary from run to run.

sections.title: Agents, prompts, and coordination
sections.summary: How Ostra names its 14 agents, renders each prompt for an executor, builds the typed spawn block and repo brief, validates each submit payload, and lets subagents ask and answer each other.
sections.body:
Ostra runs 14 leaf agents on five kinds of executor: the native loop and four harnesses. Each executor names its tools differently, and each agent needs different inputs and returns a different result. Without one shared layer, every prompt holds five sets of tool names. A missing input shows only when the agent fails. A result in free text forces the engine to scrape it.

This page covers the layer that removes these problems:

- The agent registry in `ostra-core` and the agent definitions in `assets/agents`.
- The prompt renderer in `ostra-agents`, which fills tool names per executor.
- The typed spawn contract, which builds the `Label: value` block that starts a run.
- The repo brief, which adds project facts to the first message.
- The `submit_<agent>` tools, which carry the structured result of each run.
- Subagent coordination, which lets one agent ask another agent a question.

The page stops before the executors that run the agents. See [Native executor loop](native-executor.md) and [Harness executors](harness-executors.md).

## What happens when Ostra spawns an agent

The engine builds each spawn with `AgentsFactory::build` in [`crates/ostra-engine/src/factory.rs`](crates/ostra-engine/src/factory.rs). The planner gives it a `SpawnRequest`, and it returns a `BuiltSpawn`. The steps run in this order:

1. The factory fills the typed spawn struct of the agent from the planner inputs. If a required input is absent, the build returns an error such as `missing task`.
2. The struct renders the `Label: value` spawn block.
3. The factory reads the workspace instructions, the visible artifacts, and the documentation books.
4. `augment` appends the repo brief to the spawn block. The result is the first message.
5. `render_prompt` renders the system prompt for the agent and the executor.
6. The factory resolves the reasoning effort. It uses `resolve_effort` over the workspace settings first. If no route gives a value, it uses `effort_for` from the agent definition.

`BuiltSpawn` holds the system prompt, the first message, the spawn block, the parameters as JSON, the report file, and the effort. The system prompt is the stable part. The first message is the part that changes for each run.

A consult run is a run that answers a question from another subagent. It uses `ConsultParams` in place of the struct of its agent. See [Subagent coordination](#subagent-coordination-between-runs).

## Agent registry and the 14 agents

The `AgentName` enum in [`crates/ostra-core/src/agent.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/agent.rs) lists every leaf agent. The kebab-case name of a variant is also the folder name in `assets/agents/<name>/`. `AgentName::ALL` holds the 14 variants in a fixed order.

| Agent | Default tier | Timeout (`timeout_seconds`) | Session-only | Has `coordinate` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `explore` | advanced | 1800 | yes | yes |
| `generate-spec` | advanced | 1800 | yes | yes |
| `fact-check` | advanced | 1800 | yes | yes |
| `plan` | advanced | 1800 | yes | yes |

| `code-reviewer` | balanced | 1200 | yes | yes |
| `execution-path-analyzer` | balanced | 1200 | yes | no |
| `write-test` | balanced | 2400 | no | yes |
