sections.title: Model providers and pricing
sections.summary: How Ostra talks to the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs through one chat interface, how it streams and retries, and how it turns token usage into dollars with the models.dev catalog.
sections.body:
## The problem and what the crate does

The native executor must call different model APIs with one loop. The Anthropic Messages API and the OpenAI Responses API differ in their request bodies, stream events, error codes, tool choice, cache markers, and usage fields. Without one interface, the loop, the judge calls, and the tests each need code for every API.

The crate `ostra-providers` solves this with a neutral chat interface. The trait `Provider` takes a `ChatRequest` and returns a `ChatResponse`. Each provider converts the neutral types to its own API and back. The crate also holds a retry policy, a stream reader, and a scripted provider for tests.

The price catalog solves a second problem. A response reports tokens, but a user wants dollars. `ostra_core::pricing` converts the tokens of each response to dollars with prices from the models.dev catalog. The server downloads and caches that catalog in `ostra_server::prices`.

This page covers the interface, the two providers, streaming, retry, the scripted provider, beta headers, token reserves, the price catalog, the cost formula, and the data of the Cost screen. The page stops before the turn loop. [Native executor loop](native-executor.md) explains how the loop uses a provider.

## Neutral request and response types

The neutral types live in `crates/ostra-providers/src/lib.rs`. A provider never exposes the shapes of its API to a caller.

### Request

`ChatRequest::new(model)` sets these defaults:

| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | the argument | The model id without the provider prefix. |
| `system` | empty | A list of `SystemBlock` values. A block has `text` and a `cache` flag that marks the end of a stable prefix. |
| `messages` | empty | A list of `Message` values. Each has a `Role` (`User` or `Assistant`) and a list of `Block` values. |
| `tools` | empty | `ToolDef` values with `name`, `description`, `input_schema`, and `cache`. |
| `server_tools` | none | `ServerTools` with `web_search` and `web_fetch` flags. |
| `max_tokens` | `32000` | The most output tokens that the caller asks for. |
| `effort` | `Effort::High` | The reasoning effort. |
| `tool_choice` | `ToolChoice::Auto` | `Auto`, `Any`, `None`, or `Tool(name)`. |
| `refusal_fallback` | `true` | Lets the provider run a declined request again on its fallback model, on models that support it. |

### Blocks

A `Block` is one of these kinds: `Text`, `Thinking` (with a signature), `RedactedThinking`, `ToolUse`, `ToolResult`, `Opaque`, or `Compaction`. A provider sends `Opaque` and `Compaction` blocks back to the same provider without change. A different provider drops an `Opaque` block. A different provider reads a `Compaction` block as its `summary` text. This rule keeps a signed or encrypted value away from a provider that cannot read it.

### Response and stream events

A `ChatResponse` holds `content`, a `StopReason`, a `Usage` value, the `model` that produced the answer, and an optional `refusal_category`. The `model` can differ from the request after a server-side fallback. The cost uses this model.

`StopReason` has these values:

- `EndTurn`
- `ToolUse`
- `MaxTokens`
- `PauseTurn`: a server-side tool loop paused, so the caller sends the assistant turn back unchanged.
- `Refusal`
- `Other(String)`

During a call, the provider reports progress through an `EventSink`. The events are `TextDelta`, `ThinkingDelta`, `ToolUseStarted`, `ToolInputDelta`, and `ServerToolUsed`. The last event reports a web search or web fetch that ran on the provider side.

### The trait

The trait `Provider` has these methods:

- `name()` returns the provider name.
- `server_tools(model)` returns the server-side tools that the provider offers. The default is none. Anthropic offers web search and web fetch. OpenAI offers web search only. The agent loop supplies a local tool for each missing one.
- `chat(req, on_event, cancel)` runs one streamed call.
- `compact(req, instructions, cancel)` compacts a conversation. The default calls `compact_on_client`.

## Find the provider, the key, and the base URL

The struct `Providers` is the registry of the providers that have a usable key on this machine. [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns the settings fields that name the key variables and the URL, and their defaults. This part owns only the order in which the registry reads the key and URL sources.

### Key lookup order

The function `lookup_key` checks these sources in order and stops at the first non-empty value:

1. The environment variable that `api_key_env` names. The source is `env:NAME`.
2. The environment variable that `auth_token_env` names. The key is a bearer token.
3. The saved `api_key` from the browser. The source is `saved`. [Secrets, credentials, and Web Push](secrets-and-push.md) explains how Ostra stores it.
4. The saved `auth_token`. The key is a bearer token.
5. The OS keychain, with the service from `keychain_service` and the provider name as the entry. The source is `keychain`.

A bearer key goes in the header `Authorization: Bearer`, because gateways and proxies take a token in that form. The type `ApiKey` never prints its value: `Debug` writes `ApiKey(***)` and `Display` writes `***`. The OpenAI provider always sends its key as a bearer token, whichever source the key came from.

### Base URL order

The function `resolve_base_url` returns the URL and its source. The order is:

1. `base_url` in the settings entry (source `config`).
2. The variable that `base_url_env` names (source `env:NAME`).
3. The saved URL (source `saved`).
4. The default (source `default`).

The function `display_url` removes the user, the password, the query, and the fragment before the URL reaches the browser, because each of them can carry a credential. An invalid URL shows as `(not a valid URL)`.

### Build, reload, and resolve

- `Providers::from_config` builds the registry from the settings and the saved credentials.
- `Providers::rebuild` (private, in `lib.rs`) adds one status for each configured name. A name with no usable key gets `has_key: false` and no client. `rebuild` skips such a name before it checks the name.
- Only the names `anthropic` and `openai` build a client. An unknown name that has a usable key writes the warning `unknown provider in config; ignored` and gets no client. An unknown name with no key is skipped without a warning, and its status shows `has_key: false`.
- `Providers::reload` rebuilds the registry in place. The executors hold the registry, so the next model call uses the new keys. The credentials code calls `reload` after a save.
- `Providers::register(name, provider)` adds a provider that has no settings entry, such as the scripted provider. Its status source is `registered`, and `reload` keeps it.
- `Providers::for_model("provider:model")` splits at the first colon. Both parts must be non-empty, or the call returns `ProviderError::BadModel`. A name that is not in the registry returns `NoKey` for `anthropic` and `openai`, and `UnknownProvider` for any other name.

A change to a key or a URL takes effect after a restart, or after a credentials save calls `reload`. The provider status shows `has_key`, `source`, `base_url`, and `base_url_source`.

## Anthropic requests

The struct `Anthropic` in `crates/ostra-providers/src/anthropic.rs` posts to `{base_url}/v1/messages` with `stream: true`. The default base URL is `https://api.anthropic.com`. The provider removes a trailing slash.

### Headers and client

- The key goes in `x-api-key`, or in `Authorization: Bearer` for a bearer key.
- `anthropic-version` is `2023-06-01`.
- `accept` is `text/event-stream`.
- `anthropic-beta` holds the beta names joined with commas. Ostra sends it only when the list is not empty.

The HTTP client sets a connect timeout of 20 seconds and sets no total timeout. The client follows no redirect, because the key header can follow a redirect to another host.

### Model capabilities

The function `caps(model)` returns the abilities of a model from its id. The function `is_model` matches an exact id or an id with a dated snapshot suffix, a hyphen and 8 digits, such as `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`.

| Model ids | Thinking | Effort values | Forced tool choice | Server fallbacks | On-demand compaction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-mythos-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5` | adaptive | all | no | yes | yes |
| `claude-opus-5` | adaptive | all | yes | yes | yes |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` | adaptive | all | no | no | yes |
| `claude-fable-5`, `claude-mythos-5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-sonnet-5` | adaptive | all | yes | no | yes |
| `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-6` | adaptive | all but `xhigh` | yes | no | yes |
| `claude-opus-4-5` | budget | `low`, `medium`, `high` | yes | no | no |
| Ids that start with `claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-1`, `claude-opus-4`, `claude-sonnet-4`, or `claude-3` | budget | none sent | yes | no | no |
| Any other id | adaptive | all | no | no | yes |

`caps` matches every id of the older list (the budget row with no effort values) with `model.starts_with(id)`, not with `is_model`. For example, `caps` treats `claude-sonnet-4-foo` as `claude-sonnet-4`. The ids `claude-opus-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-7`, and `claude-opus-4-8` match earlier, so this prefix rule does not change them. The list has the longest ids first, so `claude-sonnet-4-5` is not read as `claude-sonnet-4`.

The last row covers a model that is newer than this build. It gets the request surface that every current model accepts. For the 4.6 models, the provider sends `high` in place of `xhigh`. For `claude-opus-4-5`, any effort above `medium` becomes `high`. The 4.6 models stay on adaptive thinking because adaptive thinking interleaves with tool calls on both of them.

### Output limit

The body sets `max_tokens` to the smaller of `ChatRequest.max_tokens` and the output limit that models.dev lists for the model. If the catalog does not list the model, the body keeps the value that the caller asked for.

### Thinking and effort

- **Adaptive models.** The body sets `thinking` to `{"type":"adaptive","display":"summarized"}`. A forced tool call sends no thinking config. The effort goes in `output_config.effort`.
- **Budget models.** The body sets `thinking` to `{"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":N}`. The next part explains `N`.

### Tool choice

The body sends `tool_choice` only when the request has tools. `Auto` and `None` map to `auto` and `none`. `Any` and `Tool(name)` map to `any` and `tool` only when the model accepts forced calls. Otherwise the body sends `auto`. The provider body makes this downgrade (`anthropic.rs`, the `tool_choice` match).

The native agent loop always uses `ToolChoice::Auto` (`crates/ostra-exec-native/src/lib.rs`), so it has no downgrade to handle. Only `structured_cancellable` handles a forced call that came back as `auto`. It makes a second attempt after a reminder turn. [Structured decisions](#structured-decisions) explains that rule.

### Cache breakpoints and tools

Every cache breakpoint uses the 1-hour TTL (`cache_mark`). The turns of one execution can be more than 5 minutes apart, for example after a long build or a permission ask. Mixed TTLs need the longer entries first, so one TTL keeps the request valid.

The provider places breakpoints on these blocks:

- The last two system blocks that have `cache: true`. If no block has the flag, the last system block.
- The last client tool.
- The last `text` or `tool_result` block of the latest user message.

Server tools use the versions `web_search_20250305` and `web_fetch_20250910`. The newer 20260209 versions run inside code execution, and their failures cost one turn each. Client tools carry `eager_input_streaming: true`.

### Server-side fallbacks and the declined partial

When `refusal_fallback` is true and the model supports fallbacks, the body sets `fallbacks` to `default` and the request adds `FALLBACK_BETA`. If the provider falls back in the middle of an answer, the stream holds a `fallback` block. The function `strip_before_fallback` then removes thinking, tool use, and unpaired server tool use before the last marker. The caller never runs or echoes the declined partial answer.

## Beta headers and token reserves

The provider adds a beta name to `anthropic-beta` only when its condition holds.

| Constant | Value | Sent when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPACT_BETA` | `compact-2026-09-04` | The messages hold a signed Anthropic compaction block, and always on a compaction request. |
| `FALLBACK_BETA` | `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` | `refusal_fallback` is true and the model supports fallbacks. |
| `INTERLEAVED_BETA` | `interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14` | A budget model that can interleave gets a thinking budget and the request has client tools. |
| `WINDOW_BETA` | `model-context-window-exceeded-2025-08-26` | The model is older than Claude 4.5. |

`WINDOW_BETA` makes the API stop generation at the context window. Without it, a request with input plus `max_tokens` past the window fails validation. Claude 4.5 and later models do this without the beta.

## Thinking budget for budget models

The function `budget_tokens(effort, max_output)` in `crates/ostra-providers/src/anthropic.rs` returns a share of the model output limit:

| Effort | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| `Low` | none, so the body sends no thinking |
| `Medium` | output limit divided by 8 |
| `High` | output limit divided by 4 |
| `Xhigh` | output limit divided by 2 |
| `Max` | output limit minus `ANSWER_RESERVE` |

`budget_tokens` gives a share of the output limit for the lower efforts. At `Max`, it gives all of the limit except `ANSWER_RESERVE`, the room for the answer. The reason is that the chosen effort is what the user agreed to spend.

The provider then limits the budget to a room value. When the model interleaves and the request has client tools, the room has no limit, because the budget spans the whole turn. Otherwise the room is `max_tokens` minus `ANSWER_RESERVE`. If the result is below `MIN_BUDGET`, or the call is a forced tool call, the body sends no thinking.

- `ANSWER_RESERVE` is `16000` tokens. It keeps room for the answer under a thinking budget, because the budget must stay below `max_tokens` and an answer can be a whole file that a tool call writes.
- `MIN_BUDGET` is `1024` tokens. It is the smallest thinking budget that the API accepts.

For example, with a 64000-token output limit, `Max` gives a budget of 48000 tokens. `High` with `max_tokens` of 16000 gives no thinking. These cases are in the unit tests of `anthropic.rs`.

## OpenAI requests

The struct `OpenAi` in `crates/ostra-providers/src/openai.rs` posts to `{base_url}/v1/responses`. The default base URL is `https://api.openai.com`. The key always goes in `Authorization: Bearer`. The client has the same 20-second connect timeout and the same rule of no redirect.

### Request body

- `store` is `false`. The run is stateless, so Ostra sends the whole conversation each time.
- `max_output_tokens` is `ChatRequest.max_tokens`. The provider does not limit it to the catalog output limit.
- `instructions` holds the non-empty system blocks joined with a blank line. The `cache` flags have no effect, because the body has no cache markers.
- A model whose id starts with `gpt-5`, `gpt-6`, or `o` is a reasoning model. Its body sets `reasoning` to the effort and `summary: auto`, and sets `include` to `reasoning.encrypted_content`. Reasoning items return to the API in later turns through that encrypted content.
- Tools use the type `function`. Web search uses `{"type":"web_search"}`. When tools exist, `parallel_tool_calls` is `true`.
- `tool_choice` maps `Auto` to `auto`, `Any` to `required`, `None` to `none`, and `Tool(name)` to a function choice. OpenAI has no downgrade rule.

### Message conversion

User text becomes an `input_text` message. A `ToolUse` block becomes a `function_call` item. A `ToolResult` block becomes a `function_call_output` item. If the result is an error and its text does not start with `Error`, the provider adds the prefix `Error: `. Only `Opaque` blocks from provider `openai` with type `reasoning` go back as reasoning items.

## Streaming

Both providers read the response as server-sent events (SSE). The function `json_events` in `crates/ostra-providers/src/sse.rs` turns the byte stream into JSON values. It skips events with empty data and the `[DONE]` sentinel.

These rules apply to bad input:

- If an event holds invalid JSON, the stream yields `ProviderError::Decode` with the event name.
- If the transport fails, the stream yields `ProviderError::Network`. The message drops the URL.
- If the SSE framing is invalid, the stream yields `ProviderError::Decode`.

Each provider feeds the events to an `Accumulator`. The accumulator calls the `EventSink` for each delta and builds the final blocks. The call ends at `message_stop` for Anthropic and at `response.completed` or `response.incomplete` for OpenAI. If the stream ends earlier, the call returns `ProviderError::Network` with the text `stream ended before message_stop` or `stream ended before response.completed`.

### Block assembly

- Anthropic keeps one slot for each content block index. A `tool_use` block collects `input_json_delta` fragments. At `content_block_stop`, the accumulator parses the JSON.
- If a tool input does not parse, the block gets the single key `__invalid_json` (`INVALID_INPUT_KEY`) with the raw text. The agent loop answers such a call with an error result and does not run the tool. OpenAI uses the same key.
- Anthropic server tool blocks, unknown blocks, and fallback markers become `Opaque` blocks. A signed `compaction` block becomes a `Compaction` block.
- OpenAI stores each finished output item by `output_index`. A `web_search_call` adds 1 to the web search count and sends `ServerToolUsed`, but it makes no block.

### Stop reasons

| Provider value | `StopReason` |
| --- | --- |
| Anthropic `end_turn`, `stop_sequence` | `EndTurn` |
| Anthropic `tool_use` | `ToolUse` |
| Anthropic `max_tokens`, `model_context_window_exceeded` | `MaxTokens` |
| Anthropic `pause_turn` | `PauseTurn` |
| Anthropic `refusal` | `Refusal`, with `refusal_category` from `stop_details.category` |
| Any other Anthropic value | `Other(value)`, or `Other("unknown")` when none came |
| OpenAI `response.completed` with a refusal part | `Refusal` |
| OpenAI `response.completed` with a tool call | `ToolUse` |
| OpenAI `response.completed` otherwise | `EndTurn` |
| OpenAI `response.incomplete`, reason `max_output_tokens` | `MaxTokens` |
| OpenAI `response.incomplete`, reason `content_filter` | `Refusal` |

## Errors and retry

Without a retry, every short network fault or rate limit stops an execution. A blind retry after output starts sends the user duplicate text and runs a tool twice. The module `crates/ostra-providers/src/retry.rs` retries only when it is safe.

### Error types

`ProviderError` has these variants: `NoKey`, `UnknownProvider`, `BadModel`, `Auth`, `InvalidRequest`, `RateLimited`, `Overloaded`, `Server`, `Network`, `Stream`, `Decode`, and `Cancelled`. The method `is_retryable` is true for `RateLimited`, `Overloaded`, `Server`, and `Network`. The method `retry_after` returns the delay in seconds for `RateLimited`, `Overloaded`, and `Server`.

### Status mapping

The function `status_error` maps an HTTP failure in this order:

| Condition | Error |
| --- | --- |
| Status 401 or 403 | `Auth` |
| Status 429 | `RateLimited` |
| Status 529 | `Overloaded` |
| Body `error.type` is `overloaded_error` | `Overloaded` |
| Status 408, 409, or 500 to 599 | `Server` |
| Any other status | `InvalidRequest` |

The message comes from `error.message` in the body. If the body has none, the message is the first 300 characters of the body. The function reads the header `Retry-After` in seconds and rounds up. Stream error events map in the same way: Anthropic `overloaded_error`, `rate_limit_error`, and `api_error`, and OpenAI `rate_limit_exceeded`, `server_error`, `server_is_overloaded`, and `slow_down`. An OpenAI `response.failed` event becomes a `Server` error.

### Retry rules

The function `run` calls the attempt again when all three conditions hold: the error is retryable, no output started, and fewer than `max_retries` retries ran. The default `RetryPolicy` is `max_retries` of 4, `base_delay` of 1000 ms, and `max_delay` of 60 seconds. A call thus makes at most 5 attempts.

The wait before retry number `n` (starting at 0) is `min(base_delay * 2^n, max_delay)` multiplied by a jitter factor from 0.5 to about 1.0. If the error carries a `Retry-After` value, the wait is the larger of the jittered delay and that value. `max_delay` does not limit a `Retry-After` value.

Output starts when the accumulator sets the `started` flag. Anthropic sets it at the first `content_block_start`. OpenAI sets it at the first of these events: `response.output_item.added`, `response.output_text.delta`, or `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta`. The last event is a thinking delta. A retryable error after that point becomes `ProviderError::Stream` and is not retried. A failure before the first block, such as an error event at the start, is retried.

#### Retry decision

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Attempt fails with an error"] --> B{"Retryable?"}
  B -- no --> C["Return the error"]
  B -- yes --> D{"Output started?"}
  D -- yes --> E["Return Stream error"]
  D -- no --> F{"Fewer than 4 retries used?"}
  F -- no --> G["Return the error"]
  F -- yes --> H["Wait: backoff, jitter, Retry-After"]
  H --> I["Run the attempt again"]
  I --> A
```

The core of the rule in `run`:

```rust
Err(e)
    if e.is_retryable()
        && !started.load(Ordering::SeqCst)
        && n < policy.max_retries =>
{
    let wait = policy.delay(n, e.retry_after());
    ...
    n += 1;
}
Err(e) if e.is_retryable() && started.load(Ordering::SeqCst) => {
    return Err(ProviderError::Stream(e.to_string()));
}
```

### What happens when

- **The caller cancels.** The cancel token ends the attempt or the wait. The call returns `ProviderError::Cancelled` and never retries. The scripted provider also returns `Cancelled` when the token is already set.
- **The error is `Auth`, `InvalidRequest`, or `Decode`.** The call returns it at once. A retry cannot fix a bad key or a bad request.
- **The retries run out.** The call returns the last error.
- **`RetryPolicy::fast(n)`.** Tests use it. It sets a delay of 1 ms and a limit of 5 ms.

## Compaction and structured calls

[Native executor loop](native-executor.md) decides when to compact. This part explains what each provider does when it receives the call.

### Compaction

`Compacted` holds `messages` and `usage`. If `messages` is `None`, no summary came back and the conversation continues unchanged. `compact_on_client` is the fallback for providers or models that have no server-side form. It sends the same request with the instructions as the last user turn, so the cached prefix is reused, and it sets `tool_choice` to `None`. If the stop reason is `EndTurn` and the text is not blank, the text becomes one `Compaction` block. The provider does not use a cut-off summary.

- **Anthropic with on-demand compaction.** The body adds `compaction: {type: summarize, instructions}`. The result must hold a signed compaction block and the stop value `compaction`. A model that returns `InvalidRequest` falls back to `compact_on_client`. The top-level usage of such a request is zero, so the provider sums the entries of `usage.iterations` with type `compaction`.
- **OpenAI.** The provider posts `model`, `input`, and `instructions` to `/v1/responses/compact`. The posted `instructions` field holds the system blocks that `request_body` joins. This form takes no compaction instructions, so the provider ignores the `instructions` argument for this call. The encrypted compaction item goes back verbatim on later turns. If the gateway rejects the endpoint with `InvalidRequest`, the provider uses `compact_on_client`, and that path does use the `instructions` argument.

### Structured decisions

The functions `structured` and `structured_cancellable` return one structured answer for the judge calls. They force the model to call a tool named `decide` (`DECIDE_TOOL`) with the given schema. The request uses `max_tokens` of 16000 and caches the system block and the tool.

The call allows two attempts, because a model that rejects forced calls gets `auto` from the provider body. If the first answer has no `decide` call, the function adds the assistant turn and a user turn that tells the model to call the tool now. A `Refusal` stop returns `ProviderError::Decode` with the category. If the second answer has no `decide` call, the function returns `ProviderError::Decode` with the text `the model did not call the \`decide\` tool`. The returned `Usage` is the sum of all attempts. [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md) explains who calls this function.

## Scripted provider for tests

The struct `ScriptedProvider` in `crates/ostra-providers/src/mock.rs` replaces a real API in tests. It does not mock the network. It answers from a queue.

- The queue returns responses in order. `push`, `push_error`, `push_text`, `push_tool_use`, and `push_tool_uses` add to it.
- `with_responder(f)` answers every request with `f` after the queue is empty. Use it when executions run in parallel and the order is not fixed.
- If the queue is empty and no responder exists, `chat` returns `ProviderError::Decode` with the text `the scripted provider has no response left`.
- `requests()` returns every request that the provider received. `remaining()` returns the queue length.
- `chat` replays each text, thinking, and tool-use block of the answer as stream events. It sends each tool input as one `ToolInputDelta`.
- `tool_id()` returns the ids `toolu_mock_1`, `toolu_mock_2`, and so on.
- The helper `response(content, stop)` makes a response with zero usage and the model `mock`.

The default name is `mock`. Register it with `Providers::register("mock", ...)`, and then `for_model("mock:any")` works. The scripted provider does no retry. [Testing and evals](testing.md) explains how the tests use it.

## Price catalog from models.dev

Providers report tokens only. The catalog supplies the price of each token class, the context window, and the output limit of each model. The catalog is the document at `https://models.dev/api.json` (`MODELS_DEV_URL`).

### Parse

`Catalog::from_models_dev` reads the document as providers that hold models. For each model it reads `cost` (`input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, and the list of context-size price steps) and `limit` (`context`, `output`). Prices are USD per million tokens.

- A model without an input price and an output price is left out.
- A window or output limit of 0 is left out.
- A missing `cache_read` defaults to the input price.
- A missing `cache_write` defaults to the input price times 1.25.
- `cache_write_1h` is the input price times 2 for provider `anthropic`. For other providers it equals `cache_write`. The reason is that models.dev lists only the 5-minute write, and only Anthropic prices 1-hour writes.
- A price tier counts only when its bound has the type `context`. The parser sorts the price tier list by size, smallest first.

### Look up a model

The functions `Catalog::price`, `context_window`, and `max_output` use one lookup. The input is a model id with or without a `provider:` prefix.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  S["Model id, with or without a provider prefix"] --> E1{"Exact id in the prefix provider or a first-party provider?"}
  E1 -- yes --> R1["Use that entry"]
  E1 -- no --> P1{"A first-party id is a prefix of the model id, followed by a hyphen?"}
  P1 -- yes --> R2["Use the longest such id"]
  P1 -- no --> X1{"Exact id in any provider, in name order?"}
  X1 -- yes --> R3["Use the first match"]
  X1 -- no --> N["No entry: the cost is 0"]
```

The first-party list `FIRST_PARTY` is `anthropic`, `openai`, `xai`, `google`, `mistral`, and `deepseek`. A first-party listing wins when a reseller lists the same id at another price. The prefix rule lets a dated snapshot such as `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` use the price of `claude-haiku-4-5`. The longest match wins, so `claude-opus-5-5-x` is not priced as `claude-opus-5`. The hyphen rule keeps `claude-opus-50` from matching `claude-opus-5`.

### Install and read

The catalog is a process-wide value (`CATALOG`). `install(catalog)` replaces it. The functions `price`, `context_window`, and `max_output` read it. Until the server installs a catalog, every cost is 0. The native loop reads `context_window` and `max_output` too. [Native executor loop](native-executor.md) explains the defaults that it uses when a model has no entry.

## Refresh and cache the catalog

The module `crates/ostra-server/src/prices.rs` keeps the catalog fresh. Without it, a restart without network prices every execution at 0.

`prices::start(data_dir)` runs once when the server starts, and it does these steps:

1. Read `models-dev.json` in the data directory. If it parses, install it at once.
2. Read the URL from `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` (`URL_ENV`). If the variable is unset, use `MODELS_DEV_URL`. If it is set to an empty value, stop. No fetch runs.
3. Start a background loop. If the cache file is younger than 24 hours (`REFRESH_EVERY`), the loop sleeps for the rest of the 24 hours. Otherwise it fetches.
4. After a good fetch, the loop sleeps 24 hours. After a failed fetch, it writes a warning, keeps the cached prices, and sleeps 1 hour (`RETRY_AFTER`).

A fetch has a timeout of 60 seconds and must return a success status. The function `refresh` parses the body and refuses a catalog that lists no priced model. It writes the text to `models-dev.json.tmp` and renames it to `models-dev.json`, and then installs the catalog. A bad download never replaces a good cache, because the write happens only after the parse and the empty check pass.

### What happens when

- **The machine has no network and a cache exists.** The cached prices stay in use.
- **The machine has no network and no cache.** Every cost is 0 and the catalog has no limits. Anthropic then keeps the `max_tokens` that the caller asked for.
- **The fetch returns `{}`.** The refresh fails with `the catalog lists no priced models`, and the old file stays.
- **A model is not in the catalog.** Its cost is 0. The Cost screen shows 0 for its executions.

### For the user

The data directory and the other environment variables of the process are in [Configuration reference](reference-configuration.md).

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | Shows the state | How to change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` | unset, so `https://models.dev/api.json` | The environment of the `ostra` process | After a restart, because `prices::start` reads it once | The log lines `model prices refreshed from <url>` and `fetching model prices from <url> failed`, the file `models-dev.json` in the data directory, and the amounts on the Cost screen | Set another URL for a mirror. Set an empty value to turn fetching off. |

Tests and the browser tests set `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` to an empty value so that they never reach the network.

## Cost formula

The function `cost(model, usage, web_searches)` in `crates/ostra-core/src/pricing.rs` turns one response into dollars. Each provider calls it when a response ends, with the model that produced the response. After a server-side fallback this model is the fallback model, so the cost uses the right price. The harness transcript reader calls the same function. [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) explains where it reads usage.

### Usage fields

The field `input_tokens` of `Usage` excludes cache reads and cache writes. Each provider normalizes its usage to this form. Anthropic reports `input_tokens` in this form already. OpenAI reports input tokens that include cached and written tokens, so the provider subtracts both.

| `Usage` field | Anthropic source | OpenAI source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `input_tokens` | `input_tokens` | `input_tokens` minus cached minus written |
| `output_tokens` | `output_tokens` | `output_tokens` |
| `cache_read_tokens` | `cache_read_input_tokens` | `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` |
| `cache_write_tokens` | `cache_creation_input_tokens` | `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` |
| `cache_write_1h_tokens` | `cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` | none |
| Web searches | `server_tool_use.web_search_requests` | count of `web_search_call` items |

### Steps

1. Look up the price of the model. If none exists, return 0.
2. Count the prompt tokens: `input_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens`.
3. Pick the rates. A price tier replaces the base rates when the prompt has more tokens than the tier size. The largest matching tier wins. A prompt of exactly the tier size still uses the lower rates.
4. Split the cache writes. `write_1h` is the smaller of `cache_write_1h_tokens` and `cache_write_tokens`. The rest are 5-minute writes.
5. Add each class: tokens times rate divided by 1,000,000.
6. Add `WEB_SEARCH_USD` of `0.01` for each web search. The value is the same on both providers.

```rust
pub fn cost(model: &str, usage: &Usage, web_searches: u64) -> f64 {
    let Some(p) = price(model) else { return 0.0 };
    let r = p.rates(usage.input_tokens + usage.cache_read_tokens + usage.cache_write_tokens);
    let write_1h = usage.cache_write_1h_tokens.min(usage.cache_write_tokens);
    usage.input_tokens as f64 * r.input / m
        + usage.output_tokens as f64 * r.output / m
        + usage.cache_read_tokens as f64 * r.cache_read / m
        + (usage.cache_write_tokens - write_1h) as f64 * r.cache_write / m
        + write_1h as f64 * r.cache_write_1h / m
        + web_searches as f64 * WEB_SEARCH_USD
}
```

In the excerpt, `m` is `1_000_000.0`. In the test sample catalog, 1 million input, 1 million output, and 1 million cache-read tokens of `claude-sonnet-5-5` plus 1 search cost 2 + 10 + 0.2 + 0.01 dollars. The same catalog prices 3 million cache-write tokens of `claude-opus-5`, of which 1 million use the 1-hour TTL, at 2 × 6.25 + 10 dollars.

The provider stores the result in `Usage.cost_usd`. A compaction call adds its own usage and cost to the response. The OpenAI `compact` call prices its usage with the requested model and 0 searches.

## Cost screen data

The Cost screen shows the spend that the executions saved. Each execution row in the workspace database holds `usage` (JSON) and `cost_usd`. [Storage: databases and lesson memory](storage.md) owns the schema.

The route `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/cost` returns a `CostReport`. The query value `since` limits the report to executions that started at or after that time.

- `since` must be an RFC 3339 time, such as `2026-09-24T00:00:00Z`. A blank value means all time. Any other text returns a 400 error that names the value.
- `WorkspaceDb::cost_report` (in `crates/ostra-store/src/workspace.rs`) reads every matching execution and sums its `Usage` with `Usage::add`.
- The report has four lists, `by_session`, `by_stage`, `by_agent`, and `by_executor`, and one `total` row with the key `total`.
- An execution without a session counts under the key `side-panel`. An execution without a stage counts under the key `none`.
- Each `CostRow` holds `key`, `executions` (the count), `usage`, and `cache_reads_per_tool_call`. The last field is `cache_read_tokens` divided by `tool_calls`, or 0 when there are no tool calls.
- Each list sorts by `cost_usd` from high to low, then by key.

`Usage::add` sums every field except `context_tokens`. That field takes the latest value that is above 0. [Workspace, settings, and setup screens](web-workspace-and-setup.md) explains the screen. It offers the ranges "This week" and "All time". The week starts at `WorkspaceActivity.week_since`, so its totals match the status bar. [REST and WebSocket API](server-api.md) explains the spend windows of the status bar.

## Limits and constants

| Name | Value | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic::DEFAULT_BASE_URL` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | The Anthropic base URL when none is set. |
| `openai::DEFAULT_BASE_URL` | `https://api.openai.com` | The OpenAI base URL when none is set. |
| `API_VERSION` | `2023-06-01` | The header `anthropic-version`. |
| `COMPACT_BETA`, `FALLBACK_BETA`, `INTERLEAVED_BETA`, `WINDOW_BETA` | See the beta table | The `anthropic-beta` names. |
| `ANSWER_RESERVE` | `16000` tokens | The room for the answer under a thinking budget. |
| `MIN_BUDGET` | `1024` tokens | The smallest thinking budget. |
| `INVALID_INPUT_KEY` | `__invalid_json` | The key of a tool input whose JSON did not parse. |
| `DECIDE_TOOL` | `decide` | The forced tool of structured calls. |
| `ChatRequest::new` `max_tokens` | `32000` | The default output request. |
| Structured call `max_tokens` | `16000` | The output limit of a judge call. |
| Connect timeout of both clients | 20 seconds | The wait for a connection. |
| `RetryPolicy::default` | 4 retries, 1000 ms base, 60 s cap | The retry schedule. |
| `MODELS_DEV_URL` | `https://models.dev/api.json` | The default catalog URL. |
| `WEB_SEARCH_USD` | `0.01` | The price of one web search. |
| `FIRST_PARTY` | `anthropic`, `openai`, `xai`, `google`, `mistral`, `deepseek` | The providers whose listing wins. |
| `REFRESH_EVERY` | 24 hours | The age at which the cache file is stale. |
| `RETRY_AFTER` of `prices.rs` | 1 hour | The wait after a failed fetch. |
| Catalog fetch timeout | 60 seconds | The limit of one download. |
| `URL_ENV` | `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` | The variable that overrides the URL. |
