sections.title: Session, execution, and gate screens
sections.summary: How the session board, the gate cards, the execution screen, and the artifact screen show a session, which checks run in the browser, how terminal output is made safe, and how the mobile screens differ.
sections.body:
A session runs many stages, and some stages wait for a person. Without a screen for each part, you cannot see which stage runs, which question waits for you, or what an agent does. This page covers four screens and their mobile versions: the session board, the gate cards on the board, the execution screen, and the artifact screen. The page stops before the project and workspace screens.

Each screen opens as a console tab with a resource ID: `session:<id>`, `exec:<id>`, or `artifact:<path>`. The shell, the API client, and the socket belong to [Web console shell](web-console.md). The rules of the pipeline belong to [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md). This page describes what the screens show and what they send.

## Session board layout

`SessionScreen` in [`web/src/screens/SessionScreen.tsx`](web/src/screens/SessionScreen.tsx) renders the board for the resource `session:<id>`. The board has one header, some banners, a lane stepper, and two tabs. A session has "ended" when its status is `completed` or `failed`.

These parts appear from top to bottom:

1. The header (`SessionHeader`): the title or "Untitled", the original request, the context that you added later, chips, and the controls.
2. The banner "The session is paused", when the status is `paused`.
3. The banner "YOLO is on", when YOLO is on and the session has not ended.
4. One `BlockerNotice` for each active security block.
5. The lane stepper (`LaneStepper`) with one entry for each lane.
6. The tabs Overview and Decisions. The count on Overview is the number of open gates. The count on Decisions is the number of decisions.

The Overview tab holds these parts in this order:

1. "Waiting for you": one gate card for each open gate.
2. The "Completion report" panel and the "Decided for you" panel.
3. The context composer.
4. The lane panel for the selected lane.
5. The phase graph.
6. The toggle "Show answered gates (N)".
7. The toggle "Show event log (N)".

The Decisions tab holds the decisions panel.

### What decides which part shows

- **Context composer:** the session is not ended and `kind.kind` is `pipeline`. An init session has no composer.
- **Phase graph:** the plan has at least 1 phase and the selected lane is one of `PHASE_LANES`: design, build, review, or test.
- **"Waiting for you":** at least 1 gate is open.
- **Answered gates:** hidden until you press the toggle. A `#gate-<id>` link opens them when that gate has an answer.
- **Decided for you:** the completion report has a heading "Decided for you" (level 1 to 3). `splitDecidedForYou` cuts that section from the report and shows it in its own panel with a warning tone.

The header chips show the category (for an init session, `Init <project>`), the status, the lane title with the stage label, one chip for each project, the cost, and the start time. `startedLabel` shows the time for today and the date with the time for an earlier day.

### What happens when

- **The session does not load:** the board shows the banner "Ostra could not load this session" with a "Try again" button. The banner shows only when no data exists. If a later reload fails, the board keeps the data that it has.
- **A `#gate-<id>` hash is in the URL:** the board switches to the Overview tab, opens the answered gates if that gate has an answer, and scrolls to the gate. It does this only when the hash changes, not on each live refresh.
- **A gate is answered:** the board replaces that gate in its data and reloads the session and the events.

## Live data on the session board

The board shows a REST snapshot and then adds live events. This keeps the page current without a reload. The sequence is:

1. `api.session(id)` loads the detail and `api.events(id)` loads the stored events.
2. The board subscribes to the channel `session:<id>` on the socket.
3. A `session_event` message adds the event to a list of live events and starts a reload of the detail. `useThrottled` limits that reload to one call each 400 ms.
4. A `session_updated` message replaces the summary in the detail at once.
5. When the events snapshot loads again, the board clears the live list, because the new snapshot contains those events.

`mergeEvents` joins the snapshot and the live events. It keeps one event for each sequence number and sorts the result by sequence number. Because of this, a snapshot and a live message that overlap never show an event twice. The same code runs on the mobile board.

The event log is a text block with one line for each event. `eventLine` writes the time as `HH:MM:SS`, then the event type with each `_` changed to `.` and padded to 20 characters, then the text from `describeEvent`. The log is hidden until you press "Show event log".

## Lanes and lane states

A lane groups the stages of one phase of work. The board shows nine lanes in the order of `LANE_ORDER`: research, requirements, verification, design, build, review, test, docs, and done. The constant `LANES` in [`web/src/content/stages.ts`](web/src/content/stages.ts) gives each lane a `title` and a `why` text. The lane panel shows the `why` text above the stages.

| Lane | What its `why` text says |
| --- | --- |
| Research | A research pass reads the code and the current documentation before anyone writes code. |
| Requirements | One spec states what the change must do, as testable requirements with acceptance criteria. |
| Verification | Fact-check verifies each concrete claim in the spec or plan before you approve it. |
| Design | The plan turns the spec into phases and waits for your approval before any code. |
| Build | An agent implements each phase and runs the project's build command. One phase runs at a time for each project. |
| Review | The reviewer checks each change against the project rules and the phase requirements. The loop repeats until the findings are fixed. |
| Test | When you ask for tests, Ostra maps what the change touches, writes tests, and runs the existing tests again. |
| Docs | When you ask for it, Ostra rewrites the workspace book for each project. |
| Done | The completion report names each stage that did not run. Under YOLO it lists each decision that Ostra made. |

### How a lane gets its state

`laneStates(d)` in [`web/src/screens/session/board.ts`](web/src/screens/session/board.ts) returns a status and a detail line for each lane. It reads only the stage cards of that lane. The status values are `pending`, `current`, `waiting`, `done`, `failed`, and `skipped`.

```ts
const waiting = find("waiting");
const running = find("running");
const failed = find("failed", "blocked");
const done = items.filter((s) => s.status === "done" || s.status === "skipped");
if (waiting) out[lane] = { status: "waiting", detail: "Waiting for you", why };
else if (running) out[lane] = { status: "current", detail: running.detail ?? running.label, why };
else if (failed) out[lane] = { status: "failed", detail: failed.detail ?? humanize(failed.status), why };
else if (done.length === items.length) { /* done, or skipped when every stage was skipped */ }
else if (done.length > 0)
  out[lane] = { status: "current", detail: `${done.length} of ${items.length} done`, why };
else out[lane] = { status: "pending", why };
```

The function checks these cases in this order:

1. The lane has no stage cards. The lane is `skipped` if the session is `completed` or if a later lane has a stage that is not `pending`. Otherwise it is `pending`.
2. A stage is `waiting`. The lane is `waiting` with the detail "Waiting for you".
3. A stage is `running`. The lane is `current` with the detail of that stage, or its label.
4. A stage is `failed` or `blocked`. The lane is `failed` with the detail of that stage, or the humanized status.
5. Every stage is `done` or `skipped`. The lane is `done` with the detail of the last finished stage, or a count such as "2 stages". If every stage is `skipped`, the lane is `skipped` with the detail "Skipped".
6. Some stages are finished. The lane is `current` with the detail "N of M done".
7. No stage has started. The lane is `pending`.

Because the checks run in this order, a waiting stage wins over a running stage, and a running stage wins over a failed stage.

### Which lane opens first

`defaultLane` picks the lane that the lane panel shows when the board opens:

1. The lane of the stage that holds the current gate.
2. The first lane in `LANE_ORDER` with the status `waiting`.
3. The first lane in `LANE_ORDER` with the status `current`.
4. The lane that the session summary names in `summary.lane`.

The current gate is the first open `permission` gate. If no permission gate is open, it is the open gate with the oldest `opened_at`. The function `currentGate` in [`web/src/lib/events.ts`](web/src/lib/events.ts) gives the permission gate priority over the other gates.

## Stages in a lane

The lane panel (`LanePanel`) lists the stages of the selected lane. Each row shows the stage label, a status, and a meta text on the right. A click on a row opens a detail box. A second click closes it.

The detail box shows:

- The stage label and a status chip.
- "Produces": what the stage creates. This text comes from `STAGES[stage].produces`.
- "Protects against": the failure that the stage prevents. This text comes from `STAGES[stage].protects`.
- The detail text of the stage, if it has one.
- One button for each execution of the stage, labeled with the agent name and the run label. The icon shows whether the run has an activity stream or a terminal. A click opens `exec:<id>`.
- A "Go to the gate" button, if the stage has a gate. It scrolls the board to that gate.

The constant `STAGES` has 38 entries, one for each `StageKind`. Each entry has the fields `label`, `produces`, and `protects`. The planner defines the stage kinds. The page [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) explains them. `STAGES` only gives them display text.

The meta text on a row comes from `stageMeta`. If the stage is `running` and one of its executions is `running` with a summary, the text is that summary. Otherwise the text is the stage detail, then a separator ` · `, then the project key. The project key is left out when the stage label already contains it. A row key is `stage:project:phase:index`, so two stages of the same kind in different projects stay separate.

If the selected lane has no stage, the panel shows: "No stage in this lane has started. It runs when the pipeline reaches it, or the completion report says why it was skipped."

## Phase graph, decisions, completion report, and event log

The phase graph shows the plan phases in columns. `phaseNodes` builds the columns with `phaseLayers`. Column 0 holds phases with no dependencies. Each later column depends only on columns to its left. A phase whose `depends_on` is `null` depends on each phase with a lower ID. A dependency on a phase that is not in the plan counts as depth 0. A dependency cycle also stops at depth 0, so the graph always draws.

A click on a phase opens its phase file as an artifact in a preview console tab. The panel text repeats the rule of the pipeline: a phase starts after each phase that it depends on passes review, phases of one project run one at a time, and phases of different projects run in parallel. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) owns that rule.

The Decisions tab lists each judge decision as "Ostra chose X because Y". `decisionChoice` writes X from the judge output. It has a case for each of the 10 judge names: `classify`, `sufficiency`, `stakes`, `track`, `feedback`, `route_answer`, `rescue`, `resolve_review`, `yolo_answer`, and `completion`. The judges, their schemas, and the override rules belong to [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md).

The screen adds these controls to each decision:

- An override button, only when the server sets `can_override` to true. The dialog subtitle says that work that depends on the decision has not started.
- The override dialog. It shows the decision output as JSON in a text field and asks for a reason.
- Two checks before the save. The text must parse as JSON, or the dialog shows "Write the decision as valid JSON, in the same shape as the judge's output." The reason must not be empty, or the dialog shows "Say why, so the record explains the change."
- The call `api.overrideDecision(id, { output, reason })`. A server error shows in the dialog.

## Header controls: YOLO, pause, and stop

The header has three controls. Each calls the server and replaces the session summary with the reply. Pause, Continue, and Stop also call `onChanged`, and the board then reloads the detail and the events. The YOLO switch does not call `onChanged`, so it does not start that reload.

- **YOLO switch:** calls `api.setYolo(id, enabled)`. The switch tooltip says that Ostra answers each gate and permission ask itself from the next gate or tool call. The switch is disabled when the session has ended. The banner "YOLO is on" lists what still applies: guards, deny rules, the fact-check PASS requirement, the session budget, and security blocks.
- **Pause and Continue:** the button calls `api.pauseSession(id)` or `api.resumeSession(id)`. After a pause, no agent runs and nothing new starts. Each paused agent continues where it stopped. You can still answer gates and add context during a pause.
- **Stop:** the button opens a dialog. Ostra cancels each running execution, denies each waiting permission ask, and marks the session failed. Files that the agents already wrote stay in the project. The dialog calls `api.stopSession(id)`.

The rules behind these controls belong to other pages. [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md) explains pause, resume, and stop. [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md) explains YOLO answers. If a call fails, the header shows the server message under the controls.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| YOLO switch | Set when the session starts, by `options.yolo` | The session event log, event `yolo_set` | From the next gate or tool call | The YOLO chip, the banner "YOLO is on", and the event log | Turn the switch off |
| Pause | Not paused | The session event log, events `session_paused` and `session_resumed` | When the server replies | The banner "The session is paused" and the status chip | Press Continue |
| Stop | Not applicable | The session event log, event `session_failed` | When the server replies | The status chip `failed` | The screen has no control to undo a stop |

The workspace setting `yolo.default` belongs to [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md).

## Context composer

The context composer lets you add text, tagged files, and uploads to a session that runs. Without it, you must stop the session to give the agents a new fact. `ContextComposer` in [`web/src/screens/session/ContextComposer.tsx`](web/src/screens/session/ContextComposer.tsx) sends the context with `api.amend(sessionId, { text, files, uploads, delivery })`.

`delivery` has two values:

- **`queue`:** the button "Queue for the next step". The context reaches the agents at the next step, and running agents finish first. A requirement change goes through research, then Ostra rewrites the spec and you approve it again.
- **`now`:** the button "Send now". Ostra stops the running executions. Each one starts again from the beginning with your context. The progress of that run is lost. Files that the run already wrote stay in the project, and the cost stays on the bill.

The composer checks and then sends:

1. If the text, the tagged files, and the uploads are all empty, the composer shows "Write the context first, tag a file with @, or upload one."
2. For `now`, a confirm dialog "Interrupt running work?" shows the number of running executions. The buttons are "Keep them running" and "Interrupt and send".
3. On success, the composer clears the text and the uploads, and the board takes the new summary.
4. On failure, the composer shows the server message and keeps your text.

The composer disables "Send now" when it is busy, when an upload is still running, when the context is empty, or when no execution runs. In the last case the tooltip says: "Nothing is running, so queued context is used right away." The key `Mod+Enter` queues the context. `Mod` is Cmd on a Mac and Ctrl on other systems. The key `Enter` alone inserts a line break.

After you send, the header lists the context under "Context you added". Each entry shows "Queued" or "Sent now", the time, the text with file chips, and upload chips. [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md) explains how the engine delivers queued context to agents.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Queue for the next step (`delivery: queue`) | The action of `Mod+Enter` | The session event log, event `request_amended` | At the next step | The line "Queued" with the time in the header | Write the context before you send. The screen has no control to remove sent context |
| Send now (`delivery: now`) | Not applied | The same event | At once, after you confirm | The line "Sent now" with the time in the header | Press "Keep them running" in the confirm dialog |

## File tags and uploads in the composer

The composer uses `FileTagInput` in [`web/src/features/context/FileTagInput.tsx`](web/src/features/context/FileTagInput.tsx). It is an editable block, not a `textarea`, because a `textarea` cannot hold file chips inside the text. The value that the component reports keeps each tag as `@project/path`.

### How tagging works

1. You type `@` at the start of the text or after a space. The component loads the file list the first time you do this.
2. The list holds each file of the session projects, the folders that contain them, and the visible artifacts of the workspace. Artifact tags use the root `_artifacts` (the constant `ARTIFACTS_ROOT`), because no project key can take that name.
3. Ostra never offers hidden artifacts, because agents never see them.
4. If the list request for a project fails, that project adds no file. The composer shows no error.
5. `rankFiles` in [`web/src/features/context/tags.ts`](web/src/features/context/tags.ts) ranks the matches. A name that starts with the query scores best, then a name that contains it, then a path that contains it. The list shows at most 8 matches. The search stops when more than 5,000 matching files have been scored (`scored.length > 5000`). The limit counts matches, not the files that the search examines. An empty query shows the first 8 files.
6. `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` move in the list. `Enter` or `Tab` picks the match. `Escape` closes the list.
7. A pick replaces the query with a chip and a space. A folder chip ends with `/`.

The list opens under the caret. If less than 300 px remain below the caret, it opens above. The left edge stays at least 8 px from the window edge and at most 528 px from the right edge.

`splitTags` finds tags in text with the pattern `(^|\s)@([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)\/(\S+)`. A tag counts only when its project is in the list of allowed projects. If a path is not a known file, the parser removes trailing punctuation from the path and tries again. A sentence such as "See @backend/src/a.ts." tags the file without the final dot.

### Drag, paste, and upload

- **Drag from the Files panel:** a row carries the drag type `application/x-ostra-context` (the constant `CONTEXT_DRAG_TYPE`). A drop on the composer inserts a chip at the drop point. The composer ignores a file from a project that is not in the allowed list.
- **Drop or paste a file:** when uploads are on, the composer stages each file with `api.uploadFile(ws, file)` when you choose it. The chip shows a spinner until the server returns an ID. A failed upload shows its error on the chip.
- **Paste text:** the composer inserts plain text only.
- **Upload button:** "Upload a file" opens the file picker and accepts many files.

Only uploads with an ID and no error go with the request. When any upload runs, both send buttons stay disabled. The hint under the field says that you must describe each file in a few words, because the agents use your note to decide how to read it. [Workspace artifacts and uploads](artifacts-and-uploads.md) owns the size and count caps and the rules for how a session claims an upload.

The constant `ZWSP` is a zero-width space. The editor adds it after a trailing line break so that the break stays visible. The serializer removes it, so it never reaches the value.

In the header and the mobile board, `TaggedText` draws each known tag as a chip. A click on a file chip opens the file in a preview console tab. A click on a folder chip opens the Files tab for that project. `UntaggedFiles` shows attached files that the text does not mention.

## Gate cards

A gate is a question that stops the pipeline until you or YOLO answer it. `GateCard` in [`web/src/features/gates/GateCard.tsx`](web/src/features/gates/GateCard.tsx) shows one gate. When the gate is open, the card shows the answer form for its kind. When the gate has an answer, the card shows the recorded answer. The wrapper has the anchor `#gate-<id>`.

The rules for when each gate opens belong to [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md). This section describes how the card behaves.

- **Open card:** the form calls `api.answerGate(gate.id, { answer })`. When the call runs, the buttons are disabled and the card is dimmed. On success, the board replaces the gate. On failure, the card shows the message under the form.
- **Answered card:** the card shows the title and a one-line summary from `answerSummary`. If YOLO answered, the card says so. If the engine closed the gate, the summary starts with "Closed by Ostra:". The card also shows the reason of the answer, if the gate has one.
- **Unknown kind:** a kind with no form shows only its title and explanation.
- **Order on the board:** `openGatesInOrder` puts the current gate first, then the other open gates with the oldest first. `answeredGates` lists answered gates with the newest answer first.

## Gate kinds and answer kinds

Each gate payload has a `kind`. Each kind accepts one answer kind. The constant `ANSWER_KIND` in [`web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts`](web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts) holds this map. It mirrors `validate_answer` in the engine (`crates/ostra-engine/src/runner.rs`). If an answer has the wrong kind, the engine returns "That answer does not fit this gate."

| Gate kind | Answer kind | Form | Buttons |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | `questions` | `QuestionsGate` | Send the answers |
| `spec_approval`, `plan_approval` | `approval` | `ApprovalGate` | Approve the spec or plan, Request changes |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `choice` | `ChoiceGate` | Run another fact-check round, Stop the session |
| `review_cap` | `choice` | `ChoiceGate` | Run another fix and review pass, Stop and block the phase |
| `stuck` | `choice` | `ChoiceGate` | Re-run with this fact, Block this work |
| `phase_blocked` | `choice` | `ChoiceGate` | Retry the phase, Leave the phase blocked |
| `harness_failure` | `choice` | `ChoiceGate` | Retry after login, Run on the native executor |
| `execution_failed` | `choice` | `ChoiceGate` | Retry the execution, Abandon this work |
| `budget_reached` | `choice` | `ChoiceGate` | Raise the budget, Stop the session |
| `implementation_review` | `choice` | `ChoiceGate` | Accept the implementation, Send feedback |
| `closing_gate` | `closing` | `ClosingGate` | Confirm the closing choices |
| `permission` | `permission` | `PermissionGate` | Allow once, Always in this workspace, Deny |
| `skill_approval` | `skills` | `SkillsGate` | Approve the skills |

The constant `CHOICES` lists the options of the eight choice gates. Each option has an `option` string that the engine matches, a button label, a variant, and a rule for the text field. The rule is `none` (the option never sends text), `optional` (it sends the text when filled in), or `required`. Each gate has exactly one primary button.

| Gate kind | Option value | Text field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `another-round`, `stop` | Optional text for the agent with the findings |
| `review_cap` | `another-pass`, `stop` | Optional instruction for the fix pass |
| `stuck` | `fact`, `block` | Required for `fact`: the missing fact, quoted to the agent verbatim |
| `phase_blocked` | `retry`, `leave` | Optional instructions for the retry |
| `harness_failure` | `retry`, `native` | None |
| `execution_failed` | `retry`, `abandon` | None |
| `budget_reached` | `raise`, `stop` | Optional amount in US dollars |
| `implementation_review` | `done`, `feedback` | Required for `feedback`: what to change |

### What each form shows

- **Open questions:** one group for each question. The group shows the ID, the tag, the question, and the options in order, with the recommended option first and a "Recommended" chip. An "Other" option opens a text field. A question with `multi_select` uses check boxes. Other questions use radio buttons. A link opens the spec or plan.
- **Approval:** a "Fact-check PASS" chip, a link to read the spec or plan, and the summary. A plan approval also shows a table of phases with the project, the complexity, the test policy, and the dependencies. A `null` dependency list shows "Unclear, runs after earlier phases". The gate opens only after a fact-check PASS. Findings of severity LOW show above the buttons, and they do not block approval. A note says what approval starts. For a spec, Ostra judges the stakes and, unless they are low, plans the phases. For a plan, implementation starts phase by phase in dependency order.
- **Fact-check recurring:** a text that says the same findings came back after N passes. The findings table follows. Stopping ends the session.
- **Review cap:** a text that says a fourth pass runs only if you choose it. Stopping blocks this phase and each phase that depends on it, and independent phases continue. The card shows the review findings and a link to the review ledger.
- **Stuck:** chips for the agent, the project, and the phase, a link to the execution, the diagnostic, and the fact that the agent needs.
- **Phase blocked:** the phase, the project, and the reason.
- **Harness failure:** the harness name, a link to the terminal, and the error. A retry uses the same harness, so log in first. The native executor runs the agent on Ostra's own loop for the rest of the session.
- **Execution failed:** chips, a link to the execution, and the error.
- **Budget reached:** the amount spent and the budget. A note says that YOLO never answers this gate, because spending more is your decision.
- **Implementation review:** the review round, the blocked items, and links to the session context and the reports. Accepting moves on to formatting, tests, documentation, and the completion report.
- **Closing gate:** one box for each project with the phase count. The box has a check box "Write tests for these phases" when the project asks for tests and "Write the documentation book" when it asks for documentation. If neither applies, the box says that your request already decided both. The default is both unchecked, and the note calls this the recommended default. The completion report says how to run either stage later. The code cites Rule D8 and T3 for this gate.
- **Permission:** the agent, the tool, a link to the execution, the tool input (a shell line for `Bash`, JSON for other tools), the reason, and the rule as `layer rule`. The execution is paused until you answer. A denial tells the agent to continue without the call.
- **Skill approval:** a table of skills with the kind, the description, the exemplar files, and a select with the four values of `DISPOSITIONS`: `generate`, `regenerate`, `reuse`, and `drop`. The defaults come from the proposal. The button area shows "N of M kept for <project>". Nothing is written until you approve. [Project init and skills](init-and-skills.md) owns the skill flow.

The permission labels are in `PERMISSION_LABELS`: `allow-once` is "Allow once", `always-in-workspace` is "Always in this workspace", and `deny` is "Deny". The button "Always in this workspace" is disabled when the payload has no `suggestion`. When it has one, the button adds that rule to the workspace allow rules and shows it as code. The engine computes the suggestion with `suggest_rule`. It returns no suggestion for a tool that changes Ostra itself, under Rule O1: no allow rule stands in for your answer. [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) owns the permission rules.

## Checks before an answer leaves the browser

The builders in `gateAnswers.ts` check an answer before the card sends it. The engine checks it again, because the engine does not trust the browser. If a check fails, the card shows the message under the form and sends nothing.

| Answer kind | Check in the browser | Message | Check in the engine |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `questions` | Each question has at least 1 selected option. A selected "Other" has non-empty text. | "`<id>` has no answer yet." or "`<id>`: write your answer in the Other field." | "Answer `<id>` before continuing." when an answer is missing or blank |
| `approval` | A request for changes has non-empty feedback. | A message that asks you to say what must change so the spec agent can rewrite it. | "Say what to change." when `approved` is false and the feedback is empty |
| `choice` | The option exists. A `required` text is not empty. | The text of `missing` in `CHOICES`, or "This gate has no option `<option>`." | For `implementation_review`: `done`, or `feedback` with text. Else "Say what to change." or "Answer done, or feedback with what to change." |
| `closing` | None. Each project sends only the flags that it asked. | None | None |
| `permission` | None | None | None |
| `skills` | None | None | None |

These details affect the answer:

- **Approval with text:** the "Approve" button is disabled when the feedback field has text, and the tooltip says "Clear the change request to approve". This stops you from approving with a change request in the field.
- **Question answers:** the answer text for one question joins the selected labels and the other text with `; `. The key of the "Other" option is the constant `OTHER` (`__other__`).
- **Budget raise:** `parseDollars` accepts a positive number, with an optional leading `$`. If the field has text that does not parse, the card shows "Enter the amount as a number of US dollars, such as 10. Leave it empty to add the budget again." An empty field adds the budget again. The answered card then shows "by $N.NN".
- **Closing answer:** `closingAnswer` sends `tests` as false for a project that did not ask about tests, and `docs` as false for a project that did not ask about documentation.

## Findings tables and security blocks

Two gates and the security notice use two tables from [`web/src/features/gates/Findings.tsx`](web/src/features/gates/Findings.tsx). `ReviewFindings` shows the severity with the rule, the file, and the finding with its exact fix and its Guidance text. `FactFindings` shows the severity, the location, and the claim with the issue. `FactFindings` shows nothing when the list is empty. The severities BLOCKER and HIGH use the bad tone, MEDIUM uses the warn tone, and all others use the neutral tone.

`BlockerNotice` shows a security block with the tone bad and no dismiss button. The text explains that the reviewer found code whose effect looks dangerous, and that a weaker generation pass or a copied insecure example can cause it. Ostra sends only these findings back with an instruction to remove the code and reviews again until they are gone. Nobody can waive the block, and the session cannot complete when the block is open. The code cites Hard 21 for this rule.

`activeSecurityBlocks` decides which blocks show. It keeps the latest `security_block` event for each key `project:phase:tests`. A later event for the same key with no findings clears the block. A block clears only through a passing review. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) owns the review rules.

## Execution screen

An execution is one run of one agent. `ExecutionScreen` in [`web/src/screens/ExecutionScreen.tsx`](web/src/screens/ExecutionScreen.tsx) shows the resource `exec:<id>`. The screen shows usage first, then the stream that the execution names in `stream`. The value `activity` shows the Activity stream, which fits the native executor. The value `terminal` shows the Terminal stream and a Tool calls tab, which fits a harness. The screen reads `stream`, not the executor string. [Native executor loop](native-executor.md) and [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) own the two executors.

The header shows:

- The title: the agent name, the run label, and the project.
- The status chip, the stage label from `STAGES`, the executor, and the model with the elapsed time.
- A "Run" select, when the group has more than 1 run. A group is the runs of the same agent and project in the session, oldest first. A choice opens that run.
- A **Cancel** button, when the execution runs. It calls `api.cancelExecution(id)`.
- A **Resume** button, when the execution has ended, `can_resume` is true, the run is not an inspect run, and no terminal exists. It calls `api.resumeExecution(id)`. The tooltip says that it reopens the harness session with its own resume command.
- An **Open the session** button. It shows only when all these conditions are true: the run has ended, the stream is `terminal`, the run has a harness session ID, no terminal exists, the run is not itself an inspect run (`!inspects`), and the run has a session (`!!e.session`). These conditions form `canInspect` in `ExecutionScreen.tsx`. The button calls `api.inspectExecution(id)` and opens the new execution.

An inspect run is read-only. The banner "Read-only session" says that Ostra reopens an ended run so that you can scroll its work and ask the agent about it, and that Ostra refuses each tool call, because the work is done. The banner has a button to open the original run.

The usage strip shows Input, Output, Cache reads, and Tool calls. It shows "Cache / call" when the run has tool calls. It shows "Build time" when the run has build time. It ends with Cost and Duration. The numbers come from the latest `usage` delta, or from the execution view when no delta arrived. When the run is live, the duration ticks each second (`useNow`). [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md) owns the cost formula.

The section "Spawn parameters" is collapsed by default. It shows `spawn_block`: the exact parameter block that the agent received, followed by the project brief. No agent sees the conversation of another agent. It also shows a link to the report, and the harness session ID when one exists. [Agents, prompts, and coordination](agents-and-prompts.md) owns the spawn contract.

### What happens when

- **The execution does not load:** the screen shows "Ostra could not load this execution" with a "Try again" button.
- **Cancel or Resume fails:** the screen shows the server message in a banner. The buttons are disabled when the call runs.
- **The execution ends with an error:** the banner "The execution ended with an error" shows `error`.
- **The activity does not load:** the banner "Ostra could not load the activity" shows the message.
- **A gate names this run:** a notice shows above the stream. See the section on tool calls and permission notices.

## Live data on the execution screen

The execution screen combines a REST snapshot with live deltas. `useActivity` in [`web/src/screens/execution/useExecution.ts`](web/src/screens/execution/useExecution.ts) does the work. A delta is one small change to the activity, such as a piece of text or a tool result. Each delta has a sequence number (`seq`).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Screen as ExecutionScreen
  participant Hook as useActivity
  participant Api as api
  participant Sock as socket
  Screen->>Hook: useExecution(id)
  Hook->>Api: api.activity(id)
  Hook->>Sock: subscribe execution:id
  Sock-->>Hook: execution_delta (before the snapshot)
  Api-->>Hook: items
  Hook->>Hook: foldActivity(items), then apply held deltas
  Sock-->>Hook: execution_delta
  Hook->>Hook: applyDelta(state, seq, delta)
  Sock-->>Hook: execution_status
  Hook->>Screen: onStatus, then exec.reload
  Sock-->>Hook: reconnect
  Hook->>Api: api.activity(id, lastSeq)
```

The flow has these rules:

1. The hook loads the snapshot with `api.activity(id)` and subscribes to the channel `execution:<id>`.
2. A delta that arrives before the snapshot goes into a held list. After the snapshot loads, the hook applies the held deltas. This is needed because `applyDelta` drops each delta with a sequence number at or below the last one that it saw.
3. `applyDelta` ignores a delta with `seq` at or below `lastSeq`. A snapshot and the live stream can overlap safely.
4. After a reconnect, the hook fetches only the items after `lastSeq`.
5. An `execution_status` message sets the status and reloads the execution.
6. `useExecution` also watches the session channel. The events `gate_opened` and `gate_answered` reload the execution (throttled to 400 ms), because the field `pending_gate` comes from the session fold. The events `execution_started`, `execution_resumed`, and `execution_finished` reload the session detail (throttled to 800 ms). The session detail supplies the sibling runs.

If the snapshot request fails, the screen shows the error banner, and the hook keeps live deltas in the held list. A later reconnect fetches the missing items.

## Activity stream

The Activity stream shows what an agent does, in order. `foldActivity` turns the deltas into entries. The entry kinds are `text`, `thinking`, `status`, `turn`, and `tool`. The delta kinds are `text`, `thinking`, `status`, `tool_call`, `policy`, `tool_output`, `tool_result`, `usage`, `turn`, and `native_session_id`.

`applyDelta` in [`web/src/lib/events.ts`](web/src/lib/events.ts) follows these rules:

- Consecutive `text` deltas of one model response join into one block. Consecutive `thinking` deltas also join.
- A `tool_call` delta adds a tool entry. The deltas `policy`, `tool_output`, and `tool_result` update the entry with the same call ID. They add the policy decision, the live output, and the final output with its error flag and duration.
- A `turn` delta closes one model response. It adds the cost of the response to the thinking block of that response. If the response has no thinking block and no tool calls, it adds a "Model response" line.
- The cost of a response with tool calls splits in equal shares among those calls. Each tool entry shows its share with a `~` prefix.
- A cost under $0.01 shows 4 decimals, and other costs show 3 decimals (`formatTurnCost`).

The stream shows each entry kind in its own form. Thinking is a collapsed block with the title "Thinking summary". Text is rendered Markdown. A status is one line. A tool call has a header with the tool, a summary, a state (`running`, `error`, or `done`), the duration, and the policy line.

### How a tool call body looks

| Tool | Body |
| --- | --- |
| `Edit` | An inline diff from `old_string` and `new_string`. The lines that both strings share at the start and at the end stay as context. |
| `Write` | Each line as an added line. The diff shows the first 400 lines (`MAX_WRITE_LINES`) and then "N more lines not shown". |
| `ApplyPatch` | The lines of a Codex patch body. The markers `*** Begin Patch` and `*** End Patch` are removed. File headers and hunk markers show as context. |
| `Bash` | The line `$ command` followed by the output. |
| `Memory` | The area and the lesson. |
| `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `Skill`, `MemoryRecall`, `DocsSearch` | The summary and the output, without the raw input. |
| Other tools | The input as JSON, then the output. |

A tool output over 20,000 characters (`MAX_OUTPUT` in `ActivityStream.tsx`) is cut and ends with an ellipsis. `toolSummary` writes the one-line summary. For `Read`, `Write`, and `Edit` it is the file path. For `Bash` it is the command, cut at 160 characters. For `Grep` and `Glob` it is the pattern, with the path when one exists. For a tool whose name starts with `submit_` it is "result submitted to Ostra". `relativize` removes the repo root from the summary, so paths show relative to the project.

The stream follows new output only when you were within 48 px of the bottom before the output arrived and the execution is live. The first snapshot does not scroll, so the page opens at the usage strip. A tool row has the key `callId:decision`. A deny or ask that arrives after the call makes a new key, so the row opens again and you see it.

## Tool calls, policy decisions, and permission notices

For a harness run, the hook bridge reports each tool call to Ostra, and the policy decides. The Tool calls tab shows the result. `hookRows` makes one row for each tool entry. `HookLog` shows the columns Tool, Input, Decision, Rule, and Time. The Decision chip is "Allowed", "Denied", "Asking you" (the call waits), "Asked you" (the call has finished), or "No decision". The Rule column shows the layer and the rule, or "default" when no rule matched. [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) owns the hook bridge. [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) owns the layers, guards, and rules.

A denied or asked call shows the reason from the policy. A denied call also shows "What to do instead". `denialAdvice` writes this text:

- For a guard rule, the text comes from the constant `GUARD_ADVICE`, keyed by the guard ID. A guard ID with no entry has no advice.
- For a deny rule of the permissions, the text says that a deny rule matched and that you can edit the rule in the workspace settings.
- For an ask, the text says that no rule allows the call yet, and that you can allow it once or for the whole workspace.

| Guard ID | Advice text, in short |
| --- | --- |
| `write-scope` | The agent can write only inside its allowed directories. It must write its output to the session directory. |
| `no-tests-from-implementer` | Tests belong to the write-test stage. That stage runs after each phase passes review and only if you ask for tests. |
| `state-ownership` | The engine records pipeline state from real results. Do the underlying work and the record updates itself. |
| `artifact-ownership` | Spec and plan files change only when their own agent runs again. Request the change through the pipeline. |
| `report-path` | Write the report at the exact path in `Report file:`. |
| `lesson-gate` | Record what fixed the failure with the Memory tool before the report. |
| `build-streak` | Five builds in a row failed. The agent must return STUCK with the diagnostic so that Ostra can find the missing fact. |
| `self-protection` | Agents must not touch the binary, the configuration, or the databases of Ostra. |

The rule behind each guard belongs to [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md).

### The permission notice

`PermissionNotice` shows above the stream when a gate names the execution or when the last tool call waits on an ask. `pendingAsk` finds that call: it is the last tool entry, its decision is `ask`, and it has not finished.

- **A permission gate is open:** the banner shows "Allow once" and "Deny". It calls `api.answerGate` with a `permission` answer and then reloads the execution. A button opens the gate on the session board. The text says that the hook bridge (terminal) or Ostra (activity) holds the call until you decide.
- **Another gate names the run:** for a stuck, failed, or harness failure gate, the banner "A gate waits on this run" shows the title and a button to open the gate. You answer on the session board.
- **A pending ask with no gate record:** the banner shows a button to open the session.

The notice has no "Always in this workspace" button. That choice exists only on the gate card of the session board.

## Terminal stream

The Terminal stream shows the own interface of a harness. `TerminalStream` and `XtermScreen` draw it with xterm.js in the terminal frame of the design system. `terminalMode` picks one of three modes:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["terminalMode(e, status)"] --> B{"has_terminal or status is running?"}
  B -- yes --> L["live: keys and resizes go to the PTY"]
  B -- no --> C{"has_transcript?"}
  C -- yes --> R["replay: read-only stored transcript"]
  C -- no --> N["none: no output was stored"]
```

- **`live`:** a PTY exists or the run still goes. You can type into the terminal. Ostra still applies its guards and permissions through the hook bridge.
- **`replay`:** the run has ended and a transcript exists. Input is off. The banner offers Resume when `can_resume` is true. After Resume, the screen goes live.
- **`none`:** no output was stored. The banner says so, and it offers Resume when the harness session can resume. Otherwise it says that the session has ended and cannot resume.

`XtermScreen` in [`web/src/screens/execution/XtermScreen.tsx`](web/src/screens/execution/XtermScreen.tsx) connects to the channel `term:<execution>`. The first frame after the subscription is the backlog: the screen so far for a live run, or the stored transcript for an ended one. After that, it sends these messages when the mode is `live`:

- `term_input` with the typed data.
- `term_resize` with the columns and the rows. The fit addon measures them when the frame resizes, when the socket reconnects, and after the fonts load.

The terminal uses a scrollback of 10,000 lines, a font size of 12.5 px, and a line height of 1.2. It takes its colors from the `--term-*` tokens of the design system, with fixed fallback colors. The pane is dark in both themes. The key `${execution}:${mode}` makes the terminal start again when the mode changes. The code loads xterm.js on demand, and a spinner shows "Loading the terminal…" until it arrives.

The frame has a height of `max(360px, calc(100vh - 400px))` (the constant `HEIGHT`). A button maximizes it. When the frame is maximized, `Escape` restores it, but only when the focus is outside the terminal. Inside the terminal, `Escape` belongs to the harness, so you press `Shift+Escape`. The terminal bar shows the project and the size as `cols×rows`.

[Harness executors](harness-executors.md) owns the PTY, the terminal log, and the transcript. [REST and WebSocket API](server-api.md) owns the channel limits.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Maximize the terminal | Off | Component state only | At once | The button label "Restore the terminal (Shift+Esc)" | Press the button, or press `Shift+Escape` inside the terminal |
| Resume an ended run | Not applied | The execution record, through `api.resumeExecution` | When the server replies | The mode changes from `replay` to `live` | Press Cancel on the live run |

## Terminal safety

Harness output is untrusted text, and a terminal executes control sequences in that text. Without checks, a program can make the browser send data that looks like typed input, or it can lead you to a harmful address. `web/src/screens/execution/terminalSafety.ts` limits both risks in the browser.

### Mute the query replies

A terminal query is a control sequence that asks the terminal to report something, such as the cursor position or the version. xterm.js normally answers each query and sends the answer to the PTY. The server already answers queries itself, one time, whether any number of browsers or none watch the run. A second answer from a browser reaches the harness as typed input. `muteQueryReplies` registers handlers that return `true` for each query. A handler that returns `true` marks the sequence as handled, so xterm.js sends no reply.

```ts
const WINDOW_REPORTS = new Set([11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21]);
...
parser.registerCsiHandler({ final: "n" }, always),
parser.registerCsiHandler({ final: "c" }, always),
...
parser.registerCsiHandler({ final: "t" }, (params) => WINDOW_REPORTS.has(Number(params[0]))),
parser.registerDcsHandler({ intermediates: "$", final: "q" }, always),
...[4, 10, 11, 12, 17, 19].map((ident) =>
  parser.registerOscHandler(ident, (data) => data.split(";").includes("?")),
),
```

The handlers cover these groups:

- **Always muted (CSI):** the finals `n` and `c` (also with the prefixes `?`, `>`, and `=` for `c`), `$p` (also with the prefix `?`), `>q`, and `?u`.
- **Muted only for a report (CSI `t`):** the first parameter must be in `WINDOW_REPORTS`: 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, or 21. Other values move or resize the window. xterm.js ignores them anyway, so the handler returns `false`.
- **Always muted (DCS):** the sequences `$q` and `+q`.
- **Muted only for a query (OSC):** the numbers 4, 10, 11, 12, 17, and 19. The handler returns `true` only when the data contains `?`. An OSC that sets a color, such as `rgb:0000/0000/0000`, still runs.

The function returns one disposable that removes every handler. The unit test `terminalSafety.test.ts` covers only part of these handlers. It checks the DCS `$q` handler (not `+q`), the OSC numbers 4 and 11 (not 10, 12, 17, or 19), and the dispose call, which leaves no handler. It does not check CSI `=c`.

### Open only web links, and only after you confirm

`linkHandler` sets `allowNonHttpProtocols` to `false`. When you activate a link, `safeLinkTarget` parses the address. It returns the address only for the protocols `http:` and `https:`. For `javascript:`, `file:`, and text that is not an address, it returns `null`, and nothing happens. For a web address, the browser asks "Open this link from the terminal?" and shows the full address. After you confirm, the browser opens the address in a new window with `noopener,noreferrer`. The terminal also sets `allowProposedApi` to `false`.

### What the terminal safety does not guarantee

- It does not filter other control sequences in the output. It only controls replies and links.
- It does not stop the harness from reading what you type. You can type into a live terminal.
- It does not check the address that you confirm. You must read it.
- It does not replace the policy. The hook bridge still applies the guards and the permissions to each tool call. See [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md).

## Artifact screen

An artifact is a file in a session directory, such as a research document, a spec, a plan, a report, or a review ledger. `ArtifactScreen` in [`web/src/screens/ArtifactScreen.tsx`](web/src/screens/ArtifactScreen.tsx) shows the resource `artifact:<absolute path>`. The server route `GET /api/artifacts?path=` serves only files inside a session directory. [Workspace artifacts and uploads](artifacts-and-uploads.md) owns the artifact rules and the other routes.

The screen calls `api.artifact(path)` and gets the content, the headings, an optional typed `document`, and a `binary` flag. The server sets `binary` to true when the file is larger than 4 MiB (`ARTIFACT_LIMIT`) or is not valid UTF-8 text. Then the content is empty. The screen shows "No preview for this file" with a Download button, and it says that the agents read the file from its path.

### The artifact kind

`artifactKind(path, refKind)` in [`web/src/screens/artifact/kind.ts`](web/src/screens/artifact/kind.ts) picks one of 8 kinds. It uses the `kind` of the session artifact reference when that value is one of the 8. Otherwise it reads the file name:

| File name or path | Kind | Label in `KIND_LABEL` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/uploads/<file>` | `upload` | Upload |
| `ostra-review-ledger*` | `ledger` | Review ledger |
| `ostra-spec-*` | `spec` | Spec |
| `ostra-plan-*phase-N*` or `phase-N.md` | `phase` | Phase file |
| `ostra-plan-*` | `plan` | Plan |
| `ostra-research-*` | `research` | Research |
| A name that contains `completion` | `completion` | Completion report |
| Anything else | `report` | Report |

The screen finds the owner session in the workspace tree. If it finds one, the screen shows the project chip, the approval badges, a button to open the session board, and the fact-check chapter. If it finds none, those parts are missing and the screen still shows the file.

### Toolbar and badges

The toolbar has the kind chip, the project chip, and the badges. At the right it has these buttons:

- "How to read requirements", when you hid the note.
- "Document" or "Markdown", only for a typed document.
- Open the session board.
- Ask about this artifact. This opens the dock with the text "In `<file>`, ".
- Copy the path, Download, and Reload.

`approvalBadges` adds chips for a spec or a plan. It reads the last fact-check stage and the last approval stage of the session. A finished fact-check shows "Fact-check PASS" when the stage detail is empty or contains "pass". Otherwise it shows "Fact-check" with the detail. A running fact-check shows "Fact-check running". The approval gate shows "Approved by you", "Approved by YOLO", or "Approved by Ostra", or the same with "Changes requested by". An open gate shows "Waiting for your approval".

A spec, a plan, and a phase file carry the reading note `EARS_NOTE`. It explains the five EARS sentence shapes (ubiquitous, event-driven, state-driven, unwanted behavior, and optional feature) and the Given, When, Then form of acceptance criteria. The "Hide the note" button saves the choice in the browser.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hide the reading note | Shown (`false`) | The browser `localStorage`, key `ostra.earsNoteHidden`, value `1` | At once, also on the mobile screen | The note banner, or the button "How to read requirements" | Press "How to read requirements" to show the note again |
| Document or Markdown view | Document, for a typed file | Component state only | At once | The label on the toggle | Press the toggle |

## Markdown artifacts

A file that is not a typed document shows as Markdown, with an outline on the left. `ArtifactMarkdown` in [`web/src/screens/artifact/ArtifactMarkdown.tsx`](web/src/screens/artifact/ArtifactMarkdown.tsx) renders it. It does not render raw HTML, so a file that an agent wrote cannot inject markup into the page.

The outline lists the headings of levels 1 to 3 from the server. `ArtifactScreen.tsx` keeps a heading when `h.level <= 3`. A click scrolls to the heading with an offset of 16 px (`SCROLL_OFFSET`) and writes the anchor in the URL. The screen marks the last heading above the top of the view as the active heading. It uses a limit of three times the offset, that is 48 px below the top edge. A `#<id>` link in the URL scrolls to the heading after the content renders.

The heading IDs must match the IDs that the server lists. `rehypeHeadingIds` in `web/src/screens/artifact/outline.ts` ports `crates/ostra-core/src/outline.rs`. It matches each heading to the next server heading with the same level and text. A heading that the server did not list gets a new slug that cannot collide with a listed one. A slug keeps letters, digits, `-`, and `_`, and turns each space into `-`. A repeated slug gets the suffix `-1`, `-2`, and so on.

The renderer also does this:

- A link that starts with `#` calls `onAnchor` and does not follow the link. Other links open in a new window with `rel="noreferrer"`.
- A code block uses `CodeView` with the language from its fence, or `txt`.
- A table sits in `ScrollTable`. The sticky scroll bar of that component stays at the bottom of the view when the table is on screen, so you can scroll a tall table sideways. Each header cell has a `ColumnResizer`.
- A cell whose text matches `ID_CELL` (such as `R1`, `AC2.1`, `E3`, `F4`, or `P5`) gets the class `art-id`.

`ColumnResizer` has the minimum width `MIN`, which is 48 px. You drag the edge with the pointer, or you press `ArrowLeft` or `ArrowRight` to change the width by 16 px (48 px with `Shift`). A double click returns the table to automatic widths. The first resize freezes each column at its current width, so a change to one column does not reflow the others.

## Typed document viewer

Research, spec, plan, and phase files carry a typed document. The server sends it as `document` with a list of `issues`. `DocumentView` in [`web/src/screens/artifact/doc/DocumentView.tsx`](web/src/screens/artifact/doc/DocumentView.tsx) shows it as chapters: a menu on the left and one chapter at a time on the right. A "Previous" and a "Next" button move between chapters. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) owns the document types and the fact-check.

Each document kind has its own chapters. A chapter marked "if present" shows only when the document has data for it.

| Kind | Chapters |
| --- | --- |
| Research | Overview, Files (if present), Patterns (if present), Data flow (if present), Dependencies (if present), External technology, Approaches, Open questions, Sources, Lessons used (if present), Not covered (if present) |
| Spec | Overview, Scope, Criteria, Deliverables, Requirements with one sub-chapter for each deliverable, Contracts, External evidence, Data impact (if present), Assumptions (if present), Open questions, Traceability, Notes (if present) |
| Plan | Overview, Phases with one sub-chapter for each phase, Traceability, Risks (if present), Clarifying questions, Checks and verification |
| Phase file | Overview, Steps, Requirements delivered, External constraints |

When a fact-check pass ran, the viewer adds the chapter "Fact-check" with the count of findings. It shows the verdict chip (`VERDICT_TONE`: PASS is `ok`, FAIL is `bad`, ERROR is `warn`, and no verdict shows "Running"). It also says which version the pass checked and whether that is the version on screen.

### Element IDs and marks

Each element of a document has an ID, such as `R3`, `AC3.2`, `E1`, `phase 2`, or `step 2.3`. `normId` turns every spelling into one key: it lowercases the ID and removes spaces, turns `phase 2` or `p2` into `phase-2`, and turns `step 2.3`, `s2.3`, or `2.3` into `step-2.3`.

A mark is a note on one element. Two sources make marks:

- **Ostra's checks (`issues`):** an issue with level `error` has the tone `bad`. Other issues have the tone `warn`.
- **Fact-check findings:** `severityTone` maps BLOCKER and HIGH to `bad`, MEDIUM to `warn`, and other severities to `info`.

A finding names its element in the `element` field, or in its `location` text. `ID_IN_TEXT` finds the first ID in that text. It matches `AC<n>.<n>`, `R<n>`, `E<n>`, `D<n>`, `C<n>`, `Q<n>`, `step <n>.<n>`, and `phase <n>`. A mark with no element goes to the chapter "Fact-check" when it comes from a fact-check, and to the Overview chapter otherwise. The menu shows a dot on each chapter that holds a mark. The dot has the tone of the worst mark (`RANK` orders the tones: `bad`, then `warn`, then `info`). A sub-chapter passes its worst tone to its parent. An open question also marks its chapter as needing attention.

An element ID in the text is a `Ref` chip. A click on the chip goes to the element. If the ID is not in the document, the chip is inert. The chip has the color of the worst mark on its element. The URL anchor is `#chapter` or `#chapter/element`, and `parseAnchor` reads it. The viewer scrolls the element to the center, or scrolls to the top when no element is named.

`pickFactCheck(all, target)` picks the pass to show. The target is `spec` for a spec and `plan` for a plan or a phase file. A research document has none. It returns the latest pass that is for the current version and has a verdict. If none qualifies, it returns the last pass of that target. On the Overview chapter, a banner shows "Ostra's checks found N issues", with the tone `bad` when any issue is an error.

The viewers use these display constants:

| Constant | File | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EARS_LABEL` | `doc/spec.tsx` | `ubiquitous` is "Ubiquitous", `event-driven` is "Event-driven", `state-driven` is "State-driven", `unwanted` is "Unwanted behavior", `optional` is "Optional feature", `complex` is "State and event" |
| `EARS` | `doc/parts.tsx` | The pattern that sets the words `THE SYSTEM SHALL`, `WHEN`, `WHILE`, `IF`, `THEN`, and `WHERE` in bold in a requirement |
| `CHANGE_TONE` | `doc/plan.tsx` | A step that creates is `ok`, one that modifies is `info`, one that deletes is `bad` |
| `LEVEL_TONE` | `doc/plan.tsx` | Low is `ok`, Medium is `warn`, High is `bad` (complexity and risk likelihood) |
| `MARK_CHIP`, `VERDICT_SEVERITY` | `doc/parts.tsx` | Map a mark tone to the chip tone with the same name |

## Review ledger view

A review ledger is the file `ostra-review-ledger*.md`. The reviewer adds one iteration for each pass, and the fix agent records FIXED or WONTFIX for each finding. `LedgerView` in [`web/src/screens/artifact/LedgerView.tsx`](web/src/screens/artifact/LedgerView.tsx) shows the findings as a table and as comments on a diff. The page text says that the loop stops when a pass comes back clean, or asks you after 3 passes. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) owns the cap.

`parseLedger` in `web/src/lib/ledger.ts` reads the tables:

1. A heading of level 1 to 4 with the text "Iteration N" sets the pass number.
2. The first row of a table is the header. A table without a `severity` column is skipped.
3. The parser matches columns by the start of the lowercase header name: `id`, `severity`, `file`, `rule`, `description`, and `fix`. It writes the severity in upper case and removes backticks from the file.

`ledgerLoop` reads the project and the phase from the path `/<project>/ostra-review-ledger[-phase-<id>].md`. The phase is `none` when the name has no phase. The view then calls `api.diff(session, project, phase)` and shows each changed file in a side-by-side Monaco diff (`MonacoDiff`). A finding matches a file when one path ends with the other. A finding that names "line N" in its description or fix becomes a line mark. BLOCKER and HIGH use a red mark, and other severities use a warning mark. The hover text shows the finding and its fix. The editor is read-only. Its height is the line count times 19 px plus 24 px, with a minimum of 120 px and a maximum of 420 px.

If no session ID or project is known, or if the diff request fails, the view shows "No diff is available for this loop, so the ledger is shown as written." The same note shows when the diff has no file.

## Mobile screens

The mobile shell shows `MSession`, `MExecution`, and `MArtifact` in place of the screens above on a small display. `MOBILE_QUERY` and the shell belong to [Web console shell](web-console.md). The mobile screens reuse the same data code and components: `laneStates`, `mergeEvents`, `GateCard`, `BlockerNotice`, `ActivityStream`, `TerminalStream`, `PermissionNotice`, `useExecution`, `docChapters`, and `ArtifactMarkdown`. The gate answers and the checks are the same.

### Mobile session board

`MSession` in [`web/src/mobile/screens/MSession.tsx`](web/src/mobile/screens/MSession.tsx) differs from the desktop board in these ways:

- The order is: request and context, chips, controls, banners, open gates, the completion report, the composer, the lane strip, and the tabs.
- The lane strip is a scroll row of cards with the lane title and the detail line. `laneCards` gives a default detail "Done", "Skipped", or "Not started" when a lane has none.
- The lane card lists the stages. A tap on a stage goes to its gate when the stage is `waiting` and has a gate. Otherwise it opens the running execution, or the latest one (`stageTarget`). The card has no "Produces" or "Protects against" text. It has a "Why this step exists" toggle with the lane `why` text.
- The tabs are `TABS`: Phases, Executions, Artifacts, Decisions, and Event log, each with a count. The first tab is Phases when the plan has phases, and Executions otherwise.
- The Phases tab shows waves (`phaseWaves`). A wave is a column of the phase graph. It has the label "Wave N", with "runs in parallel" when it holds more than 1 phase. A phase line shows the complexity, "tests <policy>", "after P1", "review pass N", and "security block" when they apply. A tap opens the phase file.
- The Executions tab groups runs by agent and project. The status dot uses `EXEC_TONE`. A tap opens `exec:<id>`.
- The Artifacts tab lists each artifact with an icon: a paper clip for an upload, a checklist for a ledger, and a file for the rest.
- The controls are YOLO, Pause or Continue, and Stop. Stop asks for confirmation inline, in the page, and does not open a dialog.
- "Add context" starts collapsed. It has no `Mod+Enter` key. "Send now" asks for confirmation inline.
- The mobile board has no desktop Overview and Decisions tab pair. Its Decisions tab is one of the five `TABS`, and it shows each `Decision` row with the same `OverrideDialog`. You can override a decision on mobile.

`STAGE_TONE` maps a stage status to a tone: `pending` and `skipped` are `neutral`, `running` is `accent`, `waiting` is `warn`, `done` is `ok`, and `failed` and `blocked` are `bad`. `EXEC_TONE` maps an execution status: `running` is `accent`, `ok` is `ok`, `stuck`, `handoff`, and `interrupted` are `warn`, `waiting` is `info`, `cancelled` is `neutral`, and `denied` and `error` are `bad`.

### Mobile execution screen

`MExecution` in [`web/src/mobile/screens/MExecution.tsx`](web/src/mobile/screens/MExecution.tsx) shows these parts:

- A grid with Executor, Model, Cost, Elapsed, Input, and Output. It has no cache, tool call, or build time numbers.
- The status chip, the stage label, and a link to the session. The link text is the session label cut to 40 characters.
- The other runs of the group as chips with a status dot (`RUN_TONE`). In `RUN_TONE`, `handoff` is `info`, but `EXEC_TONE` uses `warn` for it.
- The tabs Activity, or Terminal with Tool calls. The Tool calls tab shows cards. Each card has an icon for the tool, the duration, the decision chip (`DECISION`: `allow` is "Allowed" and `deny` is "Denied"), the summary, and the rule.
- The buttons at the bottom: "Cancel the execution", "Resume" (only for an activity stream, because the terminal frame has its own Resume button), "Open the session to read its work", and "Open the report".
- The terminal title without the prefix `harness:`.

There is no Spawn parameters section on mobile.

### Mobile artifact screen

`MArtifact` in [`web/src/mobile/screens/MArtifact.tsx`](web/src/mobile/screens/MArtifact.tsx) differs in these ways:

- A typed document shows its chapters as a scroll row of chips, with "Previous" and "Next" buttons. A chapter change writes the anchor in the URL without a history entry, so Back leaves the artifact and does not step through the chapters.
- A segmented control switches between Document and Markdown. The Markdown view of a typed document is a plain `pre` block.
- A binary file with the extension png, jpg, jpeg, gif, webp, or avif (`IMAGE`) shows as an image. Other binary files show the same "No preview" banner, and the text says "this device".
- A Markdown artifact shows a chip row of its level 2 headings when there are at least 2.
- A ledger shows its findings as cards (`SEVERITY_TONE` sets the severity chip) and shows each changed file as a unified diff. `unifiedDiff` builds the diff in the browser. It replaces the Monaco diff, which is too large for a phone. [Project, Files, and dependency screens](web-project-screens.md) owns `unifiedDiff` and its limit.
- The actions are at the bottom of the page: the session board, "Ask about it", Download, Copy path, and "How to read requirements".

## Constants of the session screens

| Constant | File | Value or content | What it controls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `LANES` | `web/src/content/stages.ts` | 9 entries with `title` and `why` | The lane titles and the why text on both boards |
| `STAGES` | `web/src/content/stages.ts` | 38 entries with `label`, `produces`, `protects` | The stage labels and the detail box |
| `EARS_NOTE` | `web/src/content/stages.ts` | A title and a Markdown body | The reading note on a spec, a plan, and a phase file |
| `LANE_ORDER` | `web/src/lib/events.ts` | research, requirements, verification, design, build, review, test, docs, done | The order of the lanes |
| `PHASE_LANES` | `web/src/screens/SessionScreen.tsx` | design, build, review, test | The lanes that show the phase graph |
| `GUARD_ADVICE` | `web/src/lib/events.ts` | 8 guard IDs | The advice under a denied call |
| `ANSWER_KIND` | `web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts` | 14 gate kinds | The answer kind of each gate |
| `OTHER` | `web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts` | `__other__` | The key of the "Other" option |
| `CHOICES` | `web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts` | 8 gate kinds with 2 options each | The buttons and the text rule of a choice gate |
| `PERMISSION_LABELS` | `web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts` | 3 labels | The text of the permission answers |
| `DISPOSITIONS` | `web/src/lib/gateAnswers.ts` | generate, regenerate, reuse, drop | The choices in the skill table |
| `NOTE` | `web/src/features/gates/ApprovalGate.tsx` | One sentence for the spec and one for the plan | The note under an approval gate |
| `ARTIFACTS_ROOT` | `web/src/features/context/tags.ts` | `_artifacts` | The tag root of workspace artifacts |
| `CONTEXT_DRAG_TYPE` | `web/src/features/context/tags.ts` | `application/x-ostra-context` | The drag type of a Files panel row |
| `ZWSP` | `web/src/features/context/FileTagInput.tsx` | U+200B | A hidden mark that keeps a trailing line break visible |
| `MAX_WRITE_LINES` | `web/src/screens/execution/model.ts` | 400 | The lines shown for a `Write` diff |
| `MAX_OUTPUT` | `web/src/screens/execution/ActivityStream.tsx` | 20,000 | The characters shown for a tool output |
| `HEIGHT` | `web/src/screens/execution/TerminalStream.tsx` | `max(360px, calc(100vh - 400px))` | The height of the terminal frame |
| `WINDOW_REPORTS` | `web/src/screens/execution/terminalSafety.ts` | 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21 | The window queries that stay muted |
| `SCROLL_OFFSET` | `web/src/screens/ArtifactScreen.tsx` | 16 px | The offset of an outline scroll |
| `ARTIFACT_LIMIT` | `crates/ostra-server/src/api.rs` | 4 MiB | The size above which a file has no preview |
| `KIND_LABEL` | `web/src/screens/artifact/kind.ts` | 8 labels | The kind chip of an artifact |
| `ID_CELL` | `web/src/screens/artifact/ArtifactMarkdown.tsx` | A pattern for IDs such as `R1` and `AC2.1` | The table cells that get the class `art-id` |
| `MIN` | `web/src/screens/artifact/ColumnResizer.tsx` | 48 px | The smallest column width |
| `ID_IN_TEXT`, `RANK` | `web/src/screens/artifact/doc/model.ts` | An ID pattern, and the order of three tones | Where a finding lands, and which tone wins |
| `VERDICT_TONE` | `web/src/screens/artifact/doc/parts.tsx` | PASS `ok`, FAIL `bad`, ERROR `warn` | The verdict chip |
| `TABS` | `web/src/mobile/screens/MSession.tsx` | 5 tabs | The tabs of the mobile board |
| `STAGE_TONE`, `EXEC_TONE` | `web/src/mobile/screens/sessionView.ts` | Status to tone maps | The dots on the mobile board |
| `RUN_TONE`, `DECISION` | `web/src/mobile/screens/MExecution.tsx` | Status and decision to tone maps | The chips on the mobile execution screen |
| `SEVERITY_TONE`, `IMAGE` | `web/src/mobile/screens/MArtifact.tsx` | A severity to tone map, and an image pattern | The ledger cards and the image preview |
