sections.title: Project, Files, and dependency screens
sections.summary: How the console shows one project: the overview and commands panel, the File screen with its Monaco editor, jump and hint actions, the diff pane, the Git dock panel, and the dependency graph.
sections.body:
## Why the project screens exist

A project in Ostra is a folder on disk with a profile in `.ostra/project.toml`. Without a screen for it, a user cannot see whether the project is initialized, change its build command, read a file that an agent changed, or see how the files depend on each other. The project screens give the console these views.

This page covers:

- the project header, the Overview tab, and the Commands panel (`ProjectScreen`, `ProjectOverview`, `CommandsPanel`)
- the File screen and its Monaco editor (`FileScreen`, `FileEditor`, `useFileEdit`)
- jump actions, completion hints, and signature hints in the editor
- the code pane with Outline, Usages, and Dependencies tabs
- the diff pane, the gutter change marks, and the mobile line diff
- the Git dock panel (`GitPanel`)
- the dependency graph and the dependency file screen

The screens read data from REST routes and from the socket. The server side belongs to [Project files, Git dock, and cloning](project-files-and-git.md) and to [Code navigation](code-navigation.md). The shell, the routing, and the API client belong to [Web console shell](web-console.md). This page explains only the browser side.

### Resource IDs

The console opens each screen from a resource ID. The helpers `fileId`, `depId`, and `locationId` in `web/src/lib/resource.ts` build the IDs for file screens. The function `resourcePath` builds the URL of each ID, and `resourceFromPath` parses it.

| Resource ID | Screen | URL form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `project:<key>` | `ProjectScreen` | `/w/:ws/p/:key` |
| `file:<key>:<path>` | `FileScreen` | `/w/:ws/f/:key/<path>` |
| `dep:<key>:<uri>` | `DependencyFileScreen` | `/w/:ws/d/:key?uri=<uri>` |

`locationId` returns a `dep:` ID when the location has a `uri`. Otherwise it returns a `file:` ID. A `#L<n>` anchor on any file ID marks line `n`.

## Project header, Pull button, and tabs

`ProjectScreen` shows one project of the open workspace. It finds the project in `useWorkspace().detail.projects` by `projectKey`. The header always shows the project, and two tabs below it switch between the Overview and the Dependencies views.

### What the header shows

- The project key as the title.
- A `StatusChip` for `init_status`.
- A branch chip. It shows `git_branch`, which Ostra reads from `.git/HEAD`, or the word `git` when the branch is unknown. A warning chip `not a git checkout` replaces it when `is_git` is false.
- The project path, then the stack label. `stackLabel` returns `p.stack`, which is the stack chosen at import. If that is empty, it returns `p.profile.stack`, which is the name that the initializer gave. If both are empty, it returns `null`.

### Pull and Browse files

The **Pull** button shows only when `is_git` is true. It calls `api.pullProject`, which sends `POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/projects/{key}/pull`. The button is disabled and reads `Pulling…` until the call ends. The tooltip says that Pull fast-forwards the checked-out branch from its upstream. The pull rules and timeouts belong to [Project files, Git dock, and cloning](project-files-and-git.md).

After the call ends, a banner shows the result:

- If the branch changed, the banner says `Pulled <branch> from <before> to <after>.`
- If nothing changed, the banner says `<branch> is already up to date.`
- If the call fails, a red banner shows the error message.

The **Browse files** button calls `shell.browseFiles(key)`. The shell then opens the sidebar, selects the Files tab, and sets `filesProject` to the key. The Files panel itself belongs to [Web console shell](web-console.md).

### What happens when

- If the workspace detail has not loaded, the screen shows `Reading the projects…`.
- If the key matches no project, the screen shows `No project <key> in this workspace. It may have been removed.` and an **Add project** button.
- If the user selects the Dependencies tab, the screen mounts `DependencyGraph` with `key={p.key}`. A new project key therefore resets the graph state.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored where | Takes effect | State shown | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pull button | Not running | Nothing is stored. The call changes the checkout on disk. | At once | The banner under the header | Wait for the call to end. The screen has no cancel control. |
| Overview or Dependencies tab | `overview` | Screen memory only | At once | The selected tab | Select the other tab. |

## Project overview by initialization status

`ProjectOverview` shows a different body for each `init_status` of the project. A project that has no profile cannot receive pipeline work, so the screen leads the user to the init session first. The init flow itself belongs to [Project init and skills](init-and-skills.md).

| `init_status` | What the Overview shows |
| --- | --- |
| `missing` | A red banner `Folder missing`. It says that Ostra cannot find the path and that removing the project deletes nothing on disk. A **Remove from workspace** button sits in the banner. |
| `initializing` | An `Initializing` panel with a horizontal stepper at step 1 of `INIT_STEPS`. If the workspace tree holds a session with `kind.kind` equal to `init` for this project, an **Open the init session** button opens it. |
| `not_initialized` | An `Initialize this project` panel with the stepper at step 0. It lists what the init writes and has the buttons **Initialize `<key>`**, **Check again**, and **Remove from workspace**. |
| other (initialized) | The Commands, Skills, and Maintenance panels, then the Modules table and the Review rules table. |

`INIT_STEPS` holds six labels: `Detect`, `Scout`, `Propose skills`, `Your approval`, `Generate`, and `Inventory`. The stepper is a fixed display. It does not read the real stage of the init session.

The `not_initialized` text says that the init scouts the code, proposes skills for approval, and then writes `.ostra/INVENTORY.md`, `.ostra/project.toml`, and the skills. It also says that no pipeline task can target the project until the init ends. If `ultracode_bootstrap` is true, the panel adds a note that a `.ultracode/` folder exists and that the init can reuse its skills.

### Panels of an initialized project

- **Commands:** the `CommandsPanel`. The next part explains it.
- **Skills:** one outlined chip for each skill in `profile.skills`. The chip tooltip shows the skill kind and path. The count of review rules and the count of lessons in memory show below the chips. The screen reads the lessons with `api.lessons` only when the status is `initialized`. The **Manage** button opens the Skills screen with `?project=<key>`.
- **Maintenance:** **Re-initialize** calls the same `init` function as the first initialization. **Memory** opens the Memory screen with `?project=<key>`. **Remove from workspace** opens a confirmation dialog.
- **Modules:** a table of `glob` and `area` from `profile.module_map`. It shows only when the list is not empty.
- **Review rules:** a table of `id`, `rule`, `severity`, and `auto_fixable` from `profile.review_rules`. It shows only when the list is not empty.

`EMPTY_COMMANDS` is the object that the Commands panel gets when the profile is missing. All seven commands are `null` in it.

### What happens when

- If the user presses **Initialize**, the screen calls `api.initProject`, reloads the workspace, and opens `session:<id>` of the new init session. The button reads `Starting…` during the call. If the call fails, a red banner shows the message.
- If the user confirms the removal, the screen calls `api.removeProject`, reloads the workspace, and closes the tab `project:<key>`. The dialog says that nothing on disk is deleted and that the path and its `.ostra/` folder stay, so the user can import the project again.
- If the removal fails, the dialog closes and a red banner shows the message.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored where | Takes effect | State shown | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Initialize or Re-initialize | Not started | The init session writes `.ostra/INVENTORY.md`, `.ostra/project.toml`, and skills. | At once. The init session opens. | The status chip, the stepper, and the init session | Stop the init session on its own screen. See [Session, execution, and gate screens](web-session-screens.md). |
| Remove from workspace | Not removed | The workspace project list | At once, after the user confirms | The project leaves the sidebar. | Import the folder again. Nothing on disk changes. |

## Commands panel

`CommandsPanel` shows and edits the `[commands]` table of `.ostra/project.toml`. Agents and the engine read the profile for each execution. A saved command therefore applies to the next execution, and a run that already started keeps the old command. The rules for the commands, and the server checks, belong to [Project init and skills](init-and-skills.md).

`COMMANDS` is the list of seven fields. Each entry has a key, a label, and a placeholder example.

| Key | Label | Placeholder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `build` | Build | `cargo build` |
| `test` | Test | `cargo test` |
| `test_one` | One test | `cargo test {name}` |
| `typecheck` | Typecheck | `tsc --noEmit` |
| `lint` | Lint | `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` |
| `format` | Format | `cargo fmt` |
| `run` | Run | `cargo run` |

The placeholders are only hints in the empty input. They are not defaults. The `test_one` field has the hint `{name} is replaced with the test to run.`

### How the panel works

1. The read view lists only the commands that have a value. If none has a value, it shows `No commands in .ostra/project.toml` and an **Add commands** button.
2. **Edit** copies the commands into a draft and shows one input for each of the seven keys.
3. **Save commands** calls `api.saveProjectCommands`, which sends `PUT /api/workspaces/{ws}/projects/{key}/commands` with the whole draft.
4. If the call succeeds, the panel drops the draft and calls `onSaved`. The overview then reloads the workspace.
5. **Cancel** drops the draft and sends nothing.

### How the panel shows a refusal

The server answers a refused save with status 422 and a list of issues. Each issue has a `path` and a `message`. `commandErrors` turns that list into two parts:

- An issue whose path is `commands.<name>`, where `<name>` is one of the seven keys, goes to the input of that key.
- Every other issue goes into one general message, joined with spaces.
- If the error has no issues, the general message is the error text.

The panel stays in edit mode after a refusal, so the user can fix the field and save again. The tests in `web/src/screens/project/commands.test.tsx` check this behavior.

| Setting | Default | Stored where | Takes effect | State shown | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `commands.build`, `commands.test`, `commands.test_one`, `commands.typecheck`, `commands.lint`, `commands.format`, `commands.run` | Empty until the init or the user sets them | `.ostra/project.toml`, table `[commands]` | At the next agent execution | The Commands panel on the Overview tab | Select **Edit**, clear the field, and save. An empty field removes the command. |

## File screen: views, header, and status bar

`FileScreen` shows one project file in the whole center pane. It has three views, and the user switches between them with a segmented tab control. The screen refreshes when the file changes on disk.

### The three views

| View ID | Tab label | When the tab exists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | File | Always |
| `rendered` | Rendered | The extension is `md` or `markdown` and the file has text content. |
| `diff` | Changes | The file has a diff against HEAD with at least one hunk. |

The screen picks the view in this order:

1. If the user is editing, the view is `file`.
2. If the user chose a view and its tab exists, that view shows.
3. If a diff exists, the view is `diff`.
4. Otherwise the view is `file`.

The screen fetches the diff with `api.projectDiff` only when the file has a git mark. The `diff` view uses `DiffPane`. The `rendered` view uses the `Markdown` component. The `file` view uses the lazy `FileEditor`.

### Header, bar, and status bar

The header is 36 px high. It holds breadcrumbs, the counts `+added` and `−removed` when a diff exists, the view tabs, the edit controls, and these icon buttons:

- **Edit this file** (pencil). It shows only on the `file` view when the file has a hash and the user is not editing. It is disabled when the file is read-only, and then its label shows the reason.
- **Show or hide the code pane.** It shows only when the file is text and the user is not editing.
- **Ask about this file.** It calls `shell.openDock` with the text `About <key>/<path>: `, so the side panel opens with a prefilled question.
- **Copy path.** It writes the path to the clipboard and shows a check icon for 1,200 ms.

The first breadcrumb opens the project beside the file. For workspace artifacts, the project key equals `ARTIFACTS_ROOT`, and the first breadcrumb reads `Artifacts`. This breadcrumb calls `shell.browseFiles(projectKey)`. In `web/src/shell/WorkspaceShell.tsx`, that call with `ARTIFACTS_ROOT` sets `leftTab` to `artifacts` and does not set `filesProject`. The breadcrumb therefore opens the Artifacts tab of the sidebar, not the Files tab. Artifacts belong to [Workspace artifacts and uploads](artifacts-and-uploads.md).

When the view is `diff` and the file has a `changed_by` record, a bar shows under the header. It says `Added by` for the git marks `A` and `?`, and `Changed by` for the others. Two links follow. The first opens the execution `exec:<id>`, and the second opens the session `session:<id>`. Both open beside the file. The bar adds `(running)` or `(staged)` when the record says so. The label comes from `changedByLabel`, for example `Write test · Phase 3 tests` or `Implementer`.

The status bar is 24 px high. It shows the file type or extension, the line count, the size, the modified time, the git word with `, staged` when the file is staged, and `cut at the size cap` when the content is truncated. At the right end it shows `read-only`, `editing`, or `unsaved changes`.

### What happens when

- If the file is binary, the screen shows `Binary file, <size>. No preview.`
- If the text exceeds the size that Ostra reads for the browser, `f.truncated` is true. A banner says that the screen shows the start of the file, and the file cannot be edited.
- If the diff is truncated, a banner says `The diff is cut at the size cap. The first changes are shown.`
- If the read fails, a red banner shows the message and a **Try again** button.
- If the server sends a `project_fs_changed` message for this project and the changed paths include this path, the screen reloads the file, the diff, and the code data. The hook `useProjectFsChanges` subscribes to the channel `workspace:<ws>`.
- If the URL hash is `#edit`, the screen starts edit mode one time after the file loads, but only for a file that has a hash and is not read-only. The Files panel adds `#edit` after the user creates a file.

The size caps and the diff caps belong to [Project files, Git dock, and cloning](project-files-and-git.md).

`web/src/screens/project/files.ts` holds pure helpers that the File screen, the Files panel, and the mobile Files screen share.

| Helper | Rule |
| --- | --- |

| `kindOf` | Returns `Folder`, `Link`, the extension in capitals, or `File`. |

## Edit a file and keep disk changes safe

The File view is read-only until the user presses the pencil. Two writers can change one file: the user in the browser and an agent or a tool on disk. A plain save could overwrite the other change without a warning. `useFileEdit` prevents this. Every save carries the hash that the edit started from, and the server refuses the save when the file has a different hash.

### How an edit works

1. **Start.** `start` copies the disk content into a draft with `saved` set to the same text and `base` set to the disk hash. It does nothing when the hash is `null`, because such a file is not UTF-8 text or exceeds the read size.
2. **Type.** `change` updates the draft. The edit is dirty when the draft differs from `saved`.
3. **Save.** `save` runs only when the edit is dirty, no save is running, and no conflict exists. It calls `api.saveProjectFile` with `{ path, content, base_hash }`.
4. **Success.** The screen takes the returned `ProjectFile`, sets `saved` to the new text, and sets `base` to the new hash. The user stays in edit mode.
5. **Leave.** `discard` on a clean edit leaves edit mode. On a dirty edit, the first press only changes the button to `Discard changes?`. The second press drops the draft.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant Edit as useFileEdit
  participant Server
  participant Socket
  User->>Edit: start edit
  Note over Edit: base is the hash of the loaded file
  User->>Edit: save
  Edit->>Server: PUT file with base_hash
  alt hash still matches
    Server-->>Edit: ProjectFile with new hash
  else file changed on disk
    Server-->>Edit: 409 with issue path base_hash
    Edit->>Server: GET file
    Note over Edit: conflict banner
  end
  Socket-->>Edit: project_fs_changed
  Note over Edit: reload shows a conflict before save
```

The diagram shows a save and a conflict. The 409 answer has an issue whose `path` is `base_hash`. `isHashConflict` checks for exactly that status and path.

### How the hook finds a conflict

The hook also compares the hash when the file reloads. A reload happens on `project_fs_changed`. This compare lets the user see a conflict before a save fails.

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (!edit || !disk || saving) return;
  if (disk.hash === edit.base) {
    setConflict(false);
  } else if (edit.draft === edit.saved && disk.hash !== null) {
    setEdit({ draft: disk.content ?? "", saved: disk.content ?? "", base: disk.hash });
    setConflict(false);
  } else {
    setConflict(true);
  }
}, [disk, edit?.base, saving]);
```

The three branches:

- The disk hash equals the base hash. No conflict exists.
- The hash differs but the draft is clean. The hook takes the disk version without a message, because the user has nothing to lose.
- The hash differs and the draft is dirty. A conflict exists.

The hook does not list the draft text as a trigger. Typing must not run the compare again.

### What happens when

- If a conflict exists, a warning banner offers **Reload** and **Overwrite**. **Reload** fetches the disk version and drops the draft. **Overwrite** fetches the current file, then saves the draft with the fresh hash. The **Save** button is disabled during a conflict.
- If a save fails for another reason, a red banner shows the message.
- If the file is read-only, an info banner shows the reason and **Save** stays disabled.
- If the user closes the tab while the edit is dirty, the hook adds a `beforeunload` handler. The browser then asks for confirmation.
- If the user presses Ctrl+S or Cmd+S outside the editor, the screen saves and blocks the browser save dialog. Inside the editor, the editor command does the same.
- If the user opens another file from the editor while the edit is dirty, the editor shows a message and does not leave. See the next part.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored where | Takes effect | State shown | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Edit mode | Off. Every file opens read-only. | The draft lives in screen memory until a save writes the file. | At once | The `● unsaved` mark, the status bar, and the **Save** button | Press **Done** or **Discard**. |
| Code pane | Open when the code provider reports a language for the file | Screen memory only. It resets when the screen closes. | At once | The active state of the pane button | Press the pane button. |

## Monaco setup and editor options

`web/src/components/monaco.ts` bundles Monaco for the lazy editor modules. The app runs on localhost, so it must not fetch code from a CDN. The file calls `loader.config({ monaco })`, which tells `@monaco-editor/react` to use the local bundle.

### What the file loads

- It imports `monaco-editor/editor/editor.api`, which loads no editing features. It then imports each feature by name: core commands, bracket matching, clipboard, comments, the context menu, folding, hover, the suggest widget, parameter hints, find, multi-cursor, snippets, word operations, and the quick-access commands. The comment gives the reason. The `editor.main` entry also pulls every language worker, so the file does not import it.
- It registers the language definitions for `go`, `java`, `javascript`, `kotlin`, `markdown`, `python`, `ruby`, `rust`, `sql`, `typescript`, and `yaml`.
- It sets `MonacoEnvironment.getWorker` to return one `EditorWorker` for every language.

Import this file only from modules that load with `lazy()`. The import pulls Monaco into the chunk that imports it. `FileScreen` and `DependencyFileScreen` both load `FileEditor` with `lazy(() => import("./project/code/FileEditor"))`. While the chunk loads, they show `Loading the editor…`.

### Language, theme, and font

- `LANG` maps these extensions to Monaco language IDs: `ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `jsx`, `java`, `kt`, `go`, `py`, `rs`, `rb`, `md`, `json`, `yml`, `yaml`, `css`, `html`, and `sql`. `languageOf(path)` returns `plaintext` for any other extension. The table also names `json`, `css`, and `html`, but the file imports no `register` module for them.
- `defineThemes` defines `ostra-dark` and `ostra-light`. The colors are literal values, because Monaco themes cannot read CSS variables. The dark editor background is `#1a1a19` and the light one is `#ffffff`. The diff insert and remove tints also have literal values for each theme. `themeName(theme)` picks the theme name.
- `EDITOR_FONT` is the font family `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace` at size 12.5.
- `EDITOR_WORD_SEPARATORS` is the default Monaco word separator set. The editor uses it for whole-word searches outside the find widget.

### Options of `FileEditor`

`FileEditor` passes these options to Monaco: no minimap, no scroll beyond the last line, no overview ruler lanes, `automaticLayout`, `tabSize` 2, `detectIndentation` on, `fixedOverflowWidgets`, and a line decoration width of 12. The read-only message is the lock reason, or `This file is read-only while you view it. Press the pencil to edit it.`

## Editor interactions: select, jump, find, and view state

`FileEditor` adds navigation on top of Monaco. The editor registers its commands one time at mount. They read the latest props through a ref named `latest`, so they never use stale props.

### Select a name for the code pane

In read-only mode, a plain click on a name selects it. The editor calls `onSymbol` with the word, the line, and the 0-based column. The click does nothing if the user held the link modifier or made a selection. The code pane then lists the usages of the name. The editor also tints each whole-word occurrence of the selected name with the class `code-sym--sel`. The tint search stops at `MAX_TINTS`, which is 2,000 matches, and uses `EDITOR_WORD_SEPARATORS`.

### Ctrl or Cmd click

The link modifier is Cmd on macOS and Ctrl on other systems. `IS_MAC` tests the user agent for `Mac`, `iPhone`, or `iPad`. While the user holds the modifier, the word under the pointer gets the class `code-link` as an underline hint.

A click with the modifier calls `api.codeUsages` for the word, with the path (or the `uri` of a dependency file), the line, and the column. `clickLanding` then decides where the click leads:

| The click is on | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A definition with no uses | A note: `Nothing in the project uses <name>.` |
| A definition with one use | Go to that use. |
| A definition with many uses | A picker titled `Usages of <name> (<n>)`. A `+` follows the count when the list is cut. |
| A use with one definition | Go to that definition. |
| A use with many definitions | A picker titled `Definitions of <name>`. |
| A name that nothing defines | Nowhere. The click does nothing. |

This navigation reads the saved file on the server. It does not see unsaved edits. Completion, signature help, and jump actions send the unsaved text instead.

### Jump actions

`JUMPS` holds two Monaco actions. Both appear in the context menu group `navigation`.

| Action ID | Label (`JUMP_LABEL`) | Key | Target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ostra.showBaseClass` | `Show base class` | Cmd or Ctrl + Shift + I | `supertypes` |
| `ostra.showImplementation` | `Show implementation` | Cmd or Ctrl + Shift + M | `implementations` |

A jump sends the socket hint `code_navigate` with the workspace, the project key, the path, the unsaved text, the line, the column, and the target. The `askJump` function returns `null` when the socket is closed or a newer jump replaced the request. The result is `null` when neither the code index nor a language server knows the name. `jumpLanding` then picks the outcome:

- If the reply has an error, the editor shows the error as a message at the cursor.
- If the reply has no locations, the editor shows `<name> extends or implements nothing that the project defines.` or `Nothing in the project extends or implements <name>.`
- If the reply has one location, the editor goes to it.
- If the reply has many locations, a picker opens. The title is `What <name> extends` or `What implements <name>`, with `(first <n>)` when the list is cut.
- In a dependency file, the editor shows `Base class and implementation jumps work in project files.`

The picker is a design `Menu` that is `PICK_WIDTH` (380 px) wide. The editor places it under the cursor and keeps it inside the editor box. Each row shows `<container>.<name> · <path>:<line>` and the line preview.

### Find, replace, and move line

Monaco binds these keys but does not list them in the context menu. `BUILTINS` adds them to the group `1_modification`.

| Action | Key | Changes text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find | Cmd or Ctrl + F | No |
| Replace | Cmd + Alt + F on macOS, Ctrl + H elsewhere | Yes |
| Move line up | Alt + Up | Yes |
| Move line down | Alt + Down | Yes |

In read-only mode, the three actions that change text start an edit first. The editor calls `onEditAt` with the line, the column, and the action. After edit mode starts, the editor puts the cursor there and runs the Monaco command that `START_ACTION` names: `editor.action.startFindReplaceAction`, `editor.action.moveLinesUpAction`, or `editor.action.moveLinesDownAction`. If the file is locked, the editor shows the lock reason instead. Replace accepts text or, with the regex toggle Alt+R, a pattern whose groups the replacement names as `$1`.

### Go to a place

The function `go` handles every target. If the target is in the same file, the editor selects the name, scrolls it into view when it is outside the viewport, and focuses the editor. If the target is in another file and the edit is dirty, the editor shows `Save or discard your changes before opening <path>, because leaving the editor drops them.` Otherwise, it calls `onOpen`, and the screen opens the target beside the current tab with the anchor `L<line>`.

### Line anchors and line tint

The prop `reveal` tints a line range with the class `code-line--hl`, scrolls to the line, and sets the cursor. A new `n` value in `reveal` scrolls again to the same line. The hash `#L<n>` sets `reveal` through `lineFromHash`, which accepts only the form `L<number>` with or without the `#`, and with a number of 1 or more. The effect for `reveal` runs after the effect that restores the view, so a jump to a line wins over the saved scroll position.

### View state per file

Switching tabs unmounts the editor. The editor therefore keeps the scroll position, the cursor, and the folds of each file in a module-level `Map`. The key is the workspace, the project key, and the model URI. `MAX_VIEW_STATES` is 200. When the map is larger, the editor removes the oldest entry. The editor saves a state only after it restored the state of the same model, because a model switch first scrolls the new model to the top.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored where | Takes effect | State shown | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Link modifier click | Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere | Not stored. `IS_MAC` decides. | At once | The `code-link` underline | Release the modifier key. |
| Saved view state | Last 200 files | Browser memory. It resets on a page reload. | At the next open of a file | The scroll position and cursor of the file | Reload the page. |

## Completion and signature hints

The editor shows completions and signature help from the project code provider, not from Monaco language services. `registerHints` in `web/src/screens/project/code/hints.ts` registers one completion provider and one signature provider for all languages (`"*"`). It runs in `beforeMount`, and a flag makes sure it registers only once.

A model answers only after `bindModel(model, { workspace, key, path })`. `FileEditor` calls `bindModel` for project files. It does not call it for a dependency file, so a dependency file has no hints. A model that is not bound gets no answer.

### How a hint request works

1. Monaco asks the provider for completions or signatures.
2. The provider builds the request from the bound `where` data, the full unsaved text of the model, the line, and the column. Ostra columns start at 0 and Monaco columns start at 1, so the provider subtracts 1.
3. The provider sends the socket hint `code_complete` or `code_signature`. The reply can be `null` when the socket is closed or a newer request replaced this one.
4. The provider turns each reply item into a Monaco item. `KIND` maps the 25 Ostra completion kinds to Monaco kinds. The item keeps the label, detail, documentation, insert text, snippet flag, range, filter text, sort text, preselect flag, deprecated tag, extra edits, and commit characters.
5. If the token is cancelled, the provider returns nothing.

The trigger characters are the same for every language, because one provider serves all of them. The server answers with an empty list after a character that its language does not use.

| Constant | Value | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPLETION_TRIGGERS` | `.` `:` `>` `/` `@` `#` `<` `"` `'` | Characters that open completions |
| `SIGNATURE_TRIGGERS` | `(` `,` `<` | Characters that open signature help |
| Retrigger characters for signatures | `)` | Characters that refresh an open signature |

The socket channel limits, the wait time for a hint, and the language server rules belong to [REST and WebSocket API](server-api.md) and [Code navigation](code-navigation.md).

## Code pane: outline, usages, and dependencies

`CodePane` is the 320 px aside on the right of the File view. It has three tabs and a footer that shows `provider <name>, <language>`. The data comes from the project code provider, which is built in or external. See [Code navigation](code-navigation.md).

The screen opens the pane by default when the provider reports a language for the file. The pane button overrides this. The pane is not available for a binary file, in the `diff` and `rendered` views, or in edit mode.

| Tab | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Outline | The symbols of the file with a kind icon. A click goes to the line. The magnifier button selects the symbol and opens Usages. A warning from the provider shows above the list. |
| Usages | A symbol search box and the definitions and uses of the selected symbol, grouped by file. |
| Dependencies | The imports of the file and the files that import it. |

The pane switches to Usages whenever a symbol gets selected.

### Usages tab rules

- The search box waits 200 ms after the last key, then calls `api.codeSymbols` with a limit of 30. If more symbols match, the tab says `More symbols match. Type more of the name.`
- A selected symbol calls `api.codeUsages` with the path, line, and column. The header shows the counts of definitions and uses. The **Clear the symbol** button removes the selection.
- If the result has a `warning`, a banner shows it. If the list is cut, the tab says `The list stops at the result cap.`
- A row opens its file beside the current tab with the anchor `L<line>`. If the row is in the same file, the screen scrolls to the line. A row with a `uri` opens a dependency file.
- `carrySymbol` and `takeCarried` pass the selected symbol to the next File screen one time. The next screen therefore starts with the same Usages list.

### Dependencies tab rules

The tab calls `api.codeDeps`. Each import row shows the line and the import text. If the import resolves to a project file, a link opens it. If it resolves to a folder, the link calls `shell.browseFiles`. If it resolves to nothing, the row says `external`. The **Imported by** list groups the importers by file.

### Colored text without Monaco

`SourceView` shows read-only text that the code provider colored. The dependency graph preview uses it. The provider sends tokens as a flat array of numbers: `[line, col, len, class]` repeated, with the class as an index into `classes`. `decodeTokens` groups them by line in one pass. It drops a run when the class is unknown, the line is outside the file, the length is 0 or less, or the run starts before the end of the previous token. A faulty provider therefore cannot break the view.

`TOKEN_CSS` maps each token class to a CSS suffix: `keyword` and `attribute` to `k`, `type` to `t`, `function` and `macro` to `f`, `constant` and `number` to `n`, `string` to `s`, `comment` to `c`, and `name` and `operator` to no color. `isSymbolClass` is true for `type`, `function`, `name`, `constant`, and `macro`. It mirrors `TokenClass::is_symbol` on the server. A click on such a token reports the symbol. If the provider sends no tokens, `SourceView` falls back to `colorLine` from the design package.

## Diff pane and gutter change marks

Two views show a change against HEAD. The diff pane shows the full unified diff. The gutter marks show the same change inside the editor. Both read the `FileDiff` from `api.projectDiff`. The server side of the diff belongs to [Project files, Git dock, and cloning](project-files-and-git.md).

### Diff pane

`diffRows(hunks)` in `web/src/screens/project/diff.ts` turns hunks into rows. A row is `add`, `del`, `ctx`, or `gap`. A `gap` row stands for the unchanged lines before a hunk. Its count is `before - prevOldEnd`, where `before` is `old_start`, or `old_start + 1` when the hunk has 0 old lines. The row gets a count of `null` when the number is not above 0. A gap row shows before the first hunk only when lines exist before it. A gap row always shows between two hunks. The row text is `⋯ N unchanged lines`, `⋯ 1 unchanged line`, or `⋯ unchanged lines`. The hunk header text, for example a function name, follows it.

`DiffPane` draws each row with an old line number and a new line number. Each number column is 44 px wide, and a 18 px column holds the sign `+`, `-`, or a space. It uses the classes `os-diff__line--add` and `os-diff__line--del` for the colors.

### Gutter marks and the HEAD zone

`changeBlocks(hunks)` groups the consecutive added and removed lines of each hunk into blocks. A context line closes the open block.

| Block kind | When | Lines the mark covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add` | Added lines only | The new line numbers |
| `mod` | Removed and added lines | The new line numbers |
| `del` | Removed lines only | The line before the removed text, at least line 1 |

The `anchor` of a block is its last marked line. `FileEditor` draws one gutter mark for each marked line with the class `code-mark code-mark--<kind>`. The tooltip reads `<Added|Changed|Removed below> since HEAD. Click to compare.` (`MARK_WORD` holds the three words.)

A click on a mark opens a view zone under the anchor line. The zone is `old.length + 1` lines high. Its first line says `HEAD lines <a>–<b>. Click the mark again to close.`, or `New lines. HEAD has nothing here.` when the block has no old text. The next lines show the HEAD text. A second click on the same mark closes the zone.

The screen passes the blocks to the editor only when the user is not editing. In edit mode, the draft lines no longer match the diff line numbers.

### Mobile line diff

`unifiedDiff(original, modified, context = 3)` in `web/src/mobile/screens/lineDiff.ts` builds a line diff in the browser. The mobile artifact screen uses it for the original and modified text of a document. It works in these steps:

1. It removes the common first lines and the common last lines.
2. It builds a longest-common-subsequence table for the middle part, with one `Uint32Array` for each row.
3. It walks the table to emit `ctx`, `add`, and `del` lines, and puts the deletions of each changed run before its additions.
4. It keeps `context` unchanged lines around each change. It replaces each longer run of unchanged lines with one line `… N unchanged line(s)`.

`MAX_CELLS` is 4,000,000. If `(old lines + 1) * (new lines + 1)` is above that value for the middle part, the function skips the table and calls `replaceDiff`, which shows the whole middle part as one removed block and one added block. The table at the cap uses about 16 MB. The comment in the file gives the reason: a larger table costs too much memory.

## Git dock panel

`GitPanel` in `web/src/shell/GitPanel.tsx` is the Git tab of the left dock. It shows the branch, the fetch, pull, and push buttons, the commit box, and the changes of one project. The server commands, their timeouts, and their caps belong to [Project files, Git dock, and cloning](project-files-and-git.md). The mobile shell has its own Git screen in `web/src/mobile/screens/MGit.tsx`.

### What the panel shows

- A project selector. If the stored project is not in the list, the panel uses the first project.
- **Fetch**, **Pull**, and **Push** icon buttons. **Pull** is disabled when the branch has no upstream and its label shows the behind count, for example `Pull 2 commits`. **Push** is disabled when no branch is checked out. If the branch has no upstream, its label reads `Push and set the upstream`.
- A branch button that opens a menu of local branches and remote branches. The current branch has a check mark. A **Create a branch…** item opens a name input. Enter creates the branch from HEAD with `api.gitCheckout` and `create: true`. Escape cancels.
- A two-row commit message box and a **Commit** button. The button label shows the number of staged files.
- Three lists: `Merge conflicts`, `Staged changes`, and `Changes`. Each row shows the file name, its folder, and the `GIT_MARK` letter in the mark color. A deleted file has a line through its name and does not open. A renamed file stages and unstages together with its `orig_path`.

### Commit rules

The commit button is enabled only when all of these are true:

- The message is not empty after trimming.
- The status has at least one staged file or at least one file staged outside this project.
- No file is in conflict.
- No git command is running and the server does not report `busy`.

Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter in the message box also commits. A commit takes the whole index of the repository. If `staged_elsewhere` is above 0, the panel warns that the commit includes those files too. The **Stage all** button calls `api.gitStage` with an empty list, and the API comment says that an empty list stages every change in the project. **Unstage all** does the same for `api.gitUnstage`.

### How the panel stays current

- The status reloads when the server sends `project_fs_changed` for the project. A throttle limits the reload to one each 500 ms.
- The status reloads when the browser window gets focus.
- The status reloads every `POLL_MS`, which is 10,000 ms, while the document is visible. Edits made outside Ostra send no message, so the poll catches them.
- Each git command (`run`) locks all buttons. If the answer holds a status, the panel shows it. If not, the panel reloads the status. If the command fails, a red banner shows the message and the panel reloads the status.
- The line `Running git <command>…` with a spinner shows only when `running !== "commit"`. A commit shows a spinner inside the **Commit** button and no label.

### What happens when

- If the workspace has no project, the panel shows `This workspace has no projects yet.` and an **Add project** button.
- If the project is not in a git repository, the panel says so and disables fetch.
- If no change exists, the panel says `No changes. The work tree matches <head>.`
- If the status is cut, the panel says `Only the first 2,000 changes of each list are shown.`

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored where | Takes effect | State shown | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Poll interval `POLL_MS` | 10,000 ms | A constant in `GitPanel.tsx`. No setting changes it. | After a rebuild of the console | The status list | Not user-settable. |
| Git operations | Idle | The repository on disk | At once | The result banner under the buttons | Wait for the command to end. The panel has no cancel control. |

## Dependency graph

The Dependencies tab draws the project code graph that the server builds from the code index. See [Code navigation](code-navigation.md) for the index, the graph rules, and the server caps. The browser does the layout, the pan and zoom, the search, and the selection.

### The four views

`GraphView` has four kinds. The screen requests each kind with `api.codeGraph`.

| `kind` | Shows | Request fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages` | Every package of the project | none |
| `package` | The files of one package | `package` (the project top uses `.`) |
| `file` | The neighborhood of one file, 1 to 3 hops | `path`, `depth` |
| `symbol` | The calls, uses, and implementations of one definition | `path`, `symbol`, `line`, `depth` |

The server numbers the columns. Column 0 is the focus. A negative column holds nodes that use the focus, and a positive column holds nodes that the focus uses. Column titles are `File` or `Definition` at 0, `Used by` and `Uses` in the file view, and `Referenced or implemented by` and `Calls, uses, implements` in the symbol view. A title adds `· N hops` when the column is more than 1 hop away.

### Layout

`layout(graph)` is a pure function. It places the columns from left to right in the server order. Then it orders the nodes of each column to reduce crossing links.

1. Sort the nodes of each column by label.
2. Run two sweeps, first from the left column to the right and then back. In a sweep, each node gets the average row of its neighbors as its score, and the column sorts by that score.
3. Split a column that has more than `MAX_ROWS` (10) nodes into lanes. The lane count is `ceil(nodes / 10)`, and the nodes spread evenly over the lanes. A wide fan-out therefore stays on the screen.
4. Place each lane in the vertical middle of the tallest lane.

```ts
// A column taller than MAX_ROWS wraps into side-by-side lanes, so a wide fan-out stays on screen.
const lanes = byCol.map((c) => Math.max(1, Math.ceil(c.length / MAX_ROWS)));
...
for (let ci = 0; ci < byCol.length; ci++) {
  colX.push(x);
  x += lanes[ci] * NODE_W + (lanes[ci] - 1) * LANE_GAP + COL_GAP;
}
```

| Constant | Value | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_W` | 208 px | Node width |
| `NODE_H` | 44 px | Node height |
| `MEMBER_H` | 20 px | Height of one member row inside a focused type |
| `MAX_INLINE_MEMBERS` | 12 | Member rows that a focused type lists in its box. A row `and N more` shows the rest. |
| `COL_GAP` | 80 px | Space between columns |
| `ROW_GAP` | 14 px | Space between nodes in a lane |
| `LANE_GAP` | 16 px | Space between lanes of one column |
| `PAD` | 20 px | Border around the graph |
| `HEADER` | 28 px | Extra top space for the column titles in the file and symbol views |
| `MAX_ROWS` | 10 | Nodes in one lane |
| `MIN_ZOOM` | 0.2 | Lowest zoom |
| `MAX_ZOOM` | 2.5 | Highest zoom |

Only the focused type node lists members. Its height is `NODE_H + 6 + (rows + 1 if more) * MEMBER_H + 6`. Other nodes keep `NODE_H`.

### How nodes and links look

- A node has a color bar and an icon by kind. A package is blue-keyword colored, a file is string colored, a type uses the number color, and a function or method uses the function color. A node of a test file has a dashed border.
- A file or package node shows `<dependents>↘ <dependencies>↗`. A symbol node that is not the focus shows `<n> ƒ` for its members. The badge `N inside` or `+N in file` shows what else a file defines.
- A link goes from the right side of one node to the left side of the other node. If both nodes are in the same column, or the link points left, the link loops around the right side.
- A link is `1.2 + log2(weight)` px wide, with a maximum of 3.5 px. A link of kind `implements` is dashed with a hollow arrow. In the package and file views, a link that is not an import is dashed, and the legend calls it `names only, no import`.
- A long label keeps its last part. `clipLabel` cuts the owner from the front of a qualified name and adds an ellipsis.

### Pan, zoom, and selection

- A drag of 4 px or more pans the canvas. A drag that ends over a node does not select the node.
- The wheel zooms around the pointer with the factor `exp(-delta * 0.0015)`. A wheel delta in lines counts as 16 px for each line. The zoom buttons use the factor 1.25. `zoomAround` keeps the point under the pointer fixed and clamps the zoom between `MIN_ZOOM` and `MAX_ZOOM`.
- **Fit to view** picks a zoom of at most 100% so that the whole graph fits with a 24 px margin. The percent button returns to 100% on the focus.
- A new view centers the focus node at 100%, or fits the whole graph when no focus exists. Moves from code animate. Moves from the pointer do not.
- Hover dims every node that is not a neighbor of the hovered node to 35% opacity. A click selects a node, and a second click clears the selection. A double-click calls `primary`, which opens the package view, the file view, or the symbol view of that node.

### Navigation and search

- The breadcrumbs start with `Packages` and add the package, the file, and the symbol. Each earlier crumb is a link.
- The **Back** button and Alt+Left return to the previous view. The history keeps 50 views. Alt+Left does nothing while the user types in an input, a text area, or an editable element.
- The **hops** tabs `1 hop`, `2 hops`, and `3 hops` show in the file and symbol views.
- The search box waits 150 ms, then calls `api.codeSymbols` with a limit of 20. It also lists up to 8 files from `matchFiles`, which keeps the paths that contain every word of the query and ranks a file name that starts with the first word first. Enter on an exact path opens that file view. A pick sets the view and history and clears the box.

### The details area and the preview

A selected node opens a details area. It shows the chips for kind, dependents, dependencies, and test files, the signature, the list of links with the names that connect the nodes, and lists of definitions (`Methods and functions`, `In this file`, `Also in this file`). A file node also lists up to 80 definitions of the file. These definitions exclude fields, variables, and modules. A click on a definition shows it in the preview. The target button at the start of a row centers the graph on it.

`DefinitionPreview` reads the file with `api.projectFile` and the tokens with `api.codeFile`. It shows the definition range in `SourceView` and scrolls the definition to the top. A click on a name calls `api.codeUsages` with a limit of 1 and moves the graph to the definition. If the definition is in a dependency, the preview says `<name> is defined in a dependency (<path>), which the graph does not show.` If no definition exists, it says `<name> is not defined in this project.` **Open in editor** opens the file at the line.

### What happens when

- If the code index has no source file, the screen says `The code index holds no source files for this project yet.`
- If the server cut nodes or links, a chip says `some nodes or links left out`.
- If the user presses **Rebuild index**, the screen calls `api.codeReindex`, then loads the graph again. A banner says `Indexed N files in M ms.` and adds `The index size cap left some files out.` when the index is cut. If the call fails, a red banner shows the message.
- If the graph request fails, a red banner shows the message.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored where | Takes effect | State shown | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph view and hops | `packages`, 1 hop | Screen memory only | At once | The breadcrumbs and the hops tabs | Press Back, use a crumb, or switch the tab. |
| Rebuild index | Not running | The code index of the project on the server | When the call ends | The banner with the file count and the time | Wait for the call to end. The screen has no cancel control. |

## Dependency file screen

`DependencyFileScreen` shows a file outside the project that a language server named. Examples are a library source in a package cache and a class inside a jar. The screen is always read-only. Its URL is `/w/:ws/d/:key?uri=<uri>`, and its resource ID is `dep:<key>:<uri>`.

The screen calls `api.codeExternal(ws, key, uri)` and shows the file in `FileEditor` with `external={{ uri, name }}`. The header shows the breadcrumbs `<key> > Dependencies > <path>`, a chip with the provider name, a `Read-only` chip, **Ask about this file**, and **Copy path**. The first crumb opens the project beside the file. The ask text reads `About <path> (a dependency of <key>): `.

`LOCKED` is the text `This file belongs to a dependency, so Ostra shows it read-only.` The editor shows it as the read-only message and as the lock reason. The change handler and the save handler are no-ops.

The external mode changes the editor in these ways:

- The model path is `dep:<uri>`. The language comes from the file name, and a `.class` name uses the `java` language.
- The editor does not call `bindModel`, so completion and signature help stay silent.
- Ctrl or Cmd click sends the `uri` to `api.codeUsages`. `clickLanding` treats a click as on a definition only when the definition is in the same `uri`. Navigation therefore continues through the library and back into the project.
- The jump actions show the note `Base class and implementation jumps work in project files.`
- `onOpen` uses `locationId`, so a location with a `uri` opens another dependency screen.

If the read fails, a red banner shows the message and a **Try again** button. The `#L<n>` hash marks a line, as on the File screen.

sections.title: Workspace, settings, and setup screens
sections.summary: How the first-run setup, the setup wizard, the workspace page, the settings editor, and the Cost, Memory, and Skills screens work, with the server code that backs the setup.
sections.body:
A new Ostra machine has no workspace, no model key, and no logged-in harness. Without guidance, the first task cannot start, because no route resolves and no key exists. After setup, a user must also change routing, permissions, and limits without hand-editing TOML files. The screens and the server code on this page solve both problems.

The page covers these areas:

- First-run setup on the server: the onboarding flag, the machine check, and the harness setup terminals.
- The setup wizard with its credentials, import, and clone forms.
- The workspace page with the New task form and the session filter.
- The settings editor with its tabs.
- The Cost, Memory, and Skills screens.

Other pages own the mechanisms that these screens call. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns the settings files, route resolution, save-time validation, and workspace creation. The [Web console shell](web-console.md) owns tabs, routing, the API client, and shortcuts.

## Screen map

The shell owns the tabs and the routing. Each screen fills the center pane for one resource ID. The table lists the screens of this page.

| Screen | Resource ID | URL | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `WorkspaceScreen` | `ws:overview` | `/w/:ws` | `web/src/screens/WorkspaceScreen.tsx` |
| `SettingsScreen` | `ws:settings` | `/w/:ws/settings` | `web/src/screens/SettingsScreen.tsx` |
| `CostScreen` | `ws:cost` | `/w/:ws/cost` | `web/src/screens/CostScreen.tsx` |
| `MemoryScreen` | `ws:memory` | `/w/:ws/memory` | `web/src/screens/MemoryScreen.tsx` |
| `SkillsScreen` | `ws:skills` | `/w/:ws/skills` | `web/src/screens/SkillsScreen.tsx` |
| `Onboarding` | none | `/` and the Run the setup guide again entry | `web/src/screens/setup/Onboarding.tsx` |
| `NewWorkspaceDialog` | none | dialog | `web/src/screens/setup/NewWorkspaceDialog.tsx` |
| `AddProjectDialog` | none | dialog | `web/src/screens/setup/AddProjectDialog.tsx` |

The settings screens share the `Page` column, the `Stat` tile, the `Loading` line, and the `LoadError` banner from `web/src/screens/workspace/Page.tsx`.

## First-run setup on the server

`crates/ostra-server/src/setup.rs` has three functions. `environment` returns the machine check. `onboarding` returns the first-run flag and the workspace count. `create` registers a workspace and marks the machine as onboarded. The route handlers in `crates/ostra-server/src/api.rs` call them.

| Route | Handler | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/onboarding` | `setup::onboarding` | `OnboardingState`: `onboarded_at` and the count of registered workspaces |
| `POST /api/onboarding/complete` | `complete_onboarding` | Calls `mark_onboarded`, then returns `OnboardingState` |
| `GET /api/environment` | `setup::environment` | `EnvironmentStatus`: providers, harnesses, stacks, sandbox, and shell |
| `POST /api/workspaces/validate` | `validate_new_workspace` | A list of `ValidationIssue`. It writes nothing. |
| `POST /api/workspaces` | `create_workspace` and `setup::create` | `WorkspaceDetail` |
| `POST /api/harnesses/:harness/setup` | `harness_setup` | `HarnessSetupTerminal` |

### When the console shows the first-run setup

The `Home` screen at `/` calls `GET /api/onboarding`. It shows `Onboarding` when all three conditions hold:

- `onboarded_at` is empty.
- `workspaces` is `0`.
- The user did not press Skip setup after the page loaded.

A machine that has a workspace never shows the setup at `/`, even when `onboarded_at` is empty. The user can start the setup again with the Run the setup guide again entry of the title bar menu and the command palette. A phone-sized browser shows `MWizard` in place of `Onboarding`. The [Web console shell](web-console.md) owns the mobile shell.

`mark_onboarded` in `crates/ostra-store/src/registry.rs` writes the key `onboarded_at` with `INSERT OR IGNORE`. A second call keeps the first time. Two callers use it: `setup::create` after the workspace is attached, and `POST /api/onboarding/complete`. The console calls the second route when the user finishes or skips the setup. The [Storage page](storage.md) owns the registry database.

### Requests of a first run

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Home as Console Home
    participant Api as api.rs
    participant Setup as setup.rs
    participant Reg as registry.db
    Home->>Api: GET /api/onboarding
    Api->>Setup: onboarding
    Setup->>Reg: onboarded_at and list_workspaces
    Api-->>Home: onboarded_at is null and workspaces is 0
    Note over Home: Home shows Onboarding
    Home->>Api: GET /api/environment
    Api-->>Home: EnvironmentStatus
    Home->>Api: POST /api/workspaces/validate
    Api-->>Home: ValidationIssue list
    Home->>Api: POST /api/workspaces
    Api->>Setup: create
    Setup->>Reg: add_workspace and mark_onboarded
    Api-->>Home: WorkspaceDetail
    Home->>Api: POST /api/onboarding/complete
```

### What happens when

- **The user presses Skip setup.** The console posts `/api/onboarding/complete` and ignores a failure of that call. Then it shows the workspace list. If the call failed, the next load of `/` shows the setup again.
- **The request has issues.** `create::register` writes nothing and returns `CreateError::Invalid`. The route answers with status 422 and the issues. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) lists the creation checks.
- **The write fails.** `CreateError::Failed` becomes status 500 with the message.
- **`attach` fails after `register`.** The route answers with status 500. The registry entry from `register` already exists.
- **`mark_onboarded` fails after `attach`.** The `?` operator turns the store error into `CreateError::Failed`. The route answers with status 500, but the workspace exists.
- **The user has a workspace and no flag.** `Home` shows the workspace list, not the setup.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First-run setup at `/` | Shown when there is no flag and no workspace | Key `onboarded_at` in the `kv` table of the machine registry | At the next load of `/` | `GET /api/onboarding` | Press Skip setup or create a workspace |
| Run the setup guide again | Not shown until chosen | Nothing is stored | At once | The full-screen `Onboarding` | Press Skip setup, or finish the steps |

## Machine check

The machine check tells the user what this machine offers before any workspace exists. `GET /api/environment` returns `EnvironmentStatus` from `crates/ostra-core/src/api.rs`. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns the global config that the check reads.

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `providers` | One `ProviderStatus` for each native provider: `has_key`, `source`, `base_url`, `base_url_source`, and what the browser saved |
| `harnesses` | One `HarnessStatus` for each of the four harnesses: `command`, `installed`, `version`, and `logged_in` |
| `stacks` | The stacks that have a seed reference. The stack inputs suggest them. |
| `sandbox` | `SandboxStatus`: mode, default mode, whether a backend works, and the gaps |
| `shell` | `ShellStatus`: the program the Bash tool starts, or the text that says what to install |

The [Sandbox page](sandbox.md) owns the sandbox status. The [Native tools page](tools.md) owns shell discovery.

### How Ostra detects a harness

`EnvStatus::detect` in `crates/ostra-server/src/env.rs` checks the harnesses in the order of `HarnessKind::ALL`: `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `agy`. For each harness it runs these steps:

1. Read the command from `GlobalConfig::harness_command`. It is the harness name when the configured command is empty.
2. Set `installed` when `which::which` finds the command.
3. When the harness is installed, run `<command> --version`. The call stops after 8 seconds. The version is the first non-empty line of the output, with stdout before stderr.
4. Set `logged_in` with the rules in the next table. A harness that is not installed gets `Some(false)`.

| Harness | `logged_in` is true when | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, or `~/.claude/.credentials.json` exists, or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set, or `~/.claude.json` contains `"oauthAccount"` | Unknown (`None`) |
| Codex | `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set, or `auth.json` exists in `CODEX_HOME` or in `~/.codex` | `false` |
| Grok Build | Never checked | Unknown (`None`) |
| Antigravity | Never checked | Unknown (`None`) |

The code gives the reason for the unknown value of Claude Code. The credentials can live in the OS keychain, which Ostra does not read. Thus a missing marker means unknown, not logged out.

`EnvStatus` stores the time of its check. `stale` is true after 60 seconds. `refresh_env` in `api.rs` detects again only when the status is stale. These routes call it first: `GET /api/environment`, `GET /api/workspaces/:ws`, `POST /api/workspaces/validate`, and `POST /api/workspaces`. The draft check of a new workspace reads `installed_harnesses` from this status, so it sees the harnesses that exist now. The [Harness executors page](harness-executors.md) owns the harness command setting.

### PATH after an install

`extend_path` in `env.rs` adds the folders of the official installers to the `PATH` of the server when they are missing. On Linux and macOS they are `~/.local/bin` and `~/.grok/bin`. On Windows the list also has `~\AppData\Roaming\npm`. `crates/ostra-server/src/main.rs` calls it before any other thread starts, because it writes the process environment. The reason is in the code: a server that starts before an install does not see a `PATH` change that a shell profile makes. With this step, a harness that the user installs while the server runs resolves by name without a restart.

### How the check step shows the result

The Check this machine step of the wizard (`StepCheck` in `web/src/screens/setup/steps.tsx`) shows four groups of rows:

- **Model providers:** `Usable` or `Missing`, with the key source from `keySource`, such as `env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `saved`, or `not set`.
- **Harness CLIs:** `Not installed`, `Logged in`, `Not logged in`, or `Installed`. `Installed` means that the login state is unknown. Each row can have an Install or a Log in button.
- **Sandbox:** `On` when `sandbox.active` is true, else `Off`.
- **Shell for the Bash tool:** `Found` or `Missing`.

The step shows an error banner when no provider has a key. The banner names `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. The rows appear one after the other, with a delay of 350 ms plus 260 ms for each row. Users who prefer reduced motion see them at once.

### What happens when

- **The request for the environment fails.** The step shows a banner with the error and a Check again button.
- **No provider has a key.** The user saves a key in the form below the rows, or sets an environment variable and restarts `ostra`. The step still allows Continue.
- **A harness is not installed.** The row shows `Not installed` and an Install button.
- **A harness is installed and its login is unknown.** The row shows `Installed` and a Log in button, because the console hides the button only when `logged_in` is `true`.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Check again | Runs when the step opens | Nothing. The server caches the result for 60 seconds. | At once | The rows of the step | Press Check again |

## Harness setup terminals

A harness CLI must be installed and logged in before an agent can run in it. A harness setup terminal runs the vendor installer or the CLI login in a PTY on the machine that runs Ostra. The browser streams the terminal and types into it, in the same way as for the terminal of a harness execution. `crates/ostra-server/src/harness_setup.rs` holds the server side. The [Harness executors page](harness-executors.md) owns the launch of a harness for an agent.

### How the server starts a terminal

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["POST /api/harnesses/:harness/setup"] --> B{"Known harness?"}
    B -- no --> C["404 not found"]
    B -- yes --> D{"PTY for this harness and action still runs?"}
    D -- yes --> E["Return the same terminal"]
    D -- no --> F{"Login and program not on PATH?"}
    F -- yes --> G["409 Install the harness first"]
    F -- no --> H["Spawn PTY 100 by 30 in the home folder"]
    H --> I["Return terminal ID and command line"]
    I --> J["Wait for the exit"]
    J --> K["Detect the harnesses again"]
    K --> L["Send harness_status on the home channel"]
```

The request body is `HarnessSetupRequest` with an `action` of `install` or `login`. A harness name that does not parse gives status 404. Every error of `start` gives status 409, with the text of the error.

### The commands

The install action runs the official installer of the vendor. `crates/ostra-exec-harness/src/setup.rs` holds the scripts.

| Harness | Linux and macOS install script | Windows install script |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash` | `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 \| iex` |
| Codex | `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh \| sh` | `npm install -g @openai/codex` |
| Grok Build | `curl -fsSL https://x.ai/cli/install.sh \| bash` | A message and `exit 1`, because Ostra has no Windows installer command for it |
| Antigravity | `curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh \| bash` | A message and `exit 1`, for the same reason |

On Linux and macOS the script runs with `sh -c`. On Windows it runs with `powershell -NoProfile -Command`, with the program from `shells::powershell`. The terminal shows the script as its command line.

Before the script, Ostra adds a `require` check. It uses `installer_tool`, which returns `curl` on Linux and macOS, and `npm` for Codex on Windows. The check stops with exit code 127 and a message that names the missing tool. The reason is in the code: the user then reads a clear message, not the bare "not found" error of the shell in the middle of a pipeline.

The login action runs `login_command`. The program is the command from `harness_command`, so a custom command for the harness applies. The arguments are in the next table.

| Harness | Login arguments |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `auth login` |
| Codex | `login` |
| Grok Build | `login` |
| Antigravity | none |

The terminal ID is `setup_<harness>_<action>`, for example `setup_agy_login`. The ID is fixed for each harness and action, so a second press attaches to the running terminal. The PTY has 100 columns and 30 rows, and the working folder is the home folder of the user, or `/` when none exists. Ostra stores the PTY in the same registry as the PTYs of harness executions, so the console uses the `term:<terminal>` channel and the `term_input` message. The [REST and WebSocket API page](server-api.md) owns the channels.

When the process exits, a task detects the harnesses again, replaces the stored status, and sends `ServerMsg::HarnessStatus` on the `home` channel. A client that subscribes to `home` also gets the current statuses at once.

```rust
// crates/ostra-server/src/harness_setup.rs, in start()
let id = terminal_id(harness, action);
...
if ptys.get(&id).is_some_and(|p| p.exit_info().is_none()) {
    return Ok(out);
}
if action == HarnessSetupAction::Login && which::which(&program).is_err() {
    return Err(format!(
        "Install {} first, because `{program}` is not on this machine's PATH.",
        harness.display_name()
    ));
}
```

Check the command line in the title of the terminal before you press Install. The terminal runs the vendor script with the rights of the user that runs Ostra, and `start` spawns the process directly and does not apply the sandbox.

### How the console shows a terminal

- `HarnessAction` shows nothing when the harness is installed and `logged_in` is `true`. It shows Log in for an installed harness, and Install for the rest.
- `useHarnessSetup` calls the route and keeps the open terminal. When a terminal is open, it listens on the `home` channel. It reloads the machine check only when the statuses differ from the shown ones.
- `SetupTerminalPanel` renders the terminal with `XtermScreen`. Keys typed in the terminal belong to the CLI, so Escape and Tab do not reach the dialog. Shift+Esc restores a maximized terminal.
- The hint under the terminal says that a login can open a browser page on another machine. In that case the user pastes the code from that page into the terminal.

### What happens when

- **The user presses the button again when the command runs.** The server returns the same terminal.
- **The command exited.** The next press spawns a new PTY and replaces the old one.
- **A login starts for a harness that is not on `PATH`.** The server answers with status 409 and the text that starts with `Install`. The console shows it in a banner.
- **The spawn fails.** The server answers with status 409 and the text `Could not start` followed by the command line and the error.
- **The install tool is missing.** The terminal prints the message of `require` and exits with code 127.
