| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Install and Log in buttons | Shown for a harness that is not ready | Nothing. The PTY lives in server memory. | At once | The terminal panel and the harness row | Close the terminal, or press Ctrl+C in it |
| Check again | Runs when a command exits | Nothing | At once | The harness rows | Press Check again |

## Provider and git credentials forms

Three forms save secrets or sessions that the whole machine shares: the provider form, the git credential form, and the sign-in sessions panel. The form fields never receive a saved secret back, because the server reports only that one exists. The [Secrets and credentials page](secrets-and-push.md) owns the sealing and storage of secrets. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns the global config that supplies the default provider settings.

### Provider keys and base URLs

`ProviderCredentials` in `web/src/screens/setup/ProviderCredentials.tsx` shows one panel for each native provider that has a label in `PROVIDER_LABEL`: `anthropic` and `openai`. The wizard check step and the Routing tab of the settings editor use it.

- The form calls `PATCH /api/providers/:name` with `ProviderCredentialsEdit`. An absent field keeps its saved value. An empty string clears it.
- Each Apply sends `base_url`. It sends a secret only when the user typed one. Then it sends an empty string for the other key type, so the provider keeps one key type.
- `KEY_KINDS` has two choices: `api_key` (API key) and `auth_token` (Auth token, Bearer). The form starts with `auth_token` only when a token is saved and no API key is saved.
- Clear saved sends empty strings for `base_url`, `api_key`, and `auth_token`.
- The server accepts only `anthropic` and `openai`, and only when the global config has the provider. Other names give status 404.
- After a save, the server reloads the provider list and returns the new `ProviderStatus`. The console reloads the check.
- The key input is a password field. A saved secret shows the placeholder `Saved. Type a new value to replace it.`

The environment wins over saved values. `ProviderStatus.source` is `env:NAME`, `saved`, `keychain`, `registered`, or `none`. `base_url_source` is `config`, `env:NAME`, `saved`, or `default`. When an environment variable hides a saved value, the panel shows an info banner that names the variable. Server issues for `base_url`, `api_key`, and `auth_token` show on their fields. The [Model providers page](providers-and-pricing.md) explains the providers.

### Git credentials

`GitCredentials` in `web/src/screens/setup/GitCredentials.tsx` fills the Git tab of the settings editor. It lists, adds, edits, and deletes the credentials that git uses for a clone or a pull. The routes are `GET` and `POST /api/git/credentials`, and `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/git/credentials/:id`.

- A credential has a kind (`https` for a token, `ssh` for a private key), a host, a name, and a secret. An HTTPS credential can also have a user name.
- The host can include a path, for example `github.com/acme`. The longest matching host and path wins.
- GitHub and GitLab accept any user name with a token. Bitbucket needs the real user name.
- When the user edits a credential, an empty secret keeps the saved one. The console sends `secret` only when the field has text.
- Import key file reads a private key file in the browser and puts the text in the secret field. The text is saved on the Ostra machine.
- `MAX_KEY_BYTES` is `64 * 1024` bytes. A larger file gives an error. The reason is in the code: a private key file is a few kilobytes, so a much larger file is the wrong file.
- A list with no credentials shows that git then uses the SSH keys and credential helpers of this machine.

The form states two rules for safety. Git receives a credential for each command, so the credential never reaches the `.git/config` of a project or the environment of an agent. The user must give a token or a key only the access that the projects need, because agents run in the same environment. For an SSH key, use a deploy key without a passphrase. The [Project files and Git page](project-files-and-git.md) owns clone and pull.

### Sign-in sessions

`SignInSessions` in `web/src/screens/setup/SignInSessions.tsx` fills the Sign-in tab. It lists every browser that is signed in to this server, the same list for every workspace. The routes are `GET /api/auth/sessions`, `DELETE /api/auth/sessions/:id`, and `POST /api/auth/sessions/revoke-others`.

- A revoked browser is signed out at once. Its next request is refused and its open tabs disconnect.
- The row of the current browser has no Revoke button.
- Sign out everywhere else is disabled when no other browser is signed in.
- The panel names the CLI fallback: `ostra sessions` lists sign-ins and `ostra sessions revoke --all` signs out every browser.

The [Browser sign-in page](browser-auth.md) owns the sign-in rules.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider base URL and key | Empty. The environment and the global config apply. | The machine registry, sealed | At once. The server reloads the provider list. | The panel subtitle, such as `key from env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Press Clear saved |
| Git credential | None. Git uses the machine setup. | The machine registry, sealed | At the next clone or pull | The Saved git credentials table | Press Delete in the row |
| Sign-in session | One for each signed-in browser | The machine registry | At once | The Sign-in tab | Press Revoke, or run `ostra sessions revoke --all` |

## The setup wizard

The setup wizard checks the machine and creates one workspace. The same state hook, `useWizard` in `web/src/screens/setup/useWizard.ts`, drives two hosts:

- `Onboarding` is the full-screen first-run setup. It uses all six steps and has a Skip setup button on the first step.
- `NewWorkspaceDialog` is the dialog for users who have a workspace. It leaves out the Welcome step (`useWizard(true)`) and has a Cancel button. The dialog cannot close when the creation runs. After success it opens `/w/<new id>`.

`ALL_STEPS` in `wizard.ts` holds the steps.

| Step ID | Label | Hint | What the user does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `welcome` | Welcome | What Ostra does | Reads three facts (`FACTS`) next to an animated lane stepper |
| `check` | Check this machine | Keys and harnesses | Reads the machine check, saves keys, installs or logs in harnesses |
| `name` | Name and folder | Where .ostra/ lives | Names the workspace and picks its folder |
| `projects` | Add projects | Folders to work on | Imports folders and queues clones |
| `defaults` | Defaults | Permissions and routing | Picks the permission mode, the routing preset, YOLO, and notifications |
| `review` | Review | Create the workspace | Reads the `workspace.toml` preview and creates the workspace |

Continue is blocked only on the `name` step. The stepper lets the user jump to any step until the creation starts.

### The values and their defaults

`initialValues` sets the defaults:

- `name` is empty. It follows the name of the chosen folder until the user types a name (`nameTouched`).
- `root` is `~/`.
- `mode` is `default`.
- `preset` is `native`.
- `yolo` is `false`.
- `push` is `true`.

`toCreateBody` builds the `CreateWorkspace` request. It trims the name and expands `~` to the home folder that the server reports.

### Name and folder rules

`isChosen` accepts a folder path when it is absolute (or starts with `~/`), has no trailing separator, and has a base name. The folder does not need to exist, because Ostra creates it. The step shows a hint when the folder is missing. It warns when the folder is an Ostra project, because a workspace usually lives next to its projects.

The workspace folder holds `.ostra/` with the workspace settings, the session database, and the session artifacts. Projects are referenced by path and never copied.

### The defaults step

The step offers three permission modes: `default`, `acceptEdits`, and `plan`. The settings editor also offers `bypass`, and the server accepts all four. The step shows a warning banner when YOLO is on.

`presetsFor` decides which routing presets the user sees. Native is always offered. The Codex and Claude Code presets appear only when that harness is installed and `logged_in` is `true`.

```ts
// web/src/screens/setup/wizard.ts
const PRESET_HARNESS: Record<Exclude<RoutingPreset, "native">, HarnessKind> = { codex: "codex", claude: "claude" };

export function presetsFor(env: EnvironmentStatus | null): RoutingPreset[] {
  const ready = new Set(
    (env?.harnesses ?? []).filter((h) => h.installed && h.logged_in === true).map((h) => h.harness),
  );
  return ["native", ...(["codex", "claude"] as const).filter((p) => ready.has(PRESET_HARNESS[p]))];
}
```

If the chosen preset is not offered any more, the step resets it to `native`. A harness preset moves the `implementer` and `write-test` agents to `harness:codex` or `harness:claude`, and the server applies the same rule in `RoutingPreset::apply`. The [Agents, prompts, and coordination page](agents-and-prompts.md) owns the agent registry. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns route resolution.

### Review, validation, and creation

The Review step shows a table of the choices and the `workspace.toml` text that `tomlFor` builds. The text covers only what the wizard decides. The server adds the seeded model routes and limits.

The step checks the request before it allows Create workspace:

1. After each change, the step waits 150 ms. Then it posts the body to `POST /api/workspaces/validate`.
2. The step shows a banner with each issue. The Go to button of an issue opens the step that owns it.
3. Create workspace is enabled only when the check ran for the current body, found no issue, and no creation runs. A change in any value disables it until the next check ends.

`stepForIssue` maps an issue path to a step:

| Issue path | Step |
| --- | --- |
| `name`, `root` | Name and folder |
| Starts with `projects` | Add projects |
| Starts with `permissions`, `yolo`, `routing`, `routing_preset`, or `notifications` | Defaults |
| Any other path | Review |

Creation is one `POST /api/workspaces` call. The checklist rows are `Write .ostra/workspace.toml`, `Create the workspace database`, `Register the workspace in registry.db`, one `Import <key>` row for each project, and one `Clone <key>` row for each clone. The rows advance on a timer of `TASK_MS` (420 ms) and hold on the last import row until the server answers. After the answer, the remaining rows advance every 210 ms (`TASK_MS / 2`).

Clones run after the workspace exists, because the clone route needs a workspace. The console clones one repository after the other with `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/clone`. It shows the git progress lines of the active clone from the `git_progress` messages on `workspace:<id>`. A failed clone does not undo the workspace. The row turns red with the error, and a banner says to clone again with Add project.

When the creation ends, the footer shows Initialize `<key>` for the first project that has `init_status` `not_initialized`, and Open workspace. `useInitAfterCreate` starts the init session with `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/projects/:key/init` and opens `session:<id>`. If that call fails, it opens `project:<key>`. The [Project init and skills page](init-and-skills.md) explains the init flow.

### What happens when

- **The server finds an issue at creation.** The status is 422 with the issues. The step shows them and writes nothing.
- **The check call fails without issues.** The step shows the banner `Ostra could not create the workspace` with the error text.
- **The folder already has a `workspace.toml`.** The server builds on it, so a folder whose registration was lost can be registered again. It ignores the mode, YOLO, limits, tool enforcement, and sandbox settings of that file. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) explains the rule.
- **The folder is a file, is empty, is relative, or is a registered workspace.** The issue is on `root`.
- **The user prefers reduced motion.** The Welcome lanes and the check rows do not animate.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Permission mode | `default` | `[permissions] mode` in `.ostra/workspace.toml` | At the next execution | The Review table and the Permissions tab | Change it in Settings |
| Where implementers run | All native | The `routing` tables of `.ostra/workspace.toml` | At the next execution | The Review table and the Routing tab | Change it in Settings |
| YOLO by default | Off | `[yolo] default` | At the next new session | The Review table | Change it in Settings |
| Browser notifications | On | `[notifications] push` | At once | The Review table | Change it in Settings |

## Import and clone forms

A workspace refers to project folders by path. The import form adds a folder on this machine. The clone form adds a git repository. The wizard and `AddProjectDialog` use both forms.

### Rules for keys and folders

- A project key is lowercase letters, digits, and dashes, and it starts with a letter or a digit (`isProjectKey`). `suggestKey` makes a key from a folder name with the same slug rule as the server. The key names the project in every stage and session folder, and it cannot change later.
- `keyError` rejects an empty key, an invalid key, and a key that the workspace already uses.
- The form expands `~` with the home folder from `useHome`. `useHome` reads it one time with `GET /api/fs?path=~&limit=1` and caches the answer.
- `useFolderInfo` checks the chosen folder with one `GET /api/fs` call, 120 ms after the last change. A newer path aborts the old request. A file or an unreadable folder counts as missing.
- `FolderPicker` lists folders through `GET /api/fs` and creates a folder with `POST /api/fs/mkdir`, which creates missing parents too. The [Project files and Git page](project-files-and-git.md) owns these routes.

### Import form

`ImportForm` takes a folder, a key, and an optional stack.

- The key follows the folder name until the user edits it.
- A folder that does not exist gives the error `No folder at <path>. Create the folder first, then import it.`
- A folder that the list already has gives the error that names its key.
- The stack input suggests the stacks from `EnvironmentStatus.stacks` in a `datalist`. An empty stack means detect from the code. For an empty folder, the stack seeds the first skills.
- With `onAdd`, the button Add project adds the folder to the list and resets the form. With `onDraft`, the form reports the complete project to its parent.

### Clone form

`CloneForm` takes the repository URL, the key, an optional branch, a credential, an optional folder, and an optional stack.

- The key comes from the repository name. `repoName` removes trailing slashes and the `.git` ending.
- The form shows the destination: the folder that the user picks, or `<workspace root>/<key>`. The folder must not exist yet, or it must be empty.
- The credential select starts with `Match by host`. That choice uses the saved credential for the host of the URL, or else the git setup of the machine.
- The branch defaults to the default branch of the remote.
- `onDraft` gets a request only when the URL and a valid key are present.

### How server errors reach the fields

The import and clone routes answer with status 422 and a list of issues. `importErrors` places an issue on `key`, `path`, or `stack`. `cloneErrors` uses `CLONE_FIELDS`: `url`, `key`, `path`, `stack`, `branch`, and `credential`. Other issues join into one general message. An error without issues shows its own message.

### Add project dialog

`AddProjectDialog` adds a project to the open workspace. The Folder on this machine tab calls `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/projects`. The Clone from git tab calls `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/clone` and shows the `git_progress` line. The tabs and the form are locked when a call runs.

The server runs a clone in a task of its own, so a closed tab does not stop git halfway and leave a partial checkout. Thus the dialog says that closing it does not stop a clone that started. When a clone runs, the Cancel button reads Close. On success the shell opens `project:<key>`. The [Project files and Git page](project-files-and-git.md) owns the clone rules and the timeouts.

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project key | The slug of the folder or repository name | `[[projects]] key` in `.ostra/workspace.toml` | At once | The Projects tab | Remove the project in the Projects tab and add it again |
| Stack | Empty (detect from the code) | `[[projects]] stack` | At the next init | The Projects tab | Edit the Stack cell |
| Clone credential | `Match by host` | Not stored. The request carries it. | For this clone | The select in the form | Pick another credential |

## The workspace page

The workspace page is the first screen of an open workspace. It shows the workspace name, the root folder, the project count, the status banners, the New task form, and the sessions table.

### Status banners

| Condition | Tone | Text and actions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `detail.validation` has issues | bad | Says that the settings have N problems, and that an agent whose route does not resolve cannot start. Has Fix it or Fix N when `detail.fixes` has entries, and Open settings. |
| The workspace has no projects | info | Says to add a project to start a task. Has Add project. |
| Some projects have `init_status` `not_initialized` | warn | Says that pipeline tasks cannot target an uninitialized project. Has an Initialize button for each of the first three projects, and Check again. |

Fix it calls `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/settings/fix`. The server applies the fixes that the workspace detail lists, such as a route for an agent that shipped after the settings were saved. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) explains validation and fixes.

### New task form

`NewTask` starts a session. The pipeline stages and tracks are in [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md). The request field, the `@` file tags, and uploads are the context composer, which the [Session screens page](web-session-screens.md) explains.

- **Request:** the text. It must not be empty.
- **Write tests:** sets `options.tests`. The tests are written after every phase passes review.
- **Write docs:** sets `options.docs`. The console then offers a book select. An empty choice means a new book or the book that matches the projects.
- **YOLO:** starts with the workspace default. The form follows a change of that default. A warning banner shows when it is on. The [Judge calls and YOLO page](judges-and-decisions.md) explains YOLO.
- **Track:** Auto (no value), Light, or Full. Auto lets Ostra pick after research. Light has no spec or plan. Full has a spec, a fact-check, and a plan that the user approves before the build.
- **Projects:** buttons that pin projects. They appear only when more than one project is initialized. With no pin, Ostra chooses.

Start is enabled when no call runs, no upload runs, the request has text, and at least one project is initialized. Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) also starts the task. The form sends `createSession` with `request`, `options`, `projects`, `files`, `uploads`, and `docs_book` when a book is chosen. On success it clears the request, the uploads, and the pins, reloads the sessions, and opens `session:<id>`. An error shows in a banner.

The form takes the text of the Turn into task action of the quick dock one time from `useShell().taskDraft`. Then it clears the draft, so a later visit starts empty.

### Pending commands

A folder file can hold commands that changed outside Ostra, such as an MCP server, a language server, a code provider, a format command, an allow rule, or a project outside the workspace. `PendingCommandsNotice` shows one warning line above every workspace screen except Settings. Without it, a command that an init agent or a pull wrote waits unseen. The Settings screen shows `PendingCommandsBanner` with each command. Approve posts `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/approve` with the project and the hash. If the file changed after the user saw the commands, the server answers with status 409 and asks the user to review again. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns the trust rules.

## The session filter

The sessions table lists every session of the workspace. `web/src/screens/workspace/sessionFilter.ts` holds the filter logic as pure functions, so the table and the tests share it.

`SessionFilters` has four fields. `NO_FILTERS` sets them all to their open value.

| Field | Values | Match rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `all`, `active`, `waiting`, `completed`, `failed` | The session status must be in the set of the choice (`STATUS_SETS`) |
| `kind` | `all`, `pipeline`, `init` | `session.kind.kind` equals the choice |
| `project` | `all` or a project key | The session lists the project |
| `text` | Free text | Every word is in the text of the session, in any case |

`STATUS_SETS` maps each status filter to session statuses:

| Filter | Session statuses |
| --- | --- |
| `active` | `running`, `waiting` |
| `waiting` | `waiting` |
| `completed` | `completed` |
| `failed` | `failed`, `stalled` |

A `paused` session is in no set, so it shows only under All. The text match joins the title, the request, the ID, the stage label, the category, and the project keys. It splits the filter text on spaces, and every word must appear.

`filterSessions` returns the matching sessions, newest `updated_at` first. `statusCounts` counts the sessions that each status tab shows under the other filters. Thus the numbers on the tabs change when the user picks a kind, a project, or text. `STATUS_TABS` holds the five tabs and the titles Running or waiting for you (Active) and Failed or stalled (Failed).

`sessionTitle` returns the title that the Classify judge made, or the request until the judge runs. `sessionProjects` joins the projects of the workspace with the projects that any session names, sorted.

The table shows the Request, Stage, Status, Cost, and Updated columns. A row opens the session in a preview tab. The Kind select appears only when an init session exists. The Project select appears only when more than one project key exists. When a filter is on and hides rows, the table shows `Showing N of M sessions`. When no row matches, it shows a Clear filters button.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Status, Kind, Project, and text filters | `NO_FILTERS` | Component state. A reload clears it. | At once | The table and the counts on the status tabs | Press Clear filters |

## The settings editor

The settings editor edits `.ostra/workspace.toml` with forms. It checks the values when the user types and again on save. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns the settings file and the save-time validation that the server runs.

### The form model

The editor does not edit `WorkspaceSettings` directly. It edits a `SettingsForm` from `settingsForm.ts`. The code comment gives the reason: text fields keep what the user typed, such as a trailing newline in a rule list or a half-written model table, and the settings that the editor sends are derived from the form.

`fromForm(form, base)` derives the settings. It starts from a copy of the saved settings, so fields that the form does not know survive. For example, each project row keeps the `code_provider` and `language_servers` that its project had, because the form has no fields for them.

The browser can find some problems before the server does. These local issues keep the base value of the field:

- The Executions at once field must be a whole number. The message says 1 or more.
- The Session budget field must be a number such as `25`.
- A custom model field must not be empty.
- A per-executor model table must have entries of the form `executor = model`.
- An MCP row must have headers as `Name: value`, variables as `KEY=value`, a closed quote in the command, and a timeout that is a whole number.

The [Event log and runner page](event-log-and-runner.md) owns the meaning of the two limit fields.

### Validation, save, and the status text

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Editor as useSettingsEditor
    participant Api as api.rs
    User->>Editor: edit a field
    Editor->>Editor: fromForm derives settings and local issues
    Note over Editor: wait 400 ms after the last edit
    Editor->>Api: POST /api/workspaces/:ws/validate
    Api-->>Editor: ValidationIssue list
    User->>Editor: press Save
    Editor->>Api: PATCH /api/workspaces/:ws
    Api-->>Editor: WorkspaceDetail
    Editor->>Editor: adopt the detail and show Saved
```

When the derived settings differ from the saved ones, the editor posts them to `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/validate` after `VALIDATE_DELAY_MS` (400 ms). A newer edit cancels the older check.

```ts
// web/src/screens/workspace/useSettingsEditor.ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (!dirty) { setServerIssues(baseIssues); setChecking(false); return; }
  let alive = true;
  setChecking(true);
  const t = setTimeout(() => {
    api.validateSettings(ws, JSON.parse(settingsKey))
      .then((list) => alive && setServerIssues(list), () => {})
      .finally(() => alive && setChecking(false));
  }, VALIDATE_DELAY_MS);
  return () => { alive = false; clearTimeout(t); };
}, [ws, settingsKey, dirty, baseIssues]);
```

The form is dirty when the local issues exist or the derived settings differ from the base. `stableJson` sorts object keys, so two settings with different table order compare as equal. Save is enabled only when the form is dirty and no save, no check, and no issue is open. Save calls `PATCH /api/workspaces/:ws`. The server renames the workspace in the registry when the name changed. If the save fails with issues, the editor shows them and opens the tab of the first issue. After a save, a banner says that the next execution uses the settings and that no restart is needed.

The status text next to the buttons has five states:

| State | Text |
| --- | --- |
| A check runs | `Checking settings…` |
| Issues exist | `N problems to fix before saving`, in red |
| The save just ended | `Saved to .ostra/workspace.toml`, in green |
| The form is dirty | `Unsaved changes` |
| The form is clean | `Checked as you edit` |

### The tabs

`SETTINGS_TABS` holds ten tabs. The count badge on a tab shows the issues that `tabOf` assigns to it.

| Tab ID | Label | Content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `general` | General | Name, YOLO default, limits, and Delete workspace |
| `projects` | Projects | The projects table |
| `git` | Git | The git credentials form |
| `routing` | Routing | Executor, model, and effort for each agent, and the native providers |
| `mcp` | MCP servers | One panel for each MCP server |
| `permissions` | Permissions | Mode, tool enforcement, sandbox, network, decoys, and rules |
| `instructions` | Instructions | Text for all agents and for each agent |
| `notifications` | Notifications | The push switch and the browser subscription |
| `shortcuts` | Shortcuts | The keyboard shortcut editor. The [Web console shell](web-console.md) explains it. |
| `signin` | Sign-in | The sign-in sessions panel |

`tabOf` reads the first part of a settings path. The paths of the MCP server list go to MCP servers, and `shortcuts` goes to Shortcuts. The tool enforcement path and every key that starts with `sandbox_` go to Permissions. `projects`, `routing`, `permissions`, `instructions`, and `notifications` go to their own tabs. Every other path goes to General. The [Policy engine page](policy-engine.md) owns the guards that the Permissions tab controls.

### Issues on other tabs and fixes

The editor shows an issue next to its field. An issue that the current tab cannot show gets a place in the banner `Problems to fix before saving`. Each entry has a button with the path that opens the tab and highlights the field. If `detail.fixes` has an entry for the path, the entry also has a fix button. A fix applies to the form, not to the file, so the user saves it with the other edits. `applyFix` handles only the paths of the model route of one agent.

### Deep links to a setting

A URL hash of the form `#setting:<dotted key>` opens the tab of that key and highlights the field. The command palette uses the same hash. `anchorCandidates` lists the element IDs from the most specific to the least specific. A key that names a whole table goes to its panel through `ALIASES`. For example, `permissions` goes to `permissions.mode`. `flash` scrolls the element into view and highlights it for `FLASH_MS` (2400 ms).

### What happens when

- **The file changes when the user edits.** If the form is clean, the editor loads the new settings. If the form is dirty, a banner says that saving writes the version of the user over the file. Load the saved settings drops the edits.
- **The user presses Discard.** The editor loads the saved settings and clears the messages.
- **The check call fails.** The editor ignores the failure and keeps the old issues. The next edit checks again.
- **The server returns issues on save.** The editor shows them, and the form stays dirty.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Save | Disabled until the form is dirty and valid | `.ostra/workspace.toml` | At the next execution, with no restart | The status text | Press Discard |
| Validation delay | 400 ms (`VALIDATE_DELAY_MS`) | Source code | At once | The status text | Not a setting |

## Routing tab

The Routing tab sets the executor, the model, and the effort of each agent. The lead text says that an agent without a route cannot start, so the tab shows an unresolved route when the user edits. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns route resolution and the routing settings.

### Executor and model for each agent

The table has one row for each key of `ROUTE_KEYS` in `web/src/content/agents.ts`: `explore`, `generate-spec`, `fact-check`, `plan`, `implementer`, `code-reviewer`, `execution-path-analyzer`, `write-test`, `documentation`, `system-architecture`, `prompt-generation`, `initializer`, `quick-answer`, `advisor`, and `judge`. `routeKeys` then adds the keys that the file names and Ostra does not know, sorted. A row of an unknown key says that the agent is not known, and that Not set removes it. `ROLE` maps each known key to its one-line role.

- **Executor:** a select with `native` and one `harness:<kind>` entry for each harness. A harness that is not installed has the suffix `(not installed)`. The `judge` and `quick-answer` rows (`NATIVE_ONLY`) show `native only`. The form writes `native` as an absent entry.
- **Model:** a select with `Not set`, `Agent default (<tier>)`, the four tiers of `TIER_NAMES` (`fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, `frontier`), `Model name…`, and `Per executor…`. A model name has the form `provider:model` for the native executor. When the choice is Agent default, the row shows the model that it resolves to for the saved executor.
- **Per executor:** the text `executor = model, executor = model`. The parser accepts a name that matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, an equals sign, and a model. A wrong entry shows `PER_EXECUTOR_HELP`.
- **Effort:** a select with the agent default and the values of `EFFORTS`: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max`. The `judge` row shows `fixed`.

### Routes by phase complexity

The second table sets the route for each phase complexity. The rows are the agents of `COMPLEXITY_AGENTS` (`implementer` and `write-test`) and any agent that the file lists, with the values of `COMPLEXITIES`: `low`, `medium`, and `high`. The subtitle says that the route for a complexity wins over the route of the agent. The `Complexity` line of the phase file picks the route. Work with no phase file counts as low. An empty cell follows the route of the agent.

### Native providers

Below the tables, the tab shows the provider panels. They are the same form as in the wizard. See [Provider keys and base URLs](#provider-keys-and-base-urls) on this page.

### What happens when

- **A route points to a harness that is not installed.** Validation reports an issue on the field. The count on the tab changes.
- **A new agent ships after the settings were saved.** The workspace page offers a fix for the missing route.
- **The file names an executor or model that the list does not have.** `withCurrent` keeps the file value selectable.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Executor of an agent | `native` | The `routing` tables of `workspace.toml` | At the next execution | The Executor cell and the tab count | Set the select to `native` |
| Model of an agent | Seeded routes of the workspace | The `routing` tables of `workspace.toml` | At the next execution | The Model cell and the resolved model | Pick Not set |
| Effort of an agent | The default of the agent definition | The `routing` tables of `workspace.toml` | At the next execution | The Effort cell | Pick the agent default |

## Permissions tab

The Permissions tab holds the mode, tool enforcement, sandbox, network, decoy, and rule settings of the workspace. The [Policy engine page](policy-engine.md) explains the two layers that check every tool call. The [Sandbox page](sandbox.md) explains the sandbox modes, the network choices, and decoys.

- **Mode** (`PERMISSION_MODES`): `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan` (read-only), and `bypass`. `bypass` asks for nothing, and guards and deny rules still apply.
- **Tool enforcement** (`TOOL_ENFORCEMENT`): Use the global setting, Disabled, or Enabled. The Policy engine page explains the guards that this choice controls.
- **Sandbox** (`SANDBOX_MODES`): Use the global setting, Required, Auto, or Off. Required refuses an execution that cannot be sandboxed. Auto runs without the sandbox, with a warning, when the machine has none. Off gives commands the full rights of the user.
- **Network** (`SANDBOX_NETWORKS`): `none`, `allowlist`, `public`, and `host`. The hosts field applies only to `allowlist` and `public` (`takesHosts`). The panel lists the global hosts and the built-in hosts.
- **Loopback** (macOS only): the panel shows when the sandbox backend is `seatbelt`. The choices are every loopback port except the blocked ones, or only the loopback ports listed in the hosts. The blocked ports text accepts numbers up to 65535, separated by spaces or commas, and drops other words. The port of Ostra is always blocked.
- **Decoy files:** one path per line, starting with `~/`. The field is disabled when the server cannot plant decoys. Linux needs bubblewrap. macOS needs an admin account. The panel names the built-in decoys that cannot be removed. `DECOY_GUIDE` links to the sandboxing guide in the repository.
- **Rules** (`RULE_LISTS`): the lists Allow, Ask, and Deny with one rule on each line, such as `Bash(npm run test *)`. Deny beats ask, and ask beats allow. Each part of a chained command is checked on its own.
- **Global rules:** a read-only list from `~/.config/ostra/config.toml`. These rules apply in every workspace, with the workspace rules.

The warning banner `UnsandboxedBanner` shows when the chosen mode runs commands without a sandbox. That is the mode `off`, the mode `auto` on a machine without a backend, or a saved mode that `runsUnsandboxed` marks. The banner lists the four effects in `UNSANDBOXED_EFFECTS`: a shell that walks the disk can read hidden artifacts, a program can read the data folder and CLI sign-in files, a started program can write anywhere the user can, and the network setting does not apply.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `permissions.mode` | `default` | `[permissions] mode` | At the next execution | The Mode panel | Pick another mode |
| `tool_enforcement` | The global setting | `tool_enforcement` | At the next execution | The panel and the global label | Pick Use the global setting |
| `sandbox_mode` | The global setting. It is `required` on Linux and macOS and `auto` on Windows. | `sandbox_mode` | At the next execution | The panel and the banner | Pick Use the global setting |
| `sandbox_network` | The global setting | `sandbox_network` | At the next execution | The Network panel | Pick Use the global setting |
| `permissions.allow`, `permissions.ask`, `permissions.deny` | Empty | `[permissions]` | At the next tool call | The Rules panel | Delete the line |

## MCP servers tab

An MCP server gives agents extra tools. The [External MCP servers page](mcp-gateway.md) owns the client, the tool names, the OAuth flow, and the `mcp_servers` settings. This section covers the form.

`McpSection` shows one panel for each server. A row has the fields of its transport only:

- **Remote server:** URL, headers, and an optional OAuth client (client ID, the name of the environment variable that holds the secret, and scopes separated by spaces).
- **Local command:** a command line that runs in the workspace folder, and environment variables as `KEY=value` lines. `splitCommand` splits the line like a shell, and an open quote is an issue.
- **Both:** a name, an On switch, the agents that get the tools (Every agent, or a list), and the tool call timeout in seconds. A new row starts with 120 seconds.

In a header or a variable, `${VAR}` reads the environment of the Ostra server. A value that the user types is saved encrypted on this machine and shows as `${ostra_secret}`. Keep that line to keep the value.

The panel shows a state chip from `STATE`:

| State | Label | Tone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connected` | Connected | ok |
| `needs_auth` | Needs sign-in | warn |
| `error` | Not reachable | bad |
| `idle` | Not connected | neutral |
| `disabled` | Off | neutral |

A row that differs from the saved server shows `Unsaved`. The panel then asks the user to save before it connects. After a save, `GET /api/workspaces/:ws/mcp` reads the status of each saved server. Reconnect calls `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/mcp/:name/refresh`. Sign out calls the logout route.

Sign in calls `POST /api/workspaces/:ws/mcp/:name/login`. The console opens a blank tab before the call, because a browser blocks a tab that opens after an `await`. It refuses a sign-in link that is not an `http` or `https` address, because a script or data link runs on the origin of Ostra. After the tab opens, the console asks for the status every 2 seconds. It stops when the server is connected or signed in, or after `SIGN_IN_WAIT_MS` (120000 ms).

The tool list shows each tool with its name, its full `mcp__` name, its description, and a read-only chip. The Offer switch changes `disabled_tools`. The panel counts the offered tools, for example `3 of 4 tools offered to agents`. A tool that is off and that the server no longer lists stays in the list. The lead text says that tools run without asking. To ask or deny, add a rule such as `mcp__github__create_issue` or `mcp__github` under Permissions. Plan mode allows only the tools that a server marks read-only.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An MCP server | None | One entry for each server in `workspace.toml` | After Save | The state chip | Switch On off, or press Remove |
| Tool call timeout | 120 seconds for a new row | `timeout_secs` | After Save | The Tool call timeout field | Edit the field |
| Offer switch of a tool | On | `disabled_tools` | After Save | The tool count | Switch the tool off |

## Other settings tabs

### General

The General tab has the workspace name, the YOLO default, and two limit fields: Executions at once and Session budget. The YOLO switch starts new sessions with YOLO on. The [Judge calls and YOLO page](judges-and-decisions.md) explains YOLO, and the guards, deny rules, the fact-check PASS requirement, and security blocks still apply. The [Event log and runner page](event-log-and-runner.md) owns the limit fields, their defaults, and their effect.

### Projects

The Projects tab lists the key, the path, and the stack of each project. A project row leaves the workspace when the user presses Remove and saves. Removing deletes nothing on disk. The server refuses to remove a project that has a live session, a running execution, or a clone, and answers with status 409. Add project opens the dialog of the same name.

### Instructions

The Instructions tab has one field for all agents and one row for each route key except `judge`. Ostra adds the text for all agents first and then the text of the agent to the brief of every agent. Routing settings are never included. Typing `@` tags a project file or a workspace artifact, and each agent gets its path to read. The [workspace and settings model](workspaces-and-settings.md) explains instructions, and the [Workspace artifacts page](artifacts-and-uploads.md) explains artifact tags.

### Notifications

The Notifications tab has the push switch `notifications.push`. The switch applies to every browser that subscribes. Enable in this browser asks the browser for permission and subscribes it. Disable in this browser removes the subscription. A browser without push support shows a message. The [Secrets and Web Push page](secrets-and-push.md) explains push.

### Delete workspace

The General tab ends with the Delete workspace panel. The user presses a button, then confirms. The console calls `DELETE /api/workspaces/:ws`. The server removes the workspace from the registry and deletes `.ostra/workspace.toml` and `.ostra/workspace.db` in the root. Project folders, the session folders under `.ostra/sessions`, and the `.ostra` files of each project stay on disk.

The server refuses the delete with status 409 in these cases:

- A session has the status `running`, `waiting`, or `paused`. The message says to stop the session or wait.
- An execution still runs. The message says to cancel it or wait.
- A git operation runs in a project. The message says to wait.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications.push` | On in the wizard | `[notifications] push` | At once | The Notifications tab | Switch it off |

## Cost screen

`CostScreen` shows the spend of the workspace by session, stage, agent, and executor. The [Model providers page](providers-and-pricing.md) owns the cost formula and the price catalog. This section covers what the screen shows.

The range switch `RANGES` has two values: This week and All time. This week uses `WorkspaceActivity.week_since` from the server, so the totals match the status bar. The week is today and the six days before it. The screen requests `GET /api/workspaces/:ws/cost?since=<RFC 3339 time>`. For All time it sends no `since`. The server answers with status 400 when `since` is not an RFC 3339 time. When the range is This week and the activity has not loaded, the screen waits and sends no request.

The summary strip shows these tiles: the total for the range, Today (the spend since local midnight on the server), This week (only in All time), Runs, Cache reads, Tool calls, `Cache / tool call`, and Build time.

The four tables come from `COST_GROUPS`: By session, By stage, By agent, and By executor. Rows sort by cost, highest first, then by key. A session row shows the title that the Classify judge made, links to the session, and opens it in a preview tab. The key `side-panel` shows as `Side-panel questions`. A stage row shows the pipeline name of the stage, or `No stage` for the key `none`. Agent and executor rows use `MONO`, the monospace style for machine names.

Each table has these columns: Runs, Input, Output, Cache reads, Cache writes 5m, Cache writes 1h, `Cache / tool call`, Build time, Cost, and Share. Cache writes are priced at 1.25 times the input rate for 5 minutes and 2 times for 1 hour on Anthropic. `Cache / tool call` is the cache reads divided by the tool calls. A rising value means that each tool call reads more context again. Build time shows how long agents spend in build and test commands. A cell stays empty when nothing happened, for example the build time of a run with no build.

### What happens when

- **The request fails and no data is loaded.** The screen shows the error with a Try again button.
- **No execution ran in the range.** The screen shows a message and a New task button.
- **An execution runs or ends.** The screen reloads after an `activity` or `session_updated` message on `workspace:<id>`. The reload runs at most every 2000 ms (`useThrottled`).

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Time range | This week | Component state | At once | The tile label | Press All time |

## Memory screen

`MemoryScreen` lists, searches, adds, edits, and deletes the lessons of one project. A lesson is a project fact that an agent records when it cost real effort to find out. Agents recall lessons by area before they work and again after a failure. The user must edit or delete a wrong lesson, because agents act on what they recall. The [Storage page](storage.md) owns lesson memory and its recall ranking. The mobile version of this screen belongs to the mobile shell, which the [Web console shell](web-console.md) explains.

- **Project choice:** with 6 projects or fewer (`MAX_TABS`), the screen shows tabs. With more, it shows a select. The first project is the default. A `?project=<key>` query or a `#project:<key>` anchor picks a project.
- **Search:** the search box waits 250 ms after the last key. Then it calls `GET /api/workspaces/:ws/projects/:key/memory?q=<text>`. The server returns at most 500 lessons.
- **Deep link:** `#lesson:<project key>:<id>` selects that lesson and highlights the row.
- **Add and edit:** both call `PATCH` on the memory route. A lesson without an ID is new, and the server records it with the source `user`. Both Area and Lesson must have text, or the server answers with status 400.
- **Delete:** a confirm dialog says that later sessions do not recall the lesson. The call is `DELETE` on the memory route with the `id` query.

The table shows the Area, the Lesson, and who recorded it with the time.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A lesson | Agents record lessons as they work | The project lesson memory | At the next recall | The Memory table | Edit or delete the row |

## Skills screen

`SkillsScreen` shows the skills of every project in one place. Only skills that `.ostra/project.toml` registers reach agents, through the repo brief. Skills in a harness directory such as `.claude/skills/` appear in the list, so the user can adopt them into `.agents/skills/`. The [Project init and skills page](init-and-skills.md) owns skill files, skill kinds, and the registration rules.

- The list groups skills by project. A project filter and a search box narrow it. `?project=<key>` sets the filter.
- The chip of a row shows the state from `skillState`: the kind of a registered skill, `Not registered`, `File missing`, or the harness folder for a harness skill.
- New skill starts from `TEMPLATE`, a `SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` fields. The name accepts letters, digits, `-`, and `_`, and it becomes the folder under `.agents/skills/`.
- `KINDS` has four values: `creation`, `test`, `convention`, and `other`. Convention skills reach every agent. The others reach the agents that create or test code. The field Use for names the component type, which the brief shows next to the skill.
- Save calls `PUT /api/workspaces/:ws/projects/:key/skills/:name`. Delete removes the entry from `project.toml` and deletes the folder with every file in it.
- A skill in a harness directory is read-only. Adopt into Ostra calls `POST` on the `adopt` route, which copies the folder into `.agents/skills/` and registers it. The harness copy stays.
- A project with a `blocked` message disables Save, Delete, and Adopt, and shows the message.

### For the user

| Control | Default | Stored in | Effect | State shown by | How to stop or change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A skill | Created by init or by the user | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and `[[skills]]` in `project.toml` | At the next execution | The state chip | Press Delete |

## Constants and limits

| Name | Value | What it controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ALL_STEPS` | 6 steps | The wizard steps, in order |
| `FACTS` | 3 facts | The Welcome step text |
| `MODES` | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan` | The permission modes of the wizard |
| `MONO_ROWS` | `Directory`, `Projects`, `Implementers` | The Review rows in a monospace font |
| `PRESET_HARNESS` | `codex` to `codex`, `claude` to `claude` | The harness of a routing preset |
| `PRESET_LABEL` | All native, Implementers on Codex, Implementers on Claude Code | The preset names |
| `PROVIDER_LABEL` | `anthropic`, `openai` | The providers that have a form |
| `HARNESS_LABEL` | Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, Antigravity | The harness names |
| `KEY_KINDS` | `api_key`, `auth_token` | The key types of the provider form |
| `MAX_KEY_BYTES` | 65536 bytes | The largest SSH key file |
| `CLONE_FIELDS` | 6 fields | The fields that get clone issues |
| `TASK_MS` | 420 ms | The time of one creation row |
| Review check delay | 150 ms | The wait before the new workspace check |
| Folder check delay | 120 ms | The wait before `useFolderInfo` asks |
| Version timeout | 8 seconds | The `--version` call of a harness |
| Environment cache | 60 seconds | The age after which `refresh_env` detects again |
| Setup PTY size | 100 columns by 30 rows | The setup terminal |
| `VALIDATE_DELAY_MS` | 400 ms | The wait before the settings check |
| `FLASH_MS` | 2400 ms | The highlight time of a deep link |
| `SETTINGS_TABS` | 10 tabs | The tabs of the settings editor |
| `ALIASES` | 12 keys | The map from table keys to panel anchors |
| `ROUTE_KEYS` | 15 keys | The agents of the routing table |
| `COMPLEXITY_AGENTS` | `implementer`, `write-test` | The agents with complexity routes |
| `COMPLEXITIES` | `low`, `medium`, `high` | The complexity values |
| `TIER_NAMES` | `fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, `frontier` | The model tiers in the select |
| `EFFORTS` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` | The effort values |
| `NATIVE_ONLY` | `judge`, `quick-answer` | The routes that cannot leave the native executor |
| `PERMISSION_MODES` | 4 modes | The modes of the Permissions tab |
| `SANDBOX_MODES` | 4 choices | The sandbox mode choices |
| `SANDBOX_NETWORKS` | `none`, `allowlist`, `public`, `host` | The network choices |
| `RULE_LISTS` | `allow`, `ask`, `deny` | The rule fields |
| `STATE` | 5 states | The MCP state chips |
| `SIGN_IN_WAIT_MS` | 120000 ms | The wait for an MCP sign-in |
| MCP sign-in poll | 2000 ms | The status check during a sign-in |
| `NO_FILTERS` | Status, kind, and project `all`, empty text | The open session filter |
| `STATUS_SETS` | 4 sets | The statuses of each status filter |
| `STATUS_TABS` | 5 tabs | The status tabs |
| `RANGES` | This week, All time | The Cost screen ranges |
| `COST_GROUPS` | 4 groups | The Cost tables |
| `MAX_TABS` | 6 | The most projects that the Memory screen shows as tabs |
| `KINDS` | `creation`, `test`, `convention`, `other` | The skill kinds in the editor |

The Check this machine step and its rows.
