sections.title: Design system
sections.summary: How the `design/` package supplies tokens, React components, icons, the live brand mark, focus helpers, the docs renderer, and the dev gallery to the console.
sections.body:
## Why the design package exists

Without a shared package, each screen of the console chooses its own colors, spacing, keyboard handling, and status wording. Then the screens look different, and a keyboard user meets different focus rules on each screen. The `design/` package (`@ostra/design`) holds one copy of these rules. It has CSS tokens, component classes, React components, an icon map, a brand mark, focus helpers, a Markdown renderer for books, and a dev gallery.

The console in `web/` imports the package for all of its controls. The package makes no Ostra server calls and has no routing. A component receives its data and its callbacks as props. The caller decides what a click does.

The root `package.json` lists `design`, `web`, and `site` as npm workspaces. The `site` folder is not in this checkout. The `description` field of `design/package.json` says that the package serves the console and the site.

### Package exports

The `exports` field of `design/package.json` defines six entry points.

| Entry point | File | What it gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@ostra/design` | `design/src/index.ts` | Every component, type, helper, and icon name. It also loads `index.css`. |
| `@ostra/design/index.css` | `design/src/index.css` | Fonts, tokens, base styles, component classes, and the brand mark styles. |
| `@ostra/design/gallery` | `design/src/Gallery.tsx` | The dev gallery, as the default export. |
| `@ostra/design/docs` | `design/src/docs/index.ts` | The docs renderer: `Docs`, `Markdown`, `Diagram`, and helpers. |
| `@ostra/design/docs.css` | `design/src/docs/docs.css` | Styles for the docs renderer. |
| `@ostra/design/docs-standalone.css` | `design/src/docs/standalone.css` | Tokens and docs styles with no fonts, for the exported HTML book. |

`index.ts` imports `./index.css`. Thus, any file that imports `@ostra/design` also loads the tokens, the component classes, and the bundled fonts. `web/src/main.tsx` also imports `@ostra/design/index.css` directly.

The package depends on `lucide-react` for icons, `@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans` and `@fontsource/jetbrains-mono` for fonts, and `mermaid` with the `mdast` and `micromark` packages for the docs renderer. React 19 is a peer dependency.

### What happens when

- A file imports a component from `@ostra/design`: the page also receives the whole `index.css`. The package has no per-component CSS split.
- A file imports `@ostra/design/docs` without `@ostra/design/docs.css`: the docs components render without their styles. The comment in `design/src/docs/index.ts` says to import both.
- The console runs without network access: all fonts load from the bundle, because Ostra runs offline.

## Design tokens and themes

A token is a CSS custom property (a name that starts with `--`) that holds one design value. The files in `design/src/tokens/` define the tokens. A component class reads a token and never holds a literal color, so a theme change needs no component change. The comment in `design/src/index.css` says that the token files are copied from the Claude Design project. The exception is `fonts.css`, which loads bundled fonts instead of Google Fonts.

`index.css` imports the files in this order: `fonts.css`, `colors.css`, `typography.css`, `spacing.css`, `effects.css`, `base.css`, `components.css`, and `components/brand/brand.css`.

### Color tokens

`colors.css` has two layers. The base layer holds raw colors. The semantic layer gives each raw color a role. Components use only the semantic layer.

- **Base grays:** `--gray-950` to `--gray-10` and `--white`. The grays are warm. The comment in the file lists `#151514`, `#1d1d1c`, and `#363633` as source values.
- **Base blue:** `--blue-200` to `--blue-950`. The accent is Ostra blue `#2459c9` (`--blue-600`). Its dark-mode tint is `#7ea3ff` (`--blue-400`).
- **Base status hues:** `--green-*`, `--amber-*`, `--red-*`, and `--violet-*`, each with a 400, 700, 900, and 50 step.
- **Surfaces:** `--surface-chrome` (title bar, status bar, docks), `--surface-panel` (sidebar), `--surface-editor` (center pane), `--surface-raised` (cards), `--surface-sunken` (code blocks and inputs), `--surface-overlay` (popovers and dialogs), `--surface-terminal`, `--surface-hover`, `--surface-active`, `--surface-selected`, and `--surface-scrim`.
- **Borders:** `--border-subtle`, `--border-default`, `--border-strong`, and `--border-focus`.
- **Text:** `--text-primary`, `--text-secondary`, `--text-muted`, `--text-disabled`, `--text-on-accent`, and `--text-link`.
- **Accent and status:** `--accent`, `--accent-hover`, `--accent-soft`, `--accent-fg`, and the pairs `--ok`, `--warn`, `--bad`, `--info`, each with a `-soft` background.
- **Terminal:** `--term-bg`, `--term-bar`, `--term-border`, `--term-fg`, `--term-muted`, `--term-blue`, `--term-green`, `--term-red`, `--term-amber`, and `--term-cursor`. These stay dark in both themes because they show output of a harness PTY.
- **Code and diff:** `--code-bg`, `--diff-add-bg`, `--diff-add-fg`, `--diff-del-bg`, `--diff-del-fg`, and the syntax tokens `--syntax-keyword`, `--syntax-string`, `--syntax-number`, `--syntax-fn`, and `--syntax-comment`.

### Other token files

- `spacing.css`: the scale `--space-0` (0px) to `--space-12` (48px), control heights (`--control-h-sm` 22px, `--control-h` 28px, `--control-h-lg` 32px), `--row-h` 26px, `--titlebar-h` 36px, `--tabbar-h` 34px, `--statusbar-h` 24px, `--sidebar-w` 264px, `--dock-w` 380px, `--content-max` 1080px, and `--prose-max` 760px.
- `typography.css`: `--font-sans` (IBM Plex Sans) and `--font-mono` (JetBrains Mono), each with a system fallback list. The size scale runs from `--text-2xs` 10.5px to `--text-2xl` 26px. The UI base size is `--text-base` 13px, and prose uses `--text-md` 14px. The role tokens `--type-ui`, `--type-prose`, `--type-title`, `--type-heading`, `--type-label`, and `--type-code` combine weight, size, line height, and family.
- `effects.css`: the radii `--radius-xs` 3px to `--radius-lg` 8px and `--radius-pill`, the shadows `--shadow-popover` and `--shadow-dialog`, the focus ring `--ring-focus`, the easings `--ease-out` and `--ease-in-out`, and the durations `--dur-instant` 60ms, `--dur-fast` 100ms, `--dur-base` 160ms, and `--dur-slow` 240ms. The comment in the file says that elevation uses borders first, and that shadows appear only on floating layers.
- `fonts.css`: `@font-face` rules for IBM Plex Sans at weights 400, 500, and 600 plus 400 italic, and JetBrains Mono at weights 400, 500, and 600. Every face is a `woff2` file with a `unicode-range`, so the browser fetches only the subsets that a page needs. The file is generated from the `@fontsource` packages. Regenerate it when those packages change.

### Dark and light themes

Dark is the default theme. The `:root` rule holds the dark values and sets `color-scheme: dark`. The `[data-theme="light"]` rule overrides the surface, border, text, accent, status, code, diff, and syntax tokens and sets `color-scheme: light`. `effects.css` has a shadow override for light. The base grays and the terminal tokens do not change.

The console sets `data-theme` on `<html>` in `web/src/lib/theme.ts`. The function `resolveTheme` returns the stored value when it is `light` or `dark`. Otherwise it follows the `prefers-color-scheme` media query of the browser, and it falls back to dark.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | What shows the state | How to change it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Theme (`light` or `dark`) | The system color scheme, or dark when the browser gives none | Workspace UI state field `theme`, and the browser `localStorage` key `ostra.theme` | At once | The `data-theme` attribute on `<html>` | Run the command palette action "Toggle light and dark theme" |
| Reduced motion | Follows the operating system | The operating system | At once | Animations last 1ms | Turn on the reduced motion option of the operating system |

[Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) explains the workspace UI state. [Web console shell](web-console.md) explains the shell that applies the theme.

## Base styles and motion

`base.css` sets the rules that apply to plain HTML before any component class.

- Every element uses `box-sizing: border-box`.
- `body` uses `--surface-editor` as its background, `--text-primary` as its color, and the `--type-ui` font.
- Links use `--text-link` and turn to `--accent-hover` with an underline on hover.
- Inline `code` gets a `--code-bg` background and a one-pixel `--border-subtle` border. A `pre` block gets the same colors with a `--radius-md` corner.
- `:focus-visible` removes the browser outline and draws `--ring-focus`. Every focusable element thus shows the same ring.
- Scrollbars are 10px wide with a `--border-default` thumb.
- Eight keyframes define the shared motion: `os-pulse`, `os-spin`, `os-fade-in`, `os-scrim-in`, `os-dialog-in`, `os-slide-in-right`, `os-slide-in-left`, and `os-rise`.

The rule `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` sets `animation-duration` and `transition-duration` to `1ms` on every element. The brand mark has its own reduced-motion rule in `brand.css`, which turns the `live-mark-pulse` animation off.

### Component classes

`components.css` has about 1,700 lines. Each React component renders classes that start with `os-`, such as `os-btn`, `os-chip`, `os-tabs`, `os-menu`, `os-gate`, and `os-term`. The comment at the top of the file says that plain HTML can use the same classes without React. A modifier uses the form `os-btn--primary`. A child part uses the form `os-panel__head`.

## Core components and the icon map

The `core` family holds the smallest controls. Every other family builds on them.

### Button, IconButton, and Kbd

- `Button` has four `variant` values: `default`, `primary`, `ghost`, and `danger`. The source comment says that `primary` is the one forward action (for example Approve or Start), `danger` is for Deny or Cancel execution, and `ghost` is for toolbars. The sizes are `sm`, `md` (default), and `lg`. The props `icon` and `iconRight` add a Lucide icon before or after the label. The prop `kbd` adds a key hint. The icon size is 13px for `sm` and 15px for the other sizes. The `type` attribute defaults to `button`, so a `Button` inside a form does not submit the form.
- When `active` is set, `Button` sets `aria-pressed`. When `active` is undefined, it sets no `aria-pressed`.
- `IconButton` requires a `label`. The label is both the `aria-label` and the tooltip, because the button has no visible text. The default `variant` is `ghost`.
- `Kbd` renders each key as its own `<kbd>` cap. Pass `keys` for several caps, or pass a child for one cap.

### Icon and the icon map

`Icon` draws a Lucide icon at stroke width 1.75 and inlines it, so the icon takes the text color. The default size is 16px. The source comment recommends 14px in dense rows and 12px inside chips. An icon with a `title` gets `role="img"` and an `aria-label`. An icon with no `title` gets `aria-hidden`.

`design/src/components/core/icons.ts` defines `ICONS`, a record from a kebab-case name to a Lucide component. The record holds 129 names. `IconName` is the union of the keys, and `ICON_NAMES` is the list of the keys. The record uses `satisfies Record<string, LucideIcon>`, so the type check fails when a value is not a Lucide icon component.

The icon map is closed on purpose. A component accepts only an `IconName`, so a screen cannot use an icon that the map does not hold. To add an icon, import it from `lucide-react` in `icons.ts` and add one entry to `ICONS`. The Gallery shows each name, so you can check the new icon there.

## Form components

The `forms` family holds the input controls. Each one forwards the standard HTML attributes of its element, so props such as `disabled`, `name`, and `onChange` work as usual.

- **`Checkbox`:** a checkbox with an optional `label` and a `description` line. The prop `radio` makes it a radio button, for single-select open questions. It works controlled (`checked` and `onChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultChecked`).
- **`Switch`:** an on/off toggle with `role="switch"`. The prop `tone="warn"` paints the on state amber. The source comment says to use it for YOLO mode. [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md) explains that mode.
- **`Input`:** a text field or, with `multiline`, a textarea (3 rows by default). It has `label`, `hint`, `error`, `icon`, `mono`, `size` (`sm` or `md`), and `trailing` props. An `error` turns the border red, sets `aria-invalid`, and replaces the hint text. The component links the note to the field with `aria-describedby`. When it has no label, hint, or error, it renders the bare field with no wrapper label.
- **`Select`:** a native `<select>`. The `options` prop takes strings or `{ value, label }` objects.
- **`Combobox`:** a text field with a suggestion list.
- **`FolderPicker`:** a field and a list for choosing a folder on the server.

### Combobox

The caller filters `items` for the query. The list opens when the field has focus, the query has text, and the list has items or the field is not loading. Keys work as follows:

- `ArrowDown` opens the list and moves the highlight down.
- `ArrowUp` moves the highlight up.
- `Enter` picks the highlighted item. With no highlighted item, it calls `onSubmit` with the query.
- `Escape` closes the list and stops the event, so an outer dialog does not close.

The highlight resets to the first item when the query changes. A `mousedown` on the list calls `preventDefault`, so a click on an item does not blur the field and close the list before the click registers. An item can have a `sub` line, an `icon`, a right-aligned `hint`, and a `group`. A group header shows when the group differs from the group of the previous item, so sort the items by group first. When a non-empty query matches nothing, the list shows `empty` (default `No matches`).

### FolderPicker

The path field drives the listing. A value that ends with a separator means that the user is browsing that folder. A value with no trailing separator is the chosen folder. The picker has two modes:

- **With `list`:** the picker loads listings itself. It lists the directory part of the typed path after `debounceMs` (default 120ms). A new request aborts the previous one with an `AbortController`, and the picker ignores a late answer from an aborted request. When the answer for the current path is missing, the picker shows a spinner.
- **Without `list`:** the caller controls browsing. It passes `browsePath`, `entries`, `parent`, `missing`, `nearest`, and `onBrowse`.

The shape `FolderListing` matches the reply of `GET /api/fs?path=` (the source comment calls it backend proposal 19). [Project files, Git dock, and cloning](project-files-and-git.md) explains the server side of folder browsing. The type `FolderLister` is a function with an optional second parameter: `(path, init?: { signal?: AbortSignal }) => Promise<FolderListing>`. The picker passes `{ signal }` from its `AbortController` on each call. A lister that ignores `init` still works, but the picker then cannot cancel the request on the network.

The typed name after the last separator filters the entries. Entries that start with the name come first. Entries that only contain the name come next. These keys work in the field:

- `Tab` completes the highlighted match.
- `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` pick a match.
- `Enter` enters the highlighted match when a name is typed. Otherwise it chooses the listed folder, unless the folder is missing.
- `Backspace` right after a separator goes up one folder.

The defaults are `initialPath` `~` and `height` 220px for the list. A relative path shows the error "Type an absolute path, starting with / or ~/." A missing folder shows "No folder at <path>.", disables the button "Use this folder", and offers a row for the nearest folder that exists. When the caller passes `mkdir`, a typed path that does not exist offers a row "Create". The `mkdir` function must work like `mkdir -p`: it creates missing parent folders too. A failure of `mkdir` stores its message in `createError`. The picker renders that message inside the `os-picker__list` container, after the Create row.

The path helpers are exported for other code: `isWindowsPath`, `isAbsolutePath`, `endsWithSep`, `trimSep`, `withSep`, `baseName`, and `splitPath`. They handle Windows paths with three module constants: `DRIVE` (`^[A-Za-z]:`), `DRIVE_NAME` (`^[A-Za-z]:$`), and `DRIVE_ROOT` (`^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]$`). A Windows path starts with a drive letter, or with `~` when the home folder is a Windows path. Both `\` and `/` separate its parts. On a Windows server, the path `/` is the list of drives. A bare drive such as `C:` filters that list, and the parent of a drive root is `/`. The tests in `design/src/forms.test.tsx` cover these cases.

## Data and feedback components

The `data` family shows information. The `feedback` family tells the user what state the system is in.

### Data components

- **`Panel`:** the only card shape. It is a bordered section with an optional header (minimum height 36px) that holds an `icon`, a `title`, a `subtitle`, and `actions`. The `tone` prop (`highlight`, `warn`, or `bad`) changes the border. `flush` removes the background. `bodyFlush` removes the body padding, for tables and lists.
- **`SectionLabel`:** an uppercase group label in 10.5px text.
- **`Table`:** a dense table with `columns` (`key`, `label`, `num`, `width`, `render`) and `rows`. A column with `num` aligns right and uses tabular mono numbers, for cost, tokens, and durations. The prop `rowKey` names the key field (default `id`), and a row with no key uses its index. The prop `onRowClick` makes rows clickable, and `Enter` on a focused row opens it. The prop `selectedKey` marks one row. An empty `rows` list shows `empty` (default `Nothing yet.`).
- **`CodeView`:** a read-only source view with line numbers and light syntax color.

#### CodeView rules

`CodeView` is not a full highlighter. A regular expression splits each line into a comment, a string, a number, a name followed by `(`, and a plain word. The classes are `os-tok-c` (comment), `os-tok-s` (string), `os-tok-n` (number), `os-tok-k` (keyword), `os-tok-f` (function call), and `os-tok-t` (a word that matches the constant `TYPES`, `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`). A `//` starts a comment unless the language is `sql`. A `#` starts a comment for `toml`, `sh`, and `py`. A `--` starts a comment for `sql`. The languages `md` and `txt` get no color. The `language` prop accepts `rs`, `ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `sql`, `toml`, `sh`, `md`, and `txt`.

A line can have only one mark. The priority is `highlight` (a finding or a search hit), then `added`, then `removed`. The prop `startLine` sets the first line number, and `flush` removes the border and background for a full-pane viewer. The function `colorLine` is exported, so another view can color one line the same way.

### Feedback components

- **`Chip`:** a small label. The `Tone` type has six values: `neutral`, `accent`, `ok`, `warn`, `bad`, and `info`. The props `mono` (ids, models, rule names), `outline`, and `icon` (11px) change the look.
- **`StatusDot`:** a dot with a `tone`. The prop `pulse` adds a slow pulse for a live state. The prop `hollow` draws an outline for a pending state. The default size is 7px.
- **`Spinner`:** a rotating ring (default 12px) with `role="status"` and the label `Loading`.
- **`Banner`:** a notice with a `tone` (`warn` by default, `bad`, `info`, or `neutral`), an optional `title`, and `actions`. The tone sets the default icon: `triangle-alert` for `warn`, `octagon-alert` for `bad`, and `info` for the other two. A `bad` banner has `role="alert"`. The others have `role="status"`. The source comment says that `warn` marks YOLO on or a project that is not initialized, `bad` marks invalid settings, errors, and security blocks, and a security block never gets a dismiss action.
- **`Dialog`:** a modal dialog.
- **`StatusChip`:** a `Chip` whose tone and text come from a backend status value.

#### Dialog rules

`Dialog` renders into `document.body` through a portal. The default `width` is 560px. These rules apply:

- The dialog closes on the close button, on `Escape`, and on a click that starts and ends on the scrim. A drag that starts in a field and ends on the scrim does not close it, because the dialog tracks where the mouse button went down. The test `feedback.test.tsx` checks this rule.
- A dialog with no `onClose` must be answered. It has no close button, and `Escape` does nothing.
- On open, focus moves to `initialFocus` or to the first focusable element. `Tab` stays inside the dialog. On close, focus returns to the element that had it before. The hook `useFocusTrap` does this work. The part "Focus and keyboard helpers" below explains it.
- With `inline`, the dialog renders as a panel with no scrim, no fixed position, no animation, and no focus trap. The source comment says that this form is for docs and cards.

#### StatusChip tones and labels

`StatusChip` takes a `kind` and a `status`. The constant `TONES` maps each pair to a tone. An unknown status gets the `neutral` tone. The label is the status with a capital first letter and spaces in place of underscores, unless the constant `LABELS` holds a special text. The function `statusTone(kind, status)` is exported, so a row or a dot can use the same tone.

| Kind | Status to tone |
| --- | --- |
| `session` | `running` accent, `waiting` warn, `completed` ok, `failed` bad, `stalled` bad, `paused` neutral |
| `execution` | `running` accent, `ok` ok, `stuck` warn, `handoff` info, `waiting` info, `error` bad, `denied` bad, `interrupted` warn, `cancelled` neutral |
| `stage` | `pending` neutral, `running` accent, `waiting` warn, `done` ok, `skipped` neutral, `failed` bad, `blocked` bad |
| `phase` | `queued` neutral, `implementing` accent, `reviewing` accent, `passed` ok, `blocked` bad, `removed` bad |
| `init` | `initialized` ok, `not_initialized` warn, `initializing` accent, `missing` bad |

The special labels are `Waiting for you` for a `session` that is `waiting`, `Not initialized` for `init` `not_initialized`, and `Folder missing` for `init` `missing`. The kind and status names come from the backend. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) explains the stage and phase states. [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md) explains the session and execution states.

## Navigation components

The `navigation` family moves the user through resources, files, and steps. Most of these components handle the keyboard in the same way: arrow keys, `Home`, and `End` through the helper `arrowIndex`.

### Tabs

`Tabs` is a controlled strip (`value` and `onChange`). The `variant` prop has three values: `underline` (default, for sections of a page), `bar` (editor tabs with close and pin buttons), and `segmented` (compact toggles). Each tab has an `id`, a `label`, and optional `icon`, `count`, `dot`, `italic`, `pinned`, and `title`. An italic label marks a preview tab that the next open replaces.

- Only the selected tab is a tab stop (`tabIndex` 0). The arrow keys move focus and select the tab. They wrap at the ends.
- `Enter` or `Space` selects the focused tab. `Delete` closes the focused tab in the `bar` variant when `onClose` exists.
- With `onMove` in the `bar` variant, tabs are draggable. A drop on the left half of a tab puts the dragged tab before it. A drop on the right half puts it after. `Ctrl+Shift+Left` or `Ctrl+Shift+Right` (or `Cmd` on macOS) moves the focused tab by one place. Without `onMove`, none of this works.
- A pinned tab shows a pin button in place of the close button. The button calls `onUnpin`.
- A strip that is wider than its box scrolls sideways. A vertical mouse wheel scrolls it sideways, except in the `segmented` variant. The function `revealSelectedTab` moves the strip so that the selected tab is in view. It does not use `scrollIntoView`, because that call also scrolls every ancestor, including a page that frames the console.

### Menu and ContextMenu

`Menu` is a dropdown. Place it in a `position: relative` wrapper next to its trigger. An item is an action, a `{ type: "divider" }`, or a `{ type: "heading", label }`. An action can have `sub`, `icon` (a name or an element), `hint`, `kbd`, `checked`, `danger`, `indent`, and `active`. An action with `checked` set becomes `menuitemradio`.

When the menu opens, focus moves to the first item. The arrow keys, `Home`, and `End` move focus. `Enter` or `Space` selects. `Escape` and `Tab` close the menu. A click on the scrim closes it. On close, focus returns to the previous element only when focus fell to the page body. If the user moved focus to another element, the menu leaves it there.

`ContextMenu` opens a `Menu` at the viewport point `at` (for example a right click). It has a default `width` of 220px. The constant `MARGIN` is 8px. The menu keeps this margin from each edge of the viewport. The height of the menu is estimated as 30px for each item plus 8px. A null `at` renders nothing.

### CommandPalette

`CommandPalette` is the resource switcher (`Cmd+K`). It renders into `document.body` when `open` is true and returns nothing when closed. Items are grouped by `group`, so sort them first. The built-in filter `filterPaletteItems` keeps each item whose label, hint, or group contains the query, ignoring case, in the original order. Pass `filterItems` to replace the filter when the server already matched the items. The prop `onQueryChange` receives each keystroke, for callers that search a server.

The panel is 560px wide, with a list that is at most 360px high. The input has focus on open. The arrow keys move the highlight and clamp at the ends. `Enter` opens the highlighted item and closes the palette. `Escape` and a click on the scrim close it. On close, focus returns to the element that opened it. When nothing matches, the list shows `Nothing matches “<query>”.` [Web console shell](web-console.md) explains the shortcut system and the palette items of the console.

### Tree components

- **`TreeItem`:** one row of the sidebar tree. Each depth level indents 14px. The prop `expanded` (true or false) adds a chevron. Omit it for a leaf. `Enter` or `Space` activates the row. `ArrowRight` opens a closed row, and `ArrowLeft` closes an open row. `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` move focus to the next row of the same tree.
- **`TreeSection`:** an uppercase group header with optional `actions`.
- **`FileTree`:** the rows of a folder tree that the caller loads one folder at a time. The caller answers `folder(dir)` for each open folder. The component shows `Reading…` when a folder has no entries and no error, and it shows the error text when loading failed. Folders come before files, and each group sorts with `localeCompare`. It supports drag start, drop targets (`dropEffect` returns `copy`, `move`, or null), a context menu, per-row look (`row`), and an inline name field for a new file or folder.
- **`NewEntryField`:** the inline name field. `Enter` creates, and `Escape` or a blur with an empty name cancels. The component trims slashes from both ends of the name.

#### Why FileTree needs role="tree"

Put `FileTree` inside an element with `role="tree"`. The function `moveFocus` in `design/src/components/navigation/TreeItem.tsx` scopes `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` to `closest('[role="tree"]')`. Without a tree element, it falls back to the parent of the enclosing `role="group"`. If no group exists either, it uses the parent of the row. In both fallbacks, arrow-key movement has a narrower scope, and focus cannot reach rows outside that parent.

#### File icons

The constant `FILE_ICON` in `FileTree.tsx` maps an extension to an icon, and `fileIcon(path)` reads it. The extensions `rs`, `ts`, `tsx`, `js`, `jsx`, `py`, `go`, `java`, and `kt` use `file-code-2`. `sql` uses `database`. `toml`, `yaml`, and `yml` use `file-cog`. `json` uses `file-json`. `md` and `txt` use `file-text`. Any other file, and any name that starts with a dot and has no other dot, uses `file`. The helpers `parentDir` and `dragHasFiles` are also exported. [Project, Files, and dependency screens](web-project-screens.md) explains the Files view that uses these components.

### Breadcrumbs and Stepper

- **`Breadcrumbs`:** the path of the open resource. Every crumb except the last navigates, with a click or with `Enter`. The last crumb has `aria-current="page"`.
- **`Stepper`:** wizard progress. Steps before `current` are done and show a check mark. A done step is clickable and calls `onSelect` with its index. The vertical form shows labels and hints. The horizontal form is a compact bar that shows only the label of the current step. [Workspace, settings, and setup screens](web-workspace-and-setup.md) explains the wizard that uses it.

## Pipeline components

The `pipeline` family shows the session pipeline: lanes, stages, phases, gates, decisions, executions, tool calls, and terminal output. These components know the vocabulary of Ostra, but they take plain props. The caller maps backend data to the props.

### LaneStepper and StageRow

`LaneStepper` is a horizontal strip of nine lanes. The constant `LANE_ORDER` fixes the order: `research`, `requirements`, `verification`, `design`, `build`, `review`, `test`, `docs`, and `done`. The constant `TITLES` gives the display names. The prop `lanes` is a partial record. A lane with no entry shows as `pending`.

Each `LaneState` has a `status`, an optional one-line `detail` (such as `3 docs` or `Phase 2 of 4`), and an optional `why` that becomes the tooltip. The statuses and their marks are in this list:

- `pending`: no mark.
- `current`: a pulsing accent dot.
- `waiting`: the `hand` icon in the warn color.
- `done`: the `check` icon in the ok color.
- `failed`: the `x` icon in the bad color.
- `skipped`: the `minus` icon in the muted text color.

The arrow keys, `Home`, and `End` move focus between lanes and select them. [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md) explains the lanes and stages.

#### ICON and ICON_COLOR

Two constants in `design/src/components/pipeline/LaneStepper.tsx` draw the lane marks.

- `ICON` is a `Record<LaneState["status"], IconName | null>`. It maps each lane status to an icon name, or to null when the lane has no icon.
- `ICON_COLOR` is a `Partial<Record<LaneState["status"], string>>`. It maps a status to the CSS color of its icon.

| Status | `ICON` value | `ICON_COLOR` value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `done` | `check` | `var(--ok)` |
| `current` | null (a pulsing dot replaces the icon) | none |
| `waiting` | `hand` | `var(--warn)` |
| `failed` | `x` | `var(--bad)` |
| `skipped` | `minus` | none |
| `pending` | null | none |

A status with an icon but no `ICON_COLOR` entry gets `var(--text-muted)`. Only `skipped` has this case. `LaneStepper` draws each icon at 11px.

`StageRow` is one stage inside a lane. Its status has seven values: `pending`, `running`, `waiting`, `done`, `skipped`, `failed`, and `blocked`. The dot is ok for `done`, accent and pulsing for `running`, warn for `waiting`, bad for `failed` and `blocked`, and hollow for `skipped` and `pending`. A skipped row has its own style. When `onClick` exists, the row is a button that opens on `Enter` or `Space`.

### PhaseDag and PhaseNode

`PhaseDag` takes `layers`, a list of columns. Each column holds phases that depend only on phases in columns to their left. The first column has the label `No dependencies`. The later columns are labeled `Step 2`, `Step 3`, up to the last column.

`PhaseNode` shows one phase: its id, title, project chip, complexity (`low`, `medium`, or `high`), test policy (`Required`, `Optional`, or `Skip`), deliverable, a `StatusChip` of kind `phase`, the review pass number when it is above 0, a `security block` chip, and the ids of the phases it depends on. The test policy chip is outlined and neutral for `Skip`, and accent for the other values.

### GateCard

A gate is a point where the pipeline waits for the user. `GateCard` is the shell for every gate: a header with an icon and a title, an explanation, then either the answer form (`children` and `actions`) or the recorded answer. The header chip says `Waiting for you` when the gate is open. After the user or YOLO answers the gate, the chip says `Answered by you` or `Answered by Ostra (YOLO)`, and the card shows `answer` and, when it exists, `Reason: <reason>`.

The type `GateKind` has 13 values. The constant `KIND_ICON` maps each to an icon:

| Gate kind | Icon |
| --- | --- |
| `open_questions` | `message-circle-question` |
| `spec_approval` | `file-check` |
| `plan_approval` | `list-checks` |
| `permission` | `shield-alert` |
| `review_cap` | `repeat` |
| `stuck` | `life-buoy` |
| `phase_blocked` | `octagon-x` |
| `closing_gate` | `flag` |
| `skill_approval` | `book-check` |
| `harness_failure` | `plug-zap` |
| `execution_failed` | `circle-x` |
| `budget_reached` | `coins` |
| `fact_check_recurring` | `refresh-ccw` |

The `kind` prop also accepts any other string. A kind that the table does not list gets the `circle-pause` icon. Thus, a console that is older than the server still shows a new gate kind. [Session, execution, and gate screens](web-session-screens.md) explains the gate forms and answer kinds.

### Decision

`Decision` shows a judge decision as a sentence: "Ostra chose <choice> because <reason>". The `reason` prop must start in lowercase, because it follows the word "because". The header has a chip with the judge name, an optional time, an `Overridden by you` chip, and an `Override` button. When `canOverride` is false, the button becomes the text `Settled`, with the tooltip "Work that depends on this decision has already started". The optional `basis` line starts with `Based on:`. [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md) explains the decisions and the override rule.

### ExecutionGroup

An execution is one run of an agent. `ExecutionGroup` lists the executions of one agent in one project as a collapsible group. The group is open by default when any run has the status `running`. The header shows the agent name, the project chip, the run count, one chip for each executor, and the total cost. The total sums each `cost` string after it removes the `$` sign, and a cost that does not parse counts as 0. A group with one run renders as a single plain row. A run with the executor `native` shows the `activity` icon, and any other executor shows `square-terminal`. A running run shows a spinner. The constant `DOT` maps the nine run statuses to the same tones as the `execution` row of the `StatusChip` table. [Native executor loop](native-executor.md) and [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) explain the two kinds of executor.

### ToolCall, DiffView, and Terminal

- **`ToolCall`:** one tool call in the Activity stream of a native execution, with its policy decision. The `PolicyInfo` has a `decision` (`allow`, `ask`, or `deny`), a `layer` (`guard` for layer 1 or `permission` for layer 2), a `rule`, an optional `reason`, and an optional `advice`. A denied or asked call opens by default. A denied call shows the chip `Denied`. An asked call that is not done shows `Asking you`. An error that is not a denial shows `Error`. The body shows "Denied by <layer> rule <rule>" or "Needs permission by <layer> rule <rule>", then the reason and the line "What to do instead:". The constant `TOOL_ICON` maps tool names to icons: `Read` to `file`, `Write` to `file-plus`, `Edit` to `file-diff`, `Bash` to `square-terminal`, `Grep` to `text-search`, `Glob` to `folder-search`, `WebFetch` to `globe`, `WebSearch` to `search`, `Skill` to `book-open`, `Report` to `file-check`, and `Memory` and `MemoryRecall` to `brain`. Any other tool gets `wrench`. [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) explains the layers and rules.
- **`DiffView`:** unified diff lines. Each `DiffLine` has a `type` (`add`, `del`, or `ctx`) and `text`. The sign column shows `+`, `-`, or a space.
- **`Terminal`:** the pane for a harness execution. It has a bar with the title, the meta text, and the state (`Live` or `Session ended`). The body is either static `lines` or the `children` slot. The slot holds a live xterm.js host element, and the component then ignores `lines`. Each static line has a `TerminalTone`: empty, `muted`, `fn`, `ok`, `add`, `bad`, `del`, or `warn`. In static mode with `live`, the pane shows a cursor and follows new output. If the user scrolls up more than 24px from the bottom, the pane stops following and shows a `Follow output` button. With `interactive` and `live`, an input row sends typed text to `onInput`. The default height is 420px. [Session, execution, and gate screens](web-session-screens.md) explains the terminal on the execution screen.

## The live brand mark

The brand mark shows session progress in one small icon. Without it, the user must open a session to see whether work is running, waiting, or failed. `LiveMark` draws the mark as an SVG. `markSvg` draws the same mark as a standalone SVG string, for the browser tab icon. The file is `design/src/components/brand/LiveMark.tsx`.

The mark is a rounded square tile with eight arcs around a center circle. The center circle is the pearl. Each arc is one board lane from `research` to `docs`. The `done` lane has no arc. The type `MarkState` is `{ arcs: MarkArc[]; pearl: MarkPearl | null }`. The constant `MARK_ARCS` is 8.

- `MarkArc` values: `done`, `run`, `wait`, `fail`, and `off`.
- `MarkPearl` values: `run`, `wait`, `fail`, `ok`, `rest`, and `off`. A pearl of `off` or null is hidden.
- `REST`: all arcs `done` and the pearl `rest`. The console shows it as the static logo.
- `IDLE`: all arcs `off` and no pearl. The console uses it when no session is open.

### Arc geometry

The viewBox is 32 by 32. The arcs sit on a circle of radius `R` 9.5 around the point 16,16. Each arc starts at the top (-90 degrees) and runs clockwise. An arc covers 45 degrees minus a gap of `GAP` 4.5 degrees on each side, so it draws 36 degrees. The constant `ARC_D` holds the eight path strings.

```ts
const R = 9.5;
const GAP = 4.5;
const pt = (deg: number) => {
  const t = (deg * Math.PI) / 180;
  return `${(16 + R * Math.cos(t)).toFixed(2)} ${(16 + R * Math.sin(t)).toFixed(2)}`;
};
const ARC_D = Array.from(
  { length: MARK_ARCS },
  (_, i) => `M${pt(-90 + i * 45 + GAP)}A${R} ${R} 0 0 1 ${pt(-90 + (i + 1) * 45 - GAP)}`,
);
```

### Colors and animation

`LiveMark` reads its colors from CSS variables through the constant `CSS_PAL`, so it follows the theme. A favicon cannot read CSS variables. Thus, `markSvg` uses the constant `PAL`, which holds literal colors for `dark` and `light`. The state `run` uses the `done` color (the accent). The state `wait` uses `--warn`, `fail` uses `--bad`, and `ok` uses `--ok`.

Each arc draws over an `off` colored track. When an arc leaves `off`, it draws clockwise through a `stroke-dashoffset` transition. The prop `draw` sets the duration of one arc (default `0.32s`). The pearl scales in and out over 0.55s. An arc or pearl in the `run` state also pulses with the `live-mark-pulse` animation (1.4s, infinite). `brand.css` turns the pulse off when the user prefers reduced motion. `markSvg` has no animation.

The console maps a session to a mark in `web/src/shell/markState.ts`. The eight arcs are the eight board lanes. Arcs before the current lane are `done`, the current lane has the state of the session (`run`, `wait`, or `fail`), and later lanes are `off`. A completed session shows eight `done` arcs and the pearl `ok`. The hook `useLiveFavicon` in that file sets the `<link rel="icon">` to a data URL of `markSvg`, and restores the old icon on unmount. [Web console shell](web-console.md) explains the shell that calls it.

## Focus and keyboard helpers

A custom control that traps focus or handles arrow keys by hand is a common source of keyboard bugs. The package therefore keeps one copy of these rules in `design/src/focus.ts`, `design/src/keys.ts`, and `design/src/cx.ts`. The components use them. Screens can import them too.

- **`focusables(root)`:** returns the focusable descendants of `root`. The constant `FOCUSABLE` is a CSS selector: `a[href]`, enabled `button`, `input` (not hidden), `select`, and `textarea`, and any element with a `tabindex` other than `-1`. The function drops each element that is inside an `[inert]` subtree.
- **`useFocusTrap(ref, active, initial?)`:** a hook for modal containers. When `active` is true, it moves focus into `ref` if focus is outside. The target is the `initial` element, else the first focusable element, else the container. On deactivate, it restores focus to the previous element when that element is still in the page. The hook returns a `keydown` handler. Attach the handler to the container. It wraps `Tab` from the last element to the first, and `Shift+Tab` from the first to the last. When the container has no focusable element, it blocks `Tab`.
- **`arrowIndex(key, index, count, orientation, wrap = true)`:** returns the next focus index for an arrow key, `Home`, or `End`, and null for any other key or when `count` is 0.
- **`activateOnKey(fn)`:** a `keydown` handler for a clickable element that is not a `<button>`. It runs `fn` on `Enter` or `Space` and calls `preventDefault`. It ignores events that come from a child element, because it checks that the target is the element itself.
- **`cx(...parts)`:** joins class names and drops false, null, undefined, and 0 values.

```ts
export function arrowIndex(
  key: string, index: number, count: number,
  orientation: "vertical" | "horizontal", wrap = true,
): number | null {
  if (count === 0) return null;
  const next = orientation === "vertical" ? "ArrowDown" : "ArrowRight";
  const prev = orientation === "vertical" ? "ArrowUp" : "ArrowLeft";
  if (key === next) return index + 1 < count ? index + 1 : wrap ? 0 : index;
  if (key === prev) return index > 0 ? index - 1 : wrap ? count - 1 : index;
  if (key === "Home") return 0;
  if (key === "End") return count - 1;
  return null;
}
```

### Where the helpers are used

| Helper | Used by |
| --- | --- |
| `useFocusTrap` | `Dialog` and `CommandPalette` |
| `arrowIndex` | `Menu`, `Tabs`, `TreeItem` (with `wrap` false), and `LaneStepper` |
| `activateOnKey` | `StageRow`, `PhaseNode`, `ExecutionGroup`, and `ToolCall` |

### What happens when

- A `Dialog` opens: the dialog saves the element that has focus, and it gives focus back on close.
- A `Menu` closes after the user moved focus to another element: the menu does not restore focus, so it does not take focus from the user.
- An `[inert]` panel sits inside a modal: `focusables` skips it, so `Tab` never enters it.
- A tree has no wrap: `TreeItem` passes `wrap` false, so `ArrowDown` on the last row stays on the last row.

## Docs renderer components

The package also holds the renderer for Markdown books. The renderer lives in `design/src/docs/` and has its own entry point, `@ostra/design/docs`. The console Docs screen and the HTML export use it. [Documentation books and search](documentation-books.md) explains the book model, the Docs screen, and the export. This part explains only the renderer code in the package.

### The Docs class

The `Docs` class takes a navigation list (`NavGroup[]`), a record of Markdown sources by file name, and an optional `fileUrl` function. Each `PageDef` has an `id`, a `title`, a `file`, and an optional `section`. The section picks one `##` part of the file by number (`8` matches `## 8. The engine`) or by exact heading text. An empty string means the text before the first `##`. The constructor throws `The docs page file <file> is not in the sources.` when a page names a missing file.

The class parses each file with `mdast-util-from-markdown` and the GFM extension. For each page, it drops the first heading and uses it as the page title. The headings one level below it make the table of contents. It gives each heading an id that comes from the function `slug`. A repeated id gets a numeric suffix that starts at `-2` and grows by 1 for each repeat.

- `fromHash(hash)`: reads a `#page/anchor` hash or an older bare anchor. An unknown value opens the first page.
- `link(href, page)`: resolves a Markdown link. A link that starts with `http:`, `https:`, or `mailto:` is external. Any other scheme (such as `javascript:` or `data:`) returns null, and the renderer shows the text with no link. A path that names a page file becomes an internal `#page/anchor` link. Any other path goes to `fileUrl`, and a null result renders as plain text.
- `search(query)`: a case-insensitive substring search. It returns one hit for each page section, and it ranks page titles before headings before body text. The constant `MAX_HITS` is 80. Each hit holds 48 characters before the match and 90 characters after it.

### Markdown and Diagram

`Markdown` turns the blocks of a page into React elements. It never renders raw HTML, except `<br>` and the SVG that Mermaid draws. It renders an image only when the caller gives the image in the `images` record. Any other image becomes a link to the file, because the pages load no image from another origin. This is the same rule as the console CSP.

`Diagram` draws a fenced `mermaid` block as SVG. These rules keep a diagram from running code or leaving the page:

- Mermaid loads with a dynamic `import("mermaid")`, so a page with no diagram does not load it.
- It runs with `securityLevel: "strict"` and `htmlLabels: false`. Labels are SVG text and never HTML.
- The constant `SECURE` lists the config keys that a diagram directive or its front matter cannot set: `secure`, `securityLevel`, `startOnLoad`, `maxTextSize`, `suppressErrorRendering`, and `maxEdges`. The component adds `htmlLabels` to that list.
- The component replaces each `<a>` element in the SVG with its child nodes, so a `click` line makes no link.
- The theme is `dark` for the dark theme and `neutral` for the light theme.
- When Mermaid cannot parse the block, the component shows the source in a `pre` block.

The file `standalone.css` imports only `colors.css`, `typography.css`, `spacing.css`, and `docs.css`. The exported HTML book inlines it, because an exported file loads no fonts and no other files. The console imports it with the `?inline` suffix in `web/src/features/docs/exportHtml.ts`.

## The gallery

The gallery is a dev-only page that shows every component in its variants. It lets a developer check a component in both themes without a running session. `design/src/Gallery.tsx` holds it, and the package exports it as `@ostra/design/gallery`.

`web/src/App.tsx` adds the route `/_design` only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. A production build does not include the route. A segmented `Tabs` control at the top switches the theme. It sets or deletes `data-theme` on `<html>`.

The page has seven cards, and each one is a function: `CoreCard`, `FormsCard`, `FeedbackCard`, `NavigationCard`, `DataCard`, `PipelineCard`, and `IconsCard`. The Icons card lists every name in `ICON_NAMES` and shows the count. The constant `GALLERY_CSS` holds the page styles, which use the prefix `gx-`. The constants `PALETTE` (8 sample palette items), `TREE` (a sample folder tree), `SRC` (a Rust sample for `CodeView`), and `ROWS` (3 sample execution rows) are sample data. The object `FS` holds sample folders for `FolderPicker`. None of this data comes from a server.

When you add a component, add a case to the card of its family. Use sample data like the data above, because the gallery has no server.

## Tests and checks

The package has three test files that run with Vitest in a jsdom environment: `design/src/forms.test.tsx`, `design/src/feedback.test.tsx`, and `design/src/navigation.test.tsx`. The config `design/vitest.config.ts` includes every `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*.test.tsx` file. The tests check keyboard behavior and the rules above, such as dialog focus, scrim click, `FolderPicker` path handling, `Combobox` keys, `CommandPalette` filtering, `Tabs` reorder, `Menu` focus, and `TreeItem` keys. The tests stub `getBoundingClientRect` for the tab drag because jsdom has no layout.

The scripts in `design/package.json` are:

| Script | Command | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` | Checks types with `strict` and `noUnusedLocals` on. |
| `test` | `vitest run` | Runs the three test files one time. |
| `lint` | `biome lint` | Runs the Biome linter. |
| `check` | `biome check` | Runs the Biome linter and formatter checks. |
| `check:fix` | `biome check --write` | Applies the Biome fixes. |

Run these scripts from the `design/` folder. [Testing and evals](testing.md) explains the other test suites of the project.

sections.title: Testing and evals
sections.summary: How to run each test layer of Ostra: Rust tests, web tests, the browser security suite, engine conformance fixtures, live-model evals with their OSTRA_EVAL_* variables, and the Windows probes. Also lists the fake services and fixtures.
sections.body:
## Choose a test layer

Ostra spawns agents that change code, and it serves a terminal and credentials to a browser. A wrong planner rule, policy rule, or render path can cause harm without a compile error. The repository has seven kinds of check. Each kind covers a different risk. This page gives the command for each kind and states what the kind needs. The rules that the tests check have their own pages, and this page links to them.

| Layer | Command | Files | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rust tests | `cargo test --workspace` | `crates/*/src`, `crates/*/tests`, `tests/conformance/main.rs` | `git` on `PATH`. No network. No paid model. |
| Web tests | `npm test` in `web` | 48 files `web/src/**/*.test.ts` and `*.test.tsx` | `npm ci` at the repository root. |
| Design tests | `npm test` in `design` | 3 files `design/src/*.test.tsx` | `npm ci` at the repository root. |
| Browser suite | `cd tests/browser && npm test` | `tests/browser/specs` | Chromium, a `site` folder, and a full build. |
| Live smoke tests | `cargo test -p ostra-providers -- --ignored` | `live_smoke` in `anthropic.rs` and `openai.rs` | A provider key. A small cost. |
| Live evals | `cargo test -p ostra-server --test <name> -- --ignored --nocapture` | `crates/ostra-server/tests/*_evals.rs` | Provider keys. A large cost. |
| Windows probes | Manual run of `winprobe` | `tests/windows-probes` | A throwaway Windows VM. |

The command `cargo test --workspace` skips every test that has `#[ignore]`, so it never calls a paid model. It does run the offline test of each eval file.

## Run the Rust tests

The Rust tests check the engine, the server, the model clients, the policy, the code index, and the stores without a network or a paid model. Run them with these commands:

- Run every test: `cargo test --workspace`.
- Run one crate: `cargo test -p ostra-engine`.
- Run one integration file: `cargo test -p ostra-engine --test pause`.
- Format the code: `cargo fmt --all`.

`rust-toolchain.toml` pins channel `1.98.1` with the components `rustfmt` and `clippy`. The workspace in `Cargo.toml` has the members `crates/*`. It excludes `tests/windows-probes`, which is a separate program (see [Run the Windows probes](#run-the-windows-probes)).

These integration test files hold the larger checks:

| Crate | Files in `tests/` | What they check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ostra-engine` | `pause.rs`, `recover.rs`, `runner.rs`, and `tests/conformance/main.rs` as the target `conformance` | The runner on a real `Engine`, and the planner on folded event histories. |
| `ostra-server` | `e2e.rs`, `mcp.rs` | The whole server with a scripted model, and workspace MCP servers. |
| `ostra-providers` | `anthropic.rs`, `openai.rs` | The two clients against a local HTTP server that replays recorded streams. |
| `ostra-policy` | `policy.rs` (50 tests) | Each guard and each permission mode. See [Policy engine](policy-engine.md). |
| `ostra-code` | `index.rs`, `graph.rs`, `graph_ostra.rs`, `usages.rs`, `outline.rs`, `lsp.rs` | The index, the graph, usage search, the outline, and the LSP provider. See [Code navigation](code-navigation.md). |
| `ostra-mcp` | `client.rs` | The client against fake stdio and HTTP servers, and an OAuth sign-in. See [External MCP servers](mcp-gateway.md). |
| `ostra-store` | `workspace_db.rs` | The workspace database. See [Storage](storage.md). |
| `ostra-sandbox` | `env_scrub.rs` | The start-up environment scrub, on macOS only. See [Sandbox](sandbox.md). |
| `ostra-core` | `fixtures/models-dev-sample.json` | A sample of the price catalog, which other crates load. |

### What happens when

- **Two e2e tests start a server at the same time.** They cannot, because each server reads its paths and keys from the process environment. The function `boot_with` sets `OSTRA_CONFIG`, `OSTRA_DATA_DIR`, `OSTRA_MASTER_KEY_FILE`, and `OSTRA_SANDBOX_CACHE` for each server. See [Configuration reference](reference-configuration.md) for these variables, and see [Secrets, credentials, and Web Push](secrets-and-push.md) for the master key that `OSTRA_MASTER_KEY_FILE` names. Each e2e test holds the `SERIAL` mutex from the start of its server to the stop.
- **The host is not Unix.** The tests for the bridge socket, the harness login terminal, and the whole file `test_stage_evals.rs` have `#[cfg(unix)]`. These three are not the only ones. The same attribute is on `crates/ostra-policy/tests/policy.rs:269`, on `crates/ostra-code/tests/index.rs:247` and `:256`, and on `crates/ostra-store/tests/workspace_db.rs:682`. It is also on one block inside a test of `e2e.rs` (line 1191). The test in `env_scrub.rs` runs only on macOS. The module `crates/ostra-sandbox/src/tests.rs` has a block for Linux.
- **The checkout has no git history.** The test file `graph_ostra.rs` runs `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` on the Ostra tree. The command needs a git repository but not history. The call `.expect("git lists the tree")` panics only when `git` cannot launch. If git exits with a failure, the output is empty, and the test fails later on its layout assertions. The test checks the crate layout against the real source.
- **A test needs the price catalog.** Tests call `ostra_core::pricing::install_test_prices()`, which loads `crates/ostra-core/tests/fixtures/models-dev-sample.json`. The e2e server sets `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` to an empty string, so it downloads nothing. See [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md).

## Check the planner with conformance fixtures

The planner `next_steps` is a pure function. A wrong rule in it shows only as a wrong stage order in a live session. The conformance fixtures in `tests/conformance/main.rs` catch such a rule without a model. The header of the file says that each rule ID of the design has one fixture. The design handover document is not in the repository.

Run the fixtures with `cargo test -p ostra-engine --test conformance`. The file is a test target of `ostra-engine`, set in `crates/ostra-engine/Cargo.toml`. It has 126 tests, and the test names start with the rule ID, for example `d1_`, `t4_`, `p3_`, and `j1_`.

Each fixture follows the same steps:

1. Build a history with the helper `H`. `H::new` appends a `SessionCreated` event with the projects and the options.
2. Add events with `H::ev`, which gives each event the next `seq`. The helpers `decide`, `classify`, `start`, `finish`, `run`, `open_gate`, and `answer` append the events that the runner writes.
3. Fold the events with `SessionState::fold`.
4. Call `next_steps` and compare the `Step::summary()` strings with the expected list.

`H::start(prefix)` finds the spawn step whose summary starts with the prefix. If no step matches, it stops with a message that lists every summary. This message shows the planner state when a rule breaks.

```rust
fn state(&self) -> SessionState {
    SessionState::fold(self.id.clone(), &self.events)
}

fn steps(&self) -> Vec<Step> {
    next_steps(&self.state(), &self.ctx)
}
```

This fixture shows the pause rule. Three containment signals from one execution pause the session. The execution then stops, and a resume restarts the signal count.

```rust
let (spec, _) = h.start("spawn generate-spec");
for n in 0..3 {
    signal(&mut h, &spec, n);
}
let st = h.state();
assert!(st.paused);
assert_eq!(st.contained, Some(spec.clone()));
h.finish(&spec, ExecutionStatus::Interrupted, None);
h.ev(SessionEvent::SessionResumed);
assert_eq!(h.state().contained, None);
```

The fixtures group by rule family. The rules themselves belong to other pages, which the list names.

- **Stage order and documents (D1 to D10, Hard 15, Hard 16).** Explore leads to Spec, Spec leads to Plan, and the plan reads only the spec. See [Session pipeline and planner](session-pipeline.md).
- **Scheduling and tests (M2 to M6, T1 to T7, A1).** Phases run in order of their dependencies, format runs once, and the closing gate is batched.
- **Context, pause, and containment (C1, C2, P1 to P3).** See [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md).
- **Review loop, BLOCKER findings, handoff, and stuck runs (Hard 4, Hard 13, Hard 21).** A BLOCKER finding has no cap and blocks the docs stage.
- **Judge routing and YOLO (J1, YOLO, F1, F2).** Every answer with content goes through the judge. See [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md).
- **Documentation books (B1 to B7).** See [Documentation books and search](documentation-books.md).
- **Init (I1), tracks, categories, and cost controls.** For example, a session budget pauses spawning, and YOLO never raises it, so `budget_pauses_spawns_until_raised` expects no `yolo-answer` step for a budget gate.

### Run one eval

1. Set the provider keys in the environment. The evals use the default settings, so they read the standard variables, for example `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. See [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md).
2. Run a narrow first test. Set `OSTRA_EVAL_CASES` to one case ID and `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` to `1`.
3. Run the command, and replace `<name>` with the test file name:

```text
OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS=anthropic:claude-opus-5-5,anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5 OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS=3 \
  cargo test -p ostra-server --test <name> -- --ignored --nocapture
```

4. Read the table that the test prints, then open the JSON report. The report goes to `target/evals/` with the name `judges-<stamp>.json`, `advisor-<stamp>.json`, `coordination-<stamp>.json`, or `test-stage-<stamp>.json`.

Caution: set a low `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` and a narrow `OSTRA_EVAL_CASES` before a full run. The cost grows with cases times models times repeats. The coordination and test-stage evals also run a grader model for each run.

### For the user

The variables exist only in the process environment of the test. No file stores them.

| Variable | Default | Stored where | When it takes effect | What shows the state | How to stop or change it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS` | A comma list of `provider:model` names. Judge evals use `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5`. Advisor evals add `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5`. Coordination and test-stage evals add `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` to those two. | Process environment | At the start of the test binary | The table that the test prints, one row for each case and model | Unset the variable. Press Ctrl-C to end a run. |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` | `3`. The advisor eval uses `5`. | Process environment | At the start of the test binary | The line `<n> sessions: <cases> cases x <models> models x <runs>` (coordination and test-stage evals) | Set a lower number. |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_CASES` | Empty, which selects every case | Process environment | At the start of the test binary | The case rows in the table | Set a comma list of substrings of case IDs. |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_TIERS` | Empty, which selects every case level | Process environment | At the start of the test binary | The level columns of the report | Set a comma list such as `1,2`. Only coordination and test-stage evals read it. |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_JOBS` | `3`. The advisor eval uses `4`. | Process environment | At the start of the test binary | The count of rows that print at the same time | Set `1` to run one session at a time. The judge eval does not read it. |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_GRADER` | `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` | Process environment | At the start of the test binary | The `grader_cost` field of the report | Set another `provider:model`. The judge eval does not read it. |

`OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS` means a different count in each eval. In the judge eval, it is the count of judge calls for each case and model. In the advisor eval, it is the count of advisor runs for each case and model. In the coordination and test-stage evals, it is the count of whole sessions for each case and model.

The case filter has one trap. The code splits the value at each comma and selects a case if its ID contains any part. An empty part, for example from a trailing comma in `a,b,`, is contained in every ID. Such a value selects every case.

```rust
fn selected(file: &File) -> Vec<Case> {
    let filter = std::env::var("OSTRA_EVAL_CASES").unwrap_or_default();
    let tiers = std::env::var("OSTRA_EVAL_TIERS").unwrap_or_default();
    file.case
        .iter()
        .filter(|c| filter.split(',').any(|f| c.id.contains(f.trim())))
        .filter(|c| {
            tiers.trim().is_empty()
                || tiers
                    .split(',')
                    .any(|t| t.trim().parse::<u8>().ok() == Some(c.tier))
        })
        .cloned()
        .collect()
}
```

If `OSTRA_EVAL_TIERS` has a value that is not a number, such as `x`, no case level matches and no case runs.

### What a live run does

The session evals run real sessions of a real `Engine`. A router executor sends each run that the case lists as `live` to the native loop on the model under test. This loop has the policy, the sandbox, a code index, and the coordination tools. The router plays every other run from the case. Thus only the runs under test cost tokens. See [Native executor loop](native-executor.md) and [Sandbox](sandbox.md).

The evals protect the user data and the host in these ways:

- **Own config and data.** The advisor, coordination, and test-stage evals set `OSTRA_CONFIG`, `OSTRA_DATA_DIR`, the sandbox cache, and an empty price URL before the first run. See [Configuration reference](reference-configuration.md). Each eval creates a per-run folder in `ostra-evals/` under `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, or under `~/.cache` if the variable is not set. The test-stage eval creates `ostra-evals/t<stamp>`, the coordination eval creates `ostra-evals/c<stamp>`, and the advisor eval creates `ostra-evals/<stamp>`. At the end, the eval calls `remove_dir_all` on that per-run folder only. The shared `ostra-evals/` folder stays.
- **Short paths.** The data folder holds the sandbox egress sockets, whose paths must stay short. It must not be under `/tmp`, because the sandbox mounts its own `/tmp`.
- **Scenarios under the target folder.** The scenarios live in `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` for the same reason. They stay after the run, so you can inspect them. The test-stage eval prints the folder.
- **Prices.** The test reads the price catalog that the server cached, so the cost column has real values. If no cache exists, the cost is 0.

### What happens when

- **The model API fails.** In the coordination and test-stage evals, a live run that ends with the status `Error` and a message that has `model call failed`, `provider error`, `overloaded`, `rate limit`, or `stream failed` counts as an infrastructure error. The session runs again, up to 2 times, in a folder with the suffix `-retry<n>`. If the error stays, the row shows `INFRA` and the pass rate leaves it out, because it says nothing about the model.
- **A session does not end.** The coordination eval stops a live session after 1800 seconds, or after 180 seconds with no new run or event. The test-stage eval uses 3600 and 300 seconds. A case can set `timeout_secs`. The offline tests use 60 and 10 seconds, and 120 and 20 seconds.
- **Every call fails.** Each live test fails only when it did no useful work. The judge eval fails when every judge call fails. The advisor eval fails when no advisor run finished. The coordination eval fails when no live run happened. The test-stage eval fails when no run used time or money. Otherwise it passes, because model results vary from run to run.
- **A fixture command is slow.** The test-stage eval stops each project test command after `COMMAND_LIMIT`, which is 240 seconds, and reports `[timed out after 240s]`.

### How each eval scores a run

| Eval | A run passes when |
| --- | --- |
| Judge | The answer matches the `expect` table of the case: category and projects, track, stakes, the needed and not needed items of a sufficiency check, or the disposition, stages, and research of each item of a route answer. An answer that the runner rejects counts as `invalid` and fails. The report also gives the spread of answers and a consistency count. |
| Advisor | The action is the expected one (`retry` or `escalate`), the text names every required fact, and the grader model finds the rubric met. |
| Coordination | Every code check holds (questions, answers, statuses, submits, files, continuations, cache reads) and the grader model finds the rubric met. The report also gives the share of live input tokens that the provider read from its prompt cache. |
| Test stage, analyzer | The report is at the declared path, the run changed no project file, the report holds each expected fact, and the grader finds the rubric met. |
| Test stage, write-test | The status is the expected one, only test files changed and all are listed, each expected level got a test, the project test types pass, every planted mutant of the source makes them fail, the files that must stay keep their text, and the grader agrees. |

The test-stage report names a write-test run on a golden analysis `write-test`. It names a write-test run after a live analyzer `stage`.

### Write or change a case

The case files are TOML. The comment at the top of each file explains its fields.

- **`judges.toml`.** Each case is a request about the source of Ostra, with the route that a careful engineer picks. The `workspace` field is `one` (Ostra as one project), `split` (`server` and `web`), or `triple` (adds `site`). The eval builds the session state through the same fold and `judge_input` that the engine uses.
- **`advisor.toml`.** Each case is a failed init step that the test lays out on disk. The default project is `notes-mcp`. Several cases come in pairs with the same surface problem and opposite answers, so an advisor that matches the problem text fails one of the pair.
- **`coordination.toml`.** A run address has the form `agent[:kind][#n]`. The `live` list names the runs that use the model. The `actor` entries play the other runs. `stop_before` ends the session when a matching run is about to start. `stop_after` ends the session after a matching run finishes. Only `stop_after` entries accept the suffix `!`, which waits for a run that ends other than `waiting`. Level 1 is answering, level 2 is deciding whether to ask, and level 3 is loops of several live runs. The case snapshot of Ostra holds only files that git lists and that are not secret. It leaves out `*_HANDOVER.md`, `tests/evals/coordination.toml`, and `coordination_evals.rs`, so an agent cannot read the expected answers. The offline test checks that rule.
- **`test_stage.toml`.** A case uses a small project from `tests/evals/test_stage/projects` (`notes`, `shop`, `storefront`). The mode is `phase` (a scripted implementer applies a change, and the engine stages it) or `request` (a new TEST session). Overlay folders in `changes/` and `goldens/` hold the changes, the reference analysis `epa.md`, and the reference tests. Level 1 is one pure function, level 2 is a change across layers, and level 3 is regressions, outside contracts, and flows that the request names in words.

The `tier` field of a case holds its level, and `OSTRA_EVAL_TIERS` filters on it. The offline tests make a broken case cost nothing. The coordination and test-stage tests replay every case with stand-ins for the live runs. The test-stage replay also checks that the project tests let every mutant survive and that the reference tests kill every mutant. The judge and advisor tests check that each case folds into the state, or builds the spawn, that the eval expects.

## Run the browser security suite

The suite in `tests/browser` proves in a real Chromium that text from agents, repositories, and uploads cannot run code in the console. It also checks the cross-origin limits, the sign-in token, and the browser storage. See [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) for the rules that it checks.

Run it with `cd tests/browser && npm test`. The command builds the web UI and the binary `target-browser/debug/ostra`, starts a scratch server, and stops it by process ID at the end. Nothing leaves the machine.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant PW as Playwright
    participant GS as global-setup
    participant FM as fake model
    participant OS as ostra server
    participant SP as specs
    PW->>GS: globalSetup
    GS->>FM: startFakeModel
    GS->>OS: spawn serve --no-open --bind 127.0.0.1
    GS->>OS: POST /api/auth/exchange
    GS->>OS: POST /api/workspaces and POST sessions
    OS->>FM: POST Anthropic Messages with SSE
    FM-->>OS: scripted agent output with test strings
    GS->>GS: writeBook into .ostra/docs/pw_book
    GS-->>PW: SuiteState in state.json
    PW->>SP: run specs with one worker
    SP->>OS: load pages in Chromium
    SP->>FM: canaryHits
```

The scratch server uses the folder `/tmp/pw-browser` with its own config, data folder, master key, and `HOME`. The global setup refuses a root outside `/tmp`. The fake model in `tests/browser/lib/fake-model.ts` plays a whole YOLO session, and every field that the UI renders carries a test string. The harness is a stub script, and the MCP server is a stub. The setup also builds the site into `/tmp/pw-browser/site` with an extra docs page of test strings, and serves it as plain files on `ostra-site.localhost`.

Each test string sets `window.__pwned` or requests `<fake>/canary/<id>` when it runs or loads. The `guard` fixture in `lib/guard.ts` fails a test on any of these events:

- `window.__pwned` gets a value.
- The fake model receives a canary request.
- A CSP violation occurs on the app origin. The message shows the blocked URL, whose ID names the render path.
- An unexpected dialog, popup, or navigation away from the app occurs.

The spec files cover these areas:

| Spec | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `00-smoke` | The app loads signed in. |
| `render` | Agent messages, tool output, artifacts, the completion report, session titles, repo file names and contents, branches, commits, MCP metadata, memory, skills, decisions, search, and the quick answer. |
| `mobile` | The same render paths in the phone layout `web/src/mobile`. |
| `terminal` | OSC 52, OSC 8, title sequences, and device queries through xterm.js. The PTY input must match a run with no browser attached. |
| `cross-origin` | Attacker pages on another port and another site: forms, fetch, WebSocket, tags, frames, a navigation to each GET route in `api.rs`, DNS rebinding, and page content that reaches `/api`. The host `evil-ostra.test` maps to `127.0.0.1`. |
| `signin` | The token leaves the URL, no request carries it, and the profile keeps nothing that is still valid. |
| `uploads` | SVG and HTML uploads never render inline. |
| `storage` | `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, and Cache Storage hold no transcripts, tokens, or keys. |
| `shortcuts` | The web app manifest and icons load under the CSP, and a recorded shortcut stays in the workspace entry. |
| `site` | Docs Markdown, Mermaid diagrams with hostile labels, the homepage, and the console shot under their meta CSP. |
| `books` | A documentation book that `global-setup.ts` writes to `.ostra/docs/pw_book/` with test strings in every field, and its exported HTML file, which must hold no script and must render under its meta CSP. |

### For the user

| Variable or flag | Default | Stored where | When it takes effect | What shows the state | How to stop or change it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `npm run test:fast` | Not set. `npm test` builds first. | `tests/browser/package.json` | At the next run | No build output. The site pages still rebuild, because the test page names the port of the fake. | Run `npm test` for a full build. |
| `PW_SKIP_BUILD` | Not set | Process environment | At the start of the run | No build output | Unset the variable. |
| `PW_KEEP_SERVER` | Not set. The server stops at the end. | Process environment | At the end of the run | The file `/tmp/pw-browser/server.pid` | Unset the variable, or send `SIGTERM` to the process ID in the file. |
| `PW_CHROME` | `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1217/chrome-linux64/chrome` | Process environment | At the start of the run | The Chromium that Playwright launches | Set the path of another Chromium binary. |
| `OSTRA_BIN` | `target-browser/debug/ostra` | Process environment | At the start of the run | The server process name | Set the path of another `ostra` binary. |

The suite has one worker (`workers: 1`), because it uses one scratch server and one PTY, and the specs that type into it must not overlap. Each test has a 90 second timeout, and each `expect` has 15 seconds. Playwright is pinned to `1.63.0`. A failed test keeps its trace.

### What happens when

- **The `site` folder is missing.** The root `package.json` lists `site` as a workspace, and `lib/site.ts` runs `npm run build:console` in `site/`. This checkout has no `site` folder, so the global setup stops with an error until you add it.
- **A stale server runs.** The setup reads `server.pid`. It sends `SIGTERM` only if the command line of that process names `ostra` and `serve`.
- **A session does not complete.** The setup waits up to 120 seconds for a final status. If the status is not `completed`, it prints a warning and the specs render what the session produced.

## Run the Windows probes

The program in `tests/windows-probes` checks which parts of a Windows sandbox design hold on a real Windows host. It holds no Ostra code, and it is not a member of the Cargo workspace. It builds with a static C runtime (`.cargo/config.toml` sets `+crt-static`), so one exe runs on a bare VM. The recorded run in `results-full.md` is from Windows Server 2025 build 26100.

Caution: run `winprobe` only on a throwaway VM. The `setup` role creates the local users `OstraProbeA` and `OstraProbeB`, changes ACLs, and adds firewall rules named `OstraProbe*`. Run `cleanup` at the end to remove them.

Run the probes in these steps:

1. Build the exe for a Windows target: `cargo build --release` in `tests/windows-probes`.
2. Copy `winprobe.exe` to the VM.
3. In an elevated shell, run `winprobe setup`. It writes a random password to `C:\ostra-probe\pass.txt`, locks the file to administrators, creates the two users, and builds an ACL test tree at `C:\ostra-probe\repo`. The constants `PASS_FILE` and `REPO` in `tests/windows-probes/src/defs.rs` spell these paths.
4. Run `winprobe run`. It spawns confined probes as `OstraProbeA`, runs the host checks, and writes `C:\ostra-probe\results.md`.
5. Read `results.md`, then run `winprobe cleanup`.

The exe has these roles:

| Role | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `setup`, `run`, `cleanup` | The host roles of the steps above. |
| `asuser <group> <out>` | The confined role. The host spawns it as a probe user. It runs the checks for identity, restricted tokens, Job Objects, cross-process access, the registry, credential stores, ACLs, reads, hard links, and escapes, and writes its findings to a file. |
| `markself`, `medspawn`, `sleeper`, `openone`, `spinjob`, `netfilter` | Small helpers that the other roles spawn. |

Each check makes a finding with five fields: the check number (`verify`), a status, a name, the expected result, and the observed result. The confined role sends findings to the host as one tab-separated line each, and the host sorts them by check number. The status is one of these:

- `PASS`: the design assumption held.
- `FAIL`: a real gap that the design must handle.
- `INCONCLUSIVE`: this VM cannot decide the check.
- `NEEDS_CLIENT`: the check needs a Windows 11 client or the antivirus of the user.

The recorded run has 54 findings: 43 `PASS`, 3 `FAIL`, 4 `INCONCLUSIVE`, and 4 `NEEDS_CLIENT`. The 3 failures show that Windows Firewall cannot limit loopback traffic to one port, and that processes of the same sandbox user can open each other. The probe also shows that a restricting SID cannot isolate such processes, so isolation must come from one user for each execution slot. See [Sandbox](sandbox.md) for the sandbox that Ostra ships.

## Check the format and the lint rules

The format and lint rules keep one style across the Rust and the TypeScript code. Run `cargo fmt --all` for Rust. Run `npm run check` in `web` or `design` for TypeScript. Run `npm run check:fix` to write the fixes.

The root file `biome.json` sets the Biome rules:

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Indent | 2 spaces |
| Line width | 120 |
| Quotes, semicolons, trailing commas | Double quotes, always, all |
| Imports | Sorted by the `organizeImports` action |
| Lint preset | `recommended`, with `a11y` off and `useExhaustiveDependencies` as a warning |
| Ignored paths | `**/dist`, `web/src/api/gen`, `**/.vitest`, `**/.shots`, `site/public/console`, `tests/browser` |

Biome ignores `web/src/api/gen` because ts-rs writes those files. It ignores `tests/browser` because that package has its own setup. Version `2.5.14` of `@biomejs/biome` is a dev dependency of `web`.
