sections.title: Configuration reference
sections.summary: A lookup catalog of the settings files, settings keys, environment variables, CLI flags, data paths, and instruction and skill file names, with defaults and a link to the page that explains each.
sections.body:
Ostra reads its configuration from three TOML files, one registry database, some environment variables, and some CLI flags. A reader who needs one value must know which of these holds it. This page is a catalog. Each row gives a key, its default, and the page that explains the behavior. The page does not explain what each setting does.

This page covers:

- The three settings files and the registry.
- The keys of the global config.
- The workspace settings keys that other pages own.
- The keys of the project profile.
- Environment variables, CLI flags, and subcommands.
- Data paths and runtime folders.
- Instruction file names, skill folders, report names, and protected home paths.

## The three settings files and the registry

[Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) owns the model of the settings files and says which keys each file holds.

| File | Path | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global config | `config.toml` in the config folder of the OS, `~/.config/ostra/config.toml` on Linux | The whole machine |
| Workspace settings | `<workspace>/.ostra/workspace.toml` | One workspace |
| Project profile | `<project>/.ostra/project.toml` | One project |
| Registry | `registry.db` in the data dir | The whole machine. It holds the workspace keys that the catalog below marks as Registry. |

## Global config keys

The global config is the `GlobalConfig` type in [`crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs). Every table has a default, so an empty file is valid. If the file does not exist, the command `ostra config` and the server start write the default file through `ensure_global_config`.

| Table and key | Default | Meaning | Explained on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tool_enforcement` | `disabled` | `enabled` adds the write-scope, report-path, and self-protection guards. This is Rule G1. | [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) |
| `[providers.<name>]` `api_key_env` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for `anthropic`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` for `openai` | Name of the variable that holds the API key | [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md) |
| `[providers.<name>]` `auth_token_env` | `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` for `anthropic`, none for `openai` | Name of the variable that holds a bearer token. Ostra uses it when no API key is set. | [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md) |
| `[providers.<name>]` `base_url_env` | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` for `anthropic`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` for `openai` | Name of the variable that holds the base URL | [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md) |
| `[providers.<name>]` `base_url` | none | Fixed base URL. It wins over the variable and over the URL saved in the browser. | [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md) |
| `[providers.<name>]` `keychain_service` | none | OS keychain service that holds the key when the variables are unset | [Secrets, credentials, and Web Push](secrets-and-push.md) |
| `[tiers.<table>]` `fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, `frontier` | See the default model table below | Model for each tier on one executor table | [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) |
| `[harness.<name>]` `command` | The harness name: `claude`, `codex`, `grok`, `agy` | Program that Ostra starts. An empty value falls back to the harness name. | [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) |
| `[harness.<name>]` `args` | `[]` | Extra arguments that Ostra adds to every launch | [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) |
| `[permissions]` `allow`, `ask`, `deny` | `allow` and `ask` empty, `deny = ["Bash(rm -rf /*)"]` | Global permission rules | [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) |
| `[server]` `port` | none | Fixed port. If it is absent, Ostra searches from `7878`. | [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md) |
| `[server]` `bind` | none, which means `127.0.0.1` | Listen address | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `[server]` `allowed_hosts` | `[]` | Extra host names that the browser can use | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `[server]` `use_ip_host` | `false` | Sign in at `127.0.0.1` in place of a private `ostra-….localhost` name | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `[sandbox]` `mode` | `required` on Linux and macOS, `auto` on Windows | `auto`, `required`, or `off` | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `[sandbox]` `network` | `allowlist` | `none`, `allowlist`, `public`, or `host` | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `[sandbox]` `allowed_hosts` | `[]` | More hosts for the egress proxy: `host`, `*.domain`, or either with `:port` | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `[sandbox]` `upstream_proxy` | none | HTTP proxy in the form `http://host:port` that the egress proxy uses | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `[sandbox]` `extra_writable` | `[]` | More paths that agent commands can write, absolute or `~/...` | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `[sandbox]` `extra_hidden` | `[]` | More paths that agent commands cannot see, absolute or `~/...` | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |

Ostra does not read the sandbox keys `loopback` and `blocked_ports` from `config.toml`. They are workspace keys only. See `sandbox_loopback` and `sandbox_blocked_ports` in the workspace catalog below.

### Default tier models

`GlobalConfig::default` sets the default model of each level on each executor table. [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md) explains how a route picks a level.

| Table | `fast` | `balanced` | `advanced` | `frontier` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `native` | `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5` | `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` | `anthropic:claude-fable-5-1` |
| `claude` | `haiku` | `sonnet` | `opus` | `fable` |
| `codex` | `gpt-5.6-luna` | `gpt-5.6-terra` | `gpt-5.6-sol` | `gpt-5.6-sol` |
| `grok` | `grok-4.5` | `grok-4.5` | `grok-4.5` | `grok-4.5` |
| `agy` | `flash` | `flash` | `flash` | `flash` |

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | Change with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Every key of the global config except the provider tables and the `[server]` table | See the tables above | `config.toml` | At the next read. Ostra reads the file on every call, so no restart is needed. | The file itself. `ostra config` prints its path. | Edit the file. A broken file keeps the last good copy. |
| The provider tables | See the table above | `config.toml` | After a restart, because Ostra builds the provider table when the server starts | The file itself | Edit the file, then restart the server |
| The `[server]` table | See the table above | `config.toml` | After a restart, because Ostra reads the table when the server starts | The line `Ostra is running on <address>` in the server output | Edit the file, or pass a serve flag for one run |

If the file cannot be parsed when the server starts, the start fails with the message `reading <path>`. A problem in the `[sandbox]` table also stops the start. The message names the problem and the config path.

## Workspace settings keys

The keys `name`, `projects`, `routing.*`, and `instructions.*` and their defaults are in [Workspaces, settings, and routing](workspaces-and-settings.md), which owns them and the checks that run when a user saves.

The table below lists the other dotted keys of `SETTING_KEYS` in [`crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs). Each row links to the page that owns the key.

| Key | What it sets | Default | Stored in | Explained on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `yolo.default` | Start new sessions in YOLO mode | `false` | Registry | [Judge calls and YOLO mode](judges-and-decisions.md) |
| `permissions.mode` | Permission mode for tool calls: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, or `bypass` | `default` | Registry | [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) |
| `permissions.allow` | Tool calls that Ostra allows without asking | `[]` | `workspace.toml` | [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) |
| `permissions.ask` | Tool calls that always ask | `[]` | `workspace.toml` | [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) |
| `permissions.deny` | Tool calls that Ostra always denies | `[]` | `workspace.toml` | [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) |
| `notifications.push` | Push notifications for gates and finished sessions | `true` | `workspace.toml` | [Secrets, credentials, and Web Push](secrets-and-push.md) |
| `limits.max_parallel_executions` | Executions that can run at the same time | `3` | Registry | [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md) |
| `limits.session_budget_usd` | Dollars that one session can spend before it pauses | `25.0`. The value `0` means no limit. | Registry | [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md) |
| `sandbox_mode` | Sandbox mode for agent commands, in place of the global one | none, which follows the global `[sandbox]` `mode` | Registry | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `tool_enforcement` | Whether guards check where tool calls read and write, in place of the global choice | none, which follows the global `tool_enforcement` | Registry | [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) |
| `sandbox_network` | What sandboxed commands can reach, in place of the global choice | none, which follows the global `[sandbox]` `network` | Registry | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `sandbox_allowed_hosts` | More hosts that sandboxed commands can reach, added to the global list | `[]` | Registry | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `sandbox_decoys` | More decoy credential files in agent sandboxes, added to the built-in ones | `[]` | Registry | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `sandbox_loopback` | Which loopback ports sandboxed commands on macOS can connect to. `listed` is the other accepted value. | `open` | Registry | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `sandbox_blocked_ports` | Loopback ports that sandboxed commands on macOS never connect to | `[]` | Registry | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `mcp_servers` | External MCP servers whose tools agents can use | `[]` | `workspace.toml` | [External MCP servers](mcp-gateway.md) |

### Sub-tables with their own defaults

| Table | Key | Default | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[[mcp_servers]]` | `enabled` | `true` | |
| `[[mcp_servers]]` | `timeout_secs` | `120` | Seconds for one tool call |
| `[[mcp_servers]]` | `disabled_tools`, `agents` | `[]`. An empty `agents` list means every agent. | |
| `[[projects]]` | `code_provider.timeout_secs` | `10` | Valid values are 1 to 120 seconds |
| `[[projects.language_servers]]` | `timeout_secs` | `10` | Valid values are 1 to 120 seconds |

See [External MCP servers](mcp-gateway.md) and [Code navigation](code-navigation.md) for the meaning of the sub-tables.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | Change with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Each key marked `workspace.toml` in the catalog | See the catalog | `<workspace>/.ostra/workspace.toml` | At the next read, so the next execution uses the saved value | The settings editor of the workspace page | Save in the settings editor |
| Each key marked Registry in the catalog | See the catalog | `registry.db`, key `workspace_access:<workspace root>` | At the next read, with no restart | The settings editor of the workspace page | Save in the settings editor. A manual edit of `workspace.toml` has no effect on these keys. |

## The SAMPLE test fixture

`SAMPLE` is a constant in the `tests` module of [`crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs`](crates/ostra-core/src/config.rs). It holds one TOML text, and only two tests read it: `parses_sample_and_routes` and `uninstalled_harness_is_refused`. Ostra never reads it at run time, and it is not a default. Use the catalogs above for the real defaults. [Testing and evals](testing.md) explains how to run the tests.

## Project profile keys

The project profile is the `ProjectProfile` type. The init flow writes `<project>/.ostra/project.toml`, and `check_profile` parses it. Every key is optional. If the file is missing, Ostra uses an empty profile. See [Project init and skills](init-and-skills.md) for how Ostra generates and uses each key.

| Key | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | number | Write `schema_version = 1`. A quoted value is an error. |
| `generated_at` | string | Time of generation |
| `stack` | string | The name of the stack, for example `rust`. Older files that use a `[stack]` table still load. Ostra joins `language` and `frameworks` as `language/framework1,framework2` and takes `build_tool` from the table. |
| `build_tool` | string | Build tool of the project |
| `commands.build`, `commands.test`, `commands.test_one`, `commands.format`, `commands.lint`, `commands.typecheck`, `commands.run` | string | One command for each purpose. An empty value counts as not set. |
| `test_framework` | string | Test framework of the project |
| `test_types.<name>` | table | Keys `command`, `command_one`, `matches`, `note`, `reports` |
| `module_map` | array of tables | Rows with `glob` and `area` |
| `skills` | array of tables | Rows with `name`, `kind`, `path`, `component_type`, `source`. `kind` is `convention`, `creation`, `test`, or `other`. `source` is `generated`, `reused`, `adopted`, or `user`. |
| `conventions` | table | Keys `immutability_keyword`, `naming`, `notes`. It is one table, so write `[conventions]` and not `[[conventions]]`. |
| `review_rules` | array of tables | Rows with `id`, `rule`, `severity` (`H`, `M`, or `L`), `auto_fixable` |

`check_profile` returns a fix for each common error. TOML has no `null`, so omit the key. `stack` is a string, not a table. The engine applies a review rule on its own only when `auto_fixable` is `true` and the ID does not start with `SEC-BLOCK` or `PHASE-REQ`.

## Environment variables

Ostra reads the variables below. A separate part lists the variables that Ostra sets for child processes, because a user does not set them.

| Variable | Default | Read by | Effect | Explained on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OSTRA_CONFIG` | The config folder of the OS plus `ostra/config.toml` | `global_config_path` | Path of the global config file | This page |
| `OSTRA_DATA_DIR` | The local data folder of the OS plus `ostra` | `data_dir` | Folder of the data dir | This page |
| `OSTRA_MASTER_KEY_FILE` | unset | `master_key::unlock` | Key file that seals saved credentials. If it is unset, Ostra uses the OS keychain, then `<data dir>/master.key`. A keychain call that takes more than 10 seconds (`KEYCHAIN_TIMEOUT`) counts as unavailable. | [Secrets, credentials, and Web Push](secrets-and-push.md) |
| `OSTRA_SANDBOX_CACHE` | `~/.cache/ostra/sandbox` | `cache_base` in the sandbox crate | Root folder of the sandbox tool caches | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |
| `OSTRA_MODELS_DEV_URL` | `https://models.dev/api.json` (`MODELS_DEV_URL`) | `prices::start`, through `URL_ENV` | URL of the price catalog. An empty value turns fetching off. | [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md) |
| `OSTRA_LOG` | `info` | `serve` in `main.rs` | Log filter in the syntax of `tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter`. A value that does not parse falls back to `info`. | This page |
| `OSTRA_ENV_FILE` | unset | `run.sh` and `install.sh` | File whose `export NAME=value` lines the script applies before it starts Ostra | [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md) |
| `OSTRA_PREFIX` | `~/.local` | `install.sh` | Install prefix. The binary goes to `<prefix>/bin`. | [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md) |
| `SKIP_BUILD` | unset | `run.sh` and `install.sh` | The value `1` skips the build and uses the existing binary | [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md) |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | unset | Each default model provider | Credentials and base URLs of the model provider | [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md) |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `CODEX_HOME` | unset | The machine check in `env.rs` | Help Ostra decide that a harness CLI is signed in | [Workspace, settings, and setup screens](web-workspace-and-setup.md) |
| `OSTRA_EVAL_RUNS`, `OSTRA_EVAL_MODELS`, `OSTRA_EVAL_CASES`, `OSTRA_EVAL_JOBS`, `OSTRA_EVAL_GRADER`, `OSTRA_EVAL_TIERS` | `OSTRA_EVAL_GRADER` is `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` | The live-model evals | Control which cases and models an eval run uses | [Testing and evals](testing.md) |
| `OSTRA_BIN`, `OSTRA_LIVE_REQUIRE` | `OSTRA_BIN` is `target-browser/debug/ostra` | The browser tests and the live provider tests | Path of the binary under test, and a switch for live tests | [Testing and evals](testing.md) |

### How the two path variables resolve

The functions `global_config_path` and `data_dir` read their variable first. If the variable is unset, they use the folder that the `dirs` crate returns. If the OS returns no folder, they use the current folder `.`.

```rust
pub fn global_config_path() -> PathBuf {
    if let Ok(p) = std::env::var("OSTRA_CONFIG") {
        return PathBuf::from(p);
    }
    dirs::config_dir()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."))
        .join("ostra")
        .join("config.toml")
}
```

The function `data_dir` has the same form with `OSTRA_DATA_DIR`, `dirs::data_local_dir`, and the folder name `ostra`.

### Variables that Ostra sets

The constant `BRIDGE_ENV` lists `OSTRA_TOKEN`, `OSTRA_EXECUTION`, `OSTRA_URL`, and `OSTRA_HARNESS`. Ostra sets them for each harness or MCP child process, so the child can call back with its own execution identity. Ostra drops any inherited copy first, because a child can inherit them only by accident. Do not set them yourself.

The function `credential_env_names` collects these names, the credential variables of each model provider, and each MCP `oauth.client_secret_env`. Ostra does not pass these variables to agent processes or MCP servers.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | Change with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `OSTRA_CONFIG` | `~/.config/ostra/config.toml` on Linux | The process environment | After a restart, because Ostra reads the path when the server starts | `ostra config` prints the path in use | Set the variable before you start `ostra`. The Docker image sets it to `/config/config.toml`. `install.sh` records it in the service launcher when it is set. |
| `OSTRA_DATA_DIR` | `~/.local/share/ostra` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/ostra` on macOS | The process environment | After a restart | The folder itself. The server log is `server.log` inside it. | Set the variable before you start `ostra`. The Docker image sets it to `/data`. `install.sh` records it in the service launcher when it is set. |
| The other variables of the table above | See the table | The process environment | After a restart | The server log shows the key source, the price fetch, and the log level in use | Set the variable before you start `ostra`, or remove it to return to the default |

Copy the data dir to a backup before you point `OSTRA_DATA_DIR` at a new folder. A new folder starts with an empty registry, so Ostra cannot see the saved credentials, the workspace list, and the sign-ins of the old folder.

## CLI flags and subcommands

The `ostra` binary uses the `clap` parser in [`crates/ostra-server/src/main.rs`](crates/ostra-server/src/main.rs). The serve flags work with the `serve` subcommand and without a subcommand, so `ostra --port 8080` and `ostra serve --port 8080` are the same. For the build and the first run, see [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md).

| Flag | Default | Effect | Explained on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--port <u16>` | `server.port`, else `7878` (`DEFAULT_PORT`) | Fixed port on the listen address. With a flag or a config port, a busy port is an error. With no port, Ostra tries `7878` to `7897`, then asks the OS for a free port. | [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md) |
| `--no-open` | off | Do not open the browser | [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md) |
| `--dev` | off | Also accept the host `localhost:5173` of the Vite dev server | [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md) |
| `--bind <address>` | `server.bind`, else `127.0.0.1` | Listen address. It accepts an IP address, `localhost`, `all`, or `*`. Ostra removes square brackets around an IPv6 address. | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `--allow-host <name>` | none | Extra host name for the browser. Repeat the flag for more names. Ostra adds them to `server.allowed_hosts`. | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |

| Subcommand | Effect | Explained on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `serve` | Start the server. This is the default. | [Ostra overview and first run](overview.md) |
| `config` | Print the config path. Write the default config first if none exists. | This page |
| `url` | Print a fresh sign-in URL for a running server | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `sessions` | List the browsers that are signed in | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `sessions revoke <id>` or `sessions revoke --all` | Revoke one sign-in or all of them. A running server refuses a revoked browser within 5 seconds. | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `signout` | Sign out every browser. It is the same as `sessions revoke --all`. | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `stop <session>` | Stop a session while the server is not running, so the next start does not recover and run its executions again. If the server runs, the command refuses and tells you to use the session board. | [Event log, runner, and limits](event-log-and-runner.md) |
| `hook` and `mcp-stdio` | Bridges that harness CLIs call. A user does not run them. | [Harness executors](harness-executors.md) |
| `sandbox-init` | Hidden helper that runs inside a sandbox before the runtime starts | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |

Pass `--bind` with an address that is not loopback only when you need network access. Ostra then serves plain HTTP, and anyone who gets a sign-in link can run commands as you. The server prints this warning at start.

### For the user

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | Change with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Each serve flag of the flag table | See the flag table | The command line of one run. The `[server]` table of the global config holds the matching keys. | At the next start | The line `Ostra is running on <address>` in the server output | Pass the flag, or remove it to return to the config value |

## Data dir paths

The data dir holds machine state. The function `ensure_data_dir` creates it and sets the mode `0700` on Unix, because it holds the registry with saved credentials and SQLite creates the `-wal` and `-shm` files readable by everyone. The database files get the mode `0600` when Ostra opens them.

| Path in the data dir | Content | Explained on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `registry.db`, `registry.db-wal`, `registry.db-shm` | The machine registry | [Storage: databases and lesson memory](storage.md) |
| `master.key` | Fallback master key: 64 hex characters, mode `0600`. Ostra uses it when no key file is set and the OS keychain is not usable. | [Secrets, credentials, and Web Push](secrets-and-push.md) |
| `server.log` | Log file that Ostra appends to. It receives the same lines as the standard output. | This page |
| `server.json` | Process ID and port of the running server. Ostra writes it at start and removes it at a clean stop. | [Browser sign-in and network binding](browser-auth.md) |
| `models-dev.json` | Cache of the price catalog. Ostra refreshes it every 24 hours (`REFRESH_EVERY`). After a failed fetch, Ostra keeps the cached prices and tries again after 1 hour. A fetch times out after 60 seconds. | [Model providers and pricing](providers-and-pricing.md) |
| `assets/` | The embedded references and skills that Ostra writes at each start | [Agents, prompts, and coordination](agents-and-prompts.md) |
| `decoys/` and `egress/` | Decoy credential files and egress proxy sockets of the sandbox | [Sandbox](sandbox.md) |

The sandbox build cache is outside the data dir, and [Sandbox](sandbox.md) explains its layout. Its root is `~/.cache/ostra/sandbox` unless `OSTRA_SANDBOX_CACHE` names another folder.

## Workspace, session, and project runtime folders

The constant `RUNTIME_DIR` is `.ostra`. It is the runtime folder name in both a workspace and a project.

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `<workspace>/.ostra/workspace.toml` | Workspace settings |
| `<workspace>/.ostra/workspace.db` | Workspace database |
| `<workspace>/.ostra/uploads/` | Uploads that wait for a session to claim them |
| `<workspace>/.ostra/sessions/<session id>/` | The session root. Cross-project artifacts such as the spec and the plan live here. |
| `<session root>/<project key>/` | Per-project reports of the session |
| `<session root>/uploads/` | Files that the user uploaded to the session |
| `<session root>/.state/` | State that the engine owns. No agent can write here. |

For the workspace database, see [Storage: databases and lesson memory](storage.md). For uploads, see [Workspace artifacts and uploads](artifacts-and-uploads.md). For the files of the harness execution folder, see [Harness executors](harness-executors.md).

## Instruction files and skill folders

The project root can hold instruction files for agents. `INSTRUCTION_FILES` lists three names: `claude.md`, `agents.md`, and `agent.md`. Ostra matches the names without regard to letter case, so `CLAUDE.md` and `Agents.md` count. A match can be a file or a symbolic link. The function `project_instruction_files` returns the matches in this order: `claude.md`, then `agents.md`, then `agent.md`.

Project skills live in folders. `SKILLS_DIR` is `.agents/skills`, the folder of the cross-harness `.agents` standard. Ostra writes every new skill there. `LEGACY_SKILLS_DIR` is `.ostra/skills`. Ostra still reads it and never writes to it. `SKILL_DIRS` holds both folders in lookup order. The function `find_project_skill` returns the `<name>/SKILL.md` of the first folder that has one, so a skill in `.agents/skills` wins over a skill of the same name in `.ostra/skills`.

| Name | Value | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `INSTRUCTION_FILES` | `claude.md`, `agents.md`, `agent.md` | Agent instruction files at the project root, matched in any letter case |
| `SKILLS_DIR` | `.agents/skills` | Folder where Ostra writes new skills |
| `LEGACY_SKILLS_DIR` | `.ostra/skills` | Older folder, read only |
| `SKILL_DIRS` | `.agents/skills`, then `.ostra/skills` | Lookup order |
| Skill file | `<skills dir>/<name>/SKILL.md` | One skill |

For how agents use these files, see [Project init and skills](init-and-skills.md) and [Agents, prompts, and coordination](agents-and-prompts.md).

| Setting | Default | Stored in | Takes effect | State shown by | Change with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Instruction file | none | A file of the three names at the project root | At the next execution that builds a prompt for the project | The skills and project screens of the console | Create, edit, or delete the file |
| Project skill | none | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | At the next execution that loads skills | The skills screen of the console | Edit in the skills screen, or edit the file. To remove a legacy skill, delete it from `.ostra/skills`. |

## Protected paths under the home folder

`HOME_CREDENTIALS` lists 56 paths under `$HOME` that no agent reads. The list has credential stores, browser profiles, and personal data for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Examples are `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.netrc`, `.git-credentials`, `Library/Keychains`, and `AppData/Roaming/Microsoft/Credentials`. Five entries belong to one harness CLI. That CLI signs in with the file, so it is the one program that can see it:

- `.claude/.credentials.json` for Claude Code
- `.codex/auth.json` for Codex
- `.grok/auth.json` for Grok Build
- `.gemini/oauth_creds.json` for Antigravity
- `.gemini/google_accounts.json` for Antigravity

The function `secret_paths` returns the full set of paths that no agent can read: the data dir, the master key file when one is set, and every `HOME_CREDENTIALS` entry. The policy refuses tool calls that name them. The sandbox hides them. The Grep and Glob tools skip them. See [Policy engine and containment](policy-engine.md) and [Sandbox](sandbox.md).

On Windows, `RESERVED_NAMES` lists 29 device names, such as `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `com1` to `com9`, and `lpt1` to `lpt9`, with their superscript forms. A file with one of these stems opens a device and not a file, under any extension and in any folder. `is_reserved_device` flags them, except `NUL`. On Unix it always returns false.

## Defaults that depend on the platform

- **`[sandbox]` `mode`:** `required` on Linux and macOS, `auto` on Windows. Windows has no sandbox backend yet. With `required`, Ostra refuses every execution on Windows, so the default `auto` runs executions unsandboxed with a warning.
- **`[sandbox]` `network`:** `allowlist` on every platform.
- **Config and data folders:** the OS decides them through the `dirs` crate. The variables `OSTRA_CONFIG` and `OSTRA_DATA_DIR` override them. If the OS gives no folder, Ostra uses the current folder `.`.
- **Owner-only modes:** Ostra creates private folders with mode `0700` and private files with mode `0600` on Unix. On Windows a new folder inherits the access list of its parent. Under the user profile, that list gives access to the user, SYSTEM, and administrators only.

A pseudo-terminal. Ostra runs each harness CLI in one and mirrors its screen.
The agent that answers one side-panel question about the projects and changes no pipeline state.
The machine database that holds approvals, the permission mode, YOLO, the limits, and sealed secrets, which a folder file must never set.
The handle of the machine-wide SQLite registry that holds workspaces, push subscriptions, and the `kv` table.
The project facts that `augment` appends to the first message of each run.
A key combination that the browser or the system handles before the page, such as `Ctrl+W`.
A string such as `file:<key>:<path>` that the console uses to open one screen in a tab and to build its URL.
The number of review passes in one loop before the next pass becomes a gate. `REVIEW_CAP` holds the base value of 3.
The cycle of work, review, and fix for one phase. It repeats until the review is clean or the cap is reached.
The choice of executor, model, and effort for one agent execution, resolved by `resolve_route`.
A wizard choice that sets the executor of the implementer agents to native, Codex, or Claude Code.
The server function that runs one git command without a terminal, with a time limit, secret redaction, and a tail of the output.
The result of a coordination tool that tells the loop to continue, wait, or finish the run.
The `.ostra` folder, named by `RUNTIME_DIR`, inside a workspace or a project. It holds the state that Ostra writes there.
The marker `${ostra_secret}` that replaces a literal `env` or `headers` value in the settings file after Ostra stores the value in its registry.
A fake model provider that returns queued or computed responses and records each request.
The type that seals and opens secret values with AES-256-GCM and uses the row key as associated data.
The macOS sandbox facility that Ostra drives with a policy for `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`.
The result of one push send: `Delivered`, `Gone`, or `Failed`.
The script `web/public/sw.js` that shows push notifications and opens their links.
The trait through which the engine reaches the global config, the workspace settings, the executors, and the judges.
A file that an agent writes in a session folder, such as a spec, a plan, or a report.
The dollar cap in `limits.session_budget_usd` after which the planner starts no new execution and opens a budget gate.
The Markdown file `ostra-session-context.md` that Ostra writes from the fold so that a revision reads an index and not a conversation.
The `ostra_session` cookie that the browser sends on each request to `/api` and `/ws` after the exchange.
The pure functions that select and count the sessions in the sessions table by status, kind, project, and text.
A fixed list of 29 dotted setting keys with descriptions that the nav search uses.
The `SettingsForm` state of the settings editor. The editor derives the settings that it sends from this state.
A cache that gives one fetch and one socket subscription to each key, for all components that read the key.
The desktop chrome around the center pane: title bar, sidebar, tab strip, quick dock, and status bar.
The registry record, under `auth:cookie:<hash>`, that proves one session cookie is valid for 30 days.
The URL that the server prints at start. It lets one browser sign in to the console.
One of three templates (A creation, B convention, C test) that a generate-skill execution fills.
A part of the repo that one scout reads to find component types.
A value that counts one running agent execution against `limits.max_parallel_executions` and gives the count back on `Drop`.
The `Label: value` text that starts an agent run, built from a typed spawn struct.
Server-sent events: the stream format that both model APIs use to send a response in small events.
A Markdown file in `assets/refs/` that lists the component types, conventions, and review rule seeds of one stack.
One node kind of the pipeline, such as `spec` or `fact-check-spec`.
The step that writes an upload in `<workspace>/.ostra/uploads/<upload id>/` before a session exists.
The value low, medium, or high that decides whether a full-track session writes a plan.
The router fallback that serves the embedded web build and returns 404 or `index.html` for other paths.
One action that the planner requests, such as a judge call, a spawn, a gate, a command, or the end of the session.
A block that the bridge sends on a Stop event when the agent has not called its submit tool. The limit is `MAX_STOP_NUDGES`.
The MCP transport that sends each JSON-RPC message as an HTTP POST and reads a JSON body or an SSE stream.
One key press as a string, for example `ctrl+shift+k`, with the modifiers in a fixed order.
The ID of the first execution of a conversation. Later runs of the conversation keep it.
The tool `submit_<agent>` that an agent calls once to return its structured result.
Text of the form `@<key>/<path>` that names a file of a project or, with the key `_artifacts`, a workspace artifact.
A control sequence in terminal output that asks the terminal to report a value, such as the cursor position.
A level of model capability (`fast`, `balanced`, `advanced`, `frontier`) that the global config maps to a concrete model for each executor.
A CSS custom property that starts with `--` and holds one design value, such as a color, a size, or a duration.
A user message that asks the model to go on after a response stopped at its output limit with no tool call.
The setting that turns on the guards that check where tool calls read and write.
The state of one execution for the tools: the working directory, the set of read files, the HTTP client, the scrub list, and the sandbox.
The result of one tool call, with the text, the error flag, the exit code, the duration, the diff, and the run end.
The store that pairs a write tool call with its result and returns a `Touch` when the call succeeded.
A record that a write tool call changed a file, which makes the server drop caches and send `project_fs_changed`.
The light or full path of an IMPLEMENT session. The full track adds the spec, the plan, and the approvals.
The type that stops a child process and all its children as one unit, with a process group on Unix and a Job Object on Windows.
The number that a signature help request sends to a language server: 1 for no typed character, 2 for a listed trigger character, 3 for a retrigger.
The function that deletes the registry keys of one workspace root when the workspace is removed.
A host that the user chose, in the allowed hosts or in a harness base URL. The proxy lets it resolve to any address.
The Rust crate that writes a TypeScript type file for each exported type of `ostra-core`.
A research, spec, plan, or phase file that the server parses into chapters and elements with IDs.
A newtype around a String with a fixed prefix and a UUID version 7, such as SessionId.
The part of a book that a `DocsSearch` hit points at, such as a section or a glossary term.
A file that the user attaches to one request as context.
The SQLite pragma where each database stores the number of migrations that it has run.
Voluntary application server identification: a P-256 key pair and a signed token that identify the server to a push service (RFC 8292).
A message that the engine delivers to a harness run that waits for an answer from another subagent.
The standalone Windows program in `tests/windows-probes` that checks a Windows sandbox design on a real host.
The `RwLock<bool>` of a workspace runtime that stops a removal while work starts, and stops a start while an exclusive holder runs.
A folder with a `.ostra` folder that holds `workspace.toml` and `workspace.db` and lists one or more projects.
A file that the user keeps for every session of one workspace, stored as a visible or a hidden file.
The handle of the per-workspace SQLite database that holds the event log and the materialized tables.
The trait through which a workspace reaches the registry and the other state of the process that opens it.
A session mode in which Ostra answers most gates itself. The judges page explains it.
